concurrent-work.label: Concurrent work
concurrent-work.description: Independent papers from the same research period.
concurrent-work.use_when: The papers are contemporaneous and neither builds on the other.
concurrent-work.avoid_when: A later paper explicitly extends, adapts, or evaluates the earlier work.

extends.label: Extended by
extends.description: The later paper strengthens a core part of the earlier method.
extends.use_when: The later paper preserves the main framework and adds a clear capability.
extends.avoid_when: The earlier paper is only cited or used as a baseline.

generalizes.label: Generalized by
generalizes.description: The later paper broadens the earlier method's scope.
generalizes.use_when: The change expands tasks, distributions, artifacts, or system scale.
generalizes.avoid_when: The papers only share a broad idea.

adapts.label: Adapted by
adapts.description: The later paper transfers a recognizable method to a new setting.
adapts.use_when: A method is reused for a different domain or design artifact.
adapts.avoid_when: The new setting is only another routine experiment.

contrasts.label: Alternative path
contrasts.description: The later paper takes a different design route on the same question.
contrasts.use_when: The link reveals a concrete trade-off in design, search, or feedback.
contrasts.avoid_when: The earlier paper is merely a benchmark baseline.

contextualizes.label: Contextualizes
contextualizes.description: A survey, benchmark, or adjacent paper places an AHD method in a broader research context.
contextualizes.use_when: The source has a documented citation or synthesis relationship but no method inheritance claim.
contextualizes.avoid_when: The papers have a direct method extension, adaptation, or concrete alternative path.

historical.label: History
historical.description: Chronology and concurrent emergence of research ideas.
historical.prompt: Is the connection primarily about when the papers appeared?

design-object.label: Design object
design-object.description: The artifact being generated or evolved, such as a heuristic, set, or program.
design-object.prompt: Does the connection change what the system is designing?

search.label: Search
search.description: Candidate generation, selection, diversity, exploration, and credit assignment.
search.prompt: Does the connection mainly change how candidates are searched?

feedback.label: Feedback
feedback.description: Scores, reflection, memory, or behavior used to guide the next proposal.
feedback.prompt: Does the connection mainly change what evidence guides improvement?

scope.label: Scope
scope.description: Transfer across instances, tasks, domains, artifacts, or full systems.
scope.prompt: Does the connection mainly broaden where or at what scale the method works?

relations.description: QSA instantiates AlphaEvolve-style program evolution through OpenEvolve for quantum compiler passes and runtime policies, retaining program-database selection and LLM mutation while adding hardness-guided circuit coresets, execution snapshots, and quantum-specific rewards.
MCTS-AHD allocates revisions with a fixed tree-search rule; Dream-COP learns executable branching and stopping policies by replaying recorded search trees before deployment.

LLaMEA-HPO evaluates generated black-box optimizers empirically with hyperparameter optimization; Lean Runtime filters formal optimizer definitions through proof guards and drift certificates, obtaining query-complexity guarantees rather than benchmark fitness.

ShinkaEvolve screens candidate novelty and adapts evolutionary sampling; Coral Discovery allocates persistent agents across verified mechanism-level directions using direction-local credit and an explicit new-direction option.

EvoMem retrieves lessons from successful mutations; TTME maintains separate operational guidelines and strategy families, adapting strategies to selected parents while replacing test-time weight updates within otherwise unchanged discovery loops.

AHD Agent supplies predefined heuristic-diagnostic actions; AgenticEvolve lets persistent agents write their own analysis scripts between formal evaluations, while an island archive and migration retain explicit population structure.

EoH evolves paired ideas and code using evolutionary prompt operators; PRS separates directional idea perturbation from multiple code rewrites and controls expansion, compression, and steering within a bounded breadth-first frontier.

EvoMem retrieves mutation lessons; ExpEvolve admits explicit idea factors using unexplained score contrasts and archive support, then uses bandit-selected factor edits and background-factor suppression to steer search.

RelayEvolve hands a diversified cheap-model population to a stronger model once; SpecEvo continues cheap-model search while periodically choosing frontier synthesis, repair, or reframing from stagnation and consolidating trajectory evidence.

RAISE generates nearby adversarial instances in an inner search, whereas CVaR-RMD keeps a specified heterogeneous condition distribution and changes candidate ranking to empirical adverse-quantile loss with tail-case mutation feedback.

Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting restarts from the incumbent while discarding sessions and search history; Épi preserves versioned alternative branches and retrieves selected lessons and dead ends to continue research across sessions.

Beyond Algorithm Evolution co-evolves solver code and guiding prompts; Organon makes selection, survival, tools, memory, worker coordination, and even revision procedures dynamically editable while preserving an authoritative evaluator and accumulated history.

SimpleEvol retains compressed search history to guide continued refinement; Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting periodically removes both conversational and external candidate history, keeping only the incumbent before restarting the communicating team.

EoH-S selects complementary heuristics with a frozen generator; EPOCH-Coverage uses instance-coverage gaps throughout parent choice, operator allocation, and recovery, while training its generator with verified reflective preference pairs.

CALM trains the model that directly generates heuristics; HarnessTTT instead trains a separate proposer of executable prompts, tools, middleware, and controls, using frozen-executor rollout rewards and retaining the harness as a transferable artifact.

ArchAgent v2 searches with predefined shortened traces before longer hardware validation; DuoDiscover co-discovers target-specific proxy evaluators and continuously tests their ranking agreement, invalidating proxies when optimized candidates expose drift.

PathWise plans heuristic discovery with a predictive representation; JANUS-World ranks research proposals in a DAG by immediate improvement, information gain, and follow-up utility, then revises explicit prediction and coordination skills from execution outcomes.

EvoAlloc retains ShinkaEvolve's program-evolution pipeline but replaces full evaluation of every eligible proposal with an evolving allocation strategy, prospective disagreement checks, and random full evaluations of rejected candidates.
RAISE uses adversarial instance search within a prescribed uncertainty set; GAL evolves structured test generators and repairs approximate-inference code against the accumulated counterexamples.

CALM updates generator parameters using online reinforcement learning; AGAR keeps the generator frozen and revises persistent text guidelines for separate controller modules, without empirical Bellman backups.

SLA preserves the full external experiment record while rebuilding role-specific contexts; Discovery with Forgetting resets both conversations and historical records, retaining only the incumbent and its score.

Both train a proposer with frozen execution, but Guidance-TTT learns parent-conditioned strategic changes whereas HarnessTTT searches the executor's prompts, skills, tools, and middleware as a complete harness.

MECo evolves a frozen heuristic set using source-task feedback for unseen constraint combinations; PE exchanges executable model interventions, retrains them on peer instances, and promotes them across training scales.

EPOCH admits artifacts according to scoped empirical, finite, or formal evidence and independent replay; Lean Runtime makes Lean-checked asymptotic expected-runtime certificates the specific validation target for generated randomized algorithms.

AgentDiscover lets agents query the history graph and choose experiments; SLA reconstructs restricted role-specific contexts in the harness and has a stateless Advisor assign concrete worker experiments.

RefineEvo uses population-conditioned operator scheduling and retrieved trajectory lessons; DiSH derives independent edit-scope restrictions from feasibility and groups diagnostic failures to preserve previously valid solver behavior.

AdaEva allocates shared-instance evaluations using explicit halving or statistical-racing rules; EvoAlloc evolves natural-language allocation strategies and checks challenger decisions on future disagreements with audits of rejected candidates.

FrugalEvo uses a strong model for batches of strategies and a cheap model for repeated implementation; SpecEvo uses cheap speculative code search with a stronger navigator invoked periodically for synthesis and redirection.

EoH-S optimizes complementary instance coverage; MECo coordinates task-conditioned populations and selects a set from source-combination scores to transfer to unseen constraint combinations without target-side heuristic search.

EvoMem consolidates promising mutation events after a run with exemplars and provenance; SEDIMA writes evidence-linked insights after each evaluation and retrieves synthesized advice through a persistent semantic hierarchy across disjoint problems.

Semantic-index evolution restricts mutable components to preserve tiny-generator proxy transfer, whereas TGR-EvoDAG budgets stage-dependent retraining and deliberately adapts downstream stages after upstream changes.

EvoSkillRec combines open-code exploration with promotion into typed reusable architecture skills; TGR-EvoDAG instead merges complete recommendation-code branches and enforces downstream adaptation after upstream-stage changes.

ADAPT uses ShinkaEvolve as one of its explicit evolution backends, wrapping program search in scientific-history retrieval and separate evolution of initialization-selection policies and numerical optimizers.

AlphaEvolve preserves a diverse candidate population, whereas ComRSI follows one accepted code lineage with a minimum-improvement and paired-bootstrap gate, trading search breadth for controlled cumulative revisions.

AlphaEvolve organizes exploration around archived programs; AI Research Teams additionally allocates opportunities to persistent researchers through discounted improvement credit and preserves their private reasoning histories.

PRECOCIAL explicitly replaces independently trained program evaluations with a single accepted lineage that carries neural pretraining checkpoints forward, making fitness history-dependent while reducing repeated training.

Evo-B&B uses TIDE's separation of island-based structural evolution and numerical tuning for joint SCIP policies, adding matched behavioral probes and restricting local tuning to promising retained candidates.

AutoNovo separates the oracle queried by an evolved sequence optimizer from an optional orthogonal oracle used by outer program selection, making transfer quality a distinct search signal rather than relying on direct optimization reward.

AITE retains a wireless performance-complexity frontier, whereas SiteEvo first selects a site-specific BER anchor and then searches its structural descendants for lower block-level cost under an explicit BER-preservation constraint.

MCTS-AHD expands heuristic-program nodes; LLM-BlockFE uses immutable block extensions and depth-calibrated child-success estimates for rollback, trading unrestricted rewriting for stable incremental feature-program construction.

LeanPlan requires a generated admissibility proof for each heuristic, while Kernaut assembles kernels through trusted PSD-preserving constructions and checks component behavior, contrasting proof search with restricted construction.

ReEvo-FAS directly applies reflective code evolution to crossover, mutation, and local-search operators for antenna-port selection, evaluating them through secrecy-aware beamforming and freezing the code before deployment.

MuEvo keeps component participation reversible and tests collaboration contexts; RLDiscover first freezes isolated component improvements, then switches to joint evolution under progressively longer multi-seed training evaluations.

A-CEoH exposes host-A* code and selects generated heuristics by time-limited solution quality, whereas LeanPlan requires domain certificates and proofs of consistency and goal awareness before comparing planning performance.

AutoSella modifies an established optimizer on fixed molecular benchmark inputs behind force-cost and energy-fidelity gates; ADAPT co-designs historical initialization selection and the subsequent optimizer as separate programs.

Knowledge-first evolves algorithmic principles and tests their code realizations; ADSD starts with numerical failure diagnoses and admits literature-derived executable skills only after claim audits and empirical implementation checks.

OptiSkill revises trajectory-derived formulation knowledge through batch-level bank checks, whereas ADSD builds literature-backed numerical solver skills from verified diagnoses and freezes them before private evaluation.

TRACE retains an EoH-style heuristic population and generation loop, adding agents that execute schema-specific log analysis and expose distilled system insights and callable surrogate tools to later proposals.

ShinkaEvolve maintains a program population; the anomaly-detector study keeps one agent's complete edit history, including regressions, and selects its session-best program without automatic hill-climbing rejection.

Network World Models provides queryable counterfactual rollouts and marginal action credit, while TRACE extracts diagnostic knowledge and tools from observed execution logs, contrasting intervention-based and retrospective feedback.

OpenArchEvo explicitly carries EoH's idea-code pairing into spike-constrained architecture programs and adds initialization-time behavioral fingerprints for novelty screening and surrogate-guided training allocation.

GraphIR extracts tensor dependencies and mutation interfaces to guide code edits; OpenArchEvo measures fixed-input responses and structural statistics to estimate novelty and rank architectures before expensive training.

GrAdaSlim searches source-index-preserving deletion programs with same-oracle activity scoring; AutoNovo searches general sequence designers with optional outer cross-oracle evaluation, separating edit validity from predictive transfer.

AutoMIP separates a persistent pool of unused research directions from its tree of restorable code and artifacts, labeling local refinements and direction switches rather than treating the state solely as a heuristic-program tree.

FormuEvo restricts improvement to formulations consumed by a fixed solver; AutoMIP's task skill permits broader executable research directions, including decomposition and neighborhood search, and restores the artifacts each requires.

AutoMark explicitly situates watermark-program discovery in AlphaEvolve's evaluator-guided research setting, then defines distribution-preservation and false-positive controls that must be screened before rewarding detection and robustness; it does not claim to reuse AlphaEvolve's implementation.

EvoSkillRec promotes validated inventions into an evolving architecture-skill library; MemEvo also admits new typed operators but fixes causal memory roles and freezes components along a prescribed staged search schedule.
FrontierOR lets agents choose a full solver route, whereas DecompGym fixes a decomposition contract and audits operative master–subproblem flow in addition to output quality.

AI4AI-Bench independently rechecks research claims; Auto-Research Arena makes quality and non-target resource constraints explicit admission gates and charges failed GPU experiments while leaving harness search policy open.
Auto-Research Arena explicitly situates population-based program evolution among research harnesses and compares open search procedures under shared language-model quality and resource objectives.

RadonBench uses an OpenEvolve constructor-program search with exact Radon certificates, transferring executable evolutionary discovery to unresolved geometric construction targets without reporting a successful target construction.

BehaveSim measures executed trajectory distance for selection; Principle Collapse diagnoses retained design-route concentration jointly with an attainable-reference gap and a plateau, contrasting observable diversity granularity and purpose.

The token-accounting analysis revisits width/depth trajectory comparisons with cumulative model-token budgets and candidate-validity audits, rather than treating a proposal as a common unit of search cost.

DivAlgo evaluates algorithmic diversity through a learned static paradigm–technique–data-structure similarity, whereas BehaveSim instruments executed trajectories; the trade-off is portable source-level semantics versus task-specific behavioral evidence.

The Bermudan audit explicitly places executable discovery beside AlphaEvolve while showing why noisy policy evaluation and a loose primal–dual gap cannot serve as an exact construction certificate or reliable optimization headroom.

ADSL-PDE constrains solver descriptions through a typed compilation interface; WorldSolver permits solver implementations behind a fixed simulation interface and evaluates executable trajectories through visual and physical evidence.

StrongPrior initializes search with strong executable priors; D2K-Bench supplies progressively detailed expert design explanations without expert source, isolating access to implementation knowledge from access to an executable seed.

When AI Designs AI assesses empirical quality and design differences; AlgoREval instead requests a named published algorithm and tests executable reconstruction, separating reproduction ability from novelty claims.

AlgoREval asks whether a named algorithm can be reconstructed correctly; DivAlgo asks whether a set of solutions spans different algorithmic paradigms, techniques, and structures, distinguishing single-program reproduction from population diversity.

The EAQECC study uses AlphaEvolve to modify exact-oracle-guided search programs, then separates finite-code generation from researcher-led family generalization, checked algebra, and nonexistence certificates.

AscendEvolve retrieves versioned external platform evidence; the RNGD case actively builds, measures, and rechecks target knowledge during toolchain changes, contrasting complementary ways to ground unfamiliar-accelerator search.

Kernel Proofs targets conditional floating-point equivalence and parallel safety; BIEvolve screens dependencies and tests bitwise outputs across batch contexts, adding a separate property with finite rather than universal checks.

TileCas attributes measurements across editable abstraction levels; AutoProfiler evolves a deterministic policy for which measurements to acquire before a fixed downstream rewrite, contrasting feedback interpretation with evidence acquisition.

D2K-Bench measures benefits of expert design explanations; JustGoal tests whether specialized guidance and workflow components add value beyond a same-model, same-scope agent that constructs its own evaluation loop.

SplatLab wraps AlphaEvolve-style editable program blocks in verified 3DGS plugin scaffolds and a domain taxonomy, linking evolved implementations to measured experiments and run-backed manuscript claims.
SplatLab explicitly uses ReEvo-style verbal gradients to turn candidate comparisons and experimental weaknesses into revisions inside its 3DGS island tournament.

LLM-SR searches expressions describing observations; OptScientist infers symbolic objectives and constraints whose induced optimizing choices explain observations, changing the scientific artifact and its identification problem.
Knowledge-first evolves knowledge hypotheses through their generated implementations; AscendEvolve instead retrieves versioned external platform evidence to constrain executable kernel search.

TileCas retains revisitable high- and low-level source alternatives, including rollback; LEKA uses a common graph–tensor–schedule IR with progressive lowering, contrasting abstraction revisitation with layered backend portability.

D2K-Bench combines finite execution tests with design-adherence judgments; Kernel Proofs instead generates conditional semantic-equivalence and parallel-safety proof obligations, exposing different guarantees for generated kernels.

EoH searches executable heuristics and paired explanations; MoSAIC fixes a priority-feature family, recovers weights with Bayesian optimization, and trains an LLM's ready-task decisions from optimal schedules.
DGM archives whole self-modified coding agents; Harmony Harness separates general and environment-specific components and decomposes selection across objectives before recomposing the harness.

ADSL-PDE keeps search within a typed solver description and fixed compiler path; TileCas makes the representation level itself a revisitable search decision to expose lower-level performance controls.

FunSearch organizes archived programs across islands; EliteTable tests a fixed ten-program table with new, edit, and remix operators for control policies, without controls establishing the superiority of that archive design.

The EDA trials explicitly situate their executable research beside AlphaEvolve, then distinguish independent acceptance authority and whole-tool utility from intermediate algorithmic or proof milestones.

Both approaches evaluate programs that construct mathematical objects, but weight-five code search ranks with staged distance estimates and selectively certifies outputs afterward, separating search fitness from exact evidence.

Weight-Five BB emphasizes finite-catalogue distance certificates, equivalence, and connected-component reduction; the later EAQECC study emphasizes researcher-led infinite-family generalization with a separate formal algebraic certificate.

TRIZa predeclares contradiction-guided mutation types and separates useful metric changes from frozen evidence-qualified promotion, rather than allowing candidate score improvement alone to establish acceptance.

The initialization study wraps ShinkaEvolve with budgeted parallel seed generation, then retains its sequential search machinery. It tests whether a stronger starting program helps more than spending the same budget on refinement.

Discovery Init prioritizes high-quality seeds with light duplicate filtering. HoliDivEvolve selects separated island seeds and continues diversity management through migration, exposing different quality-diversity choices at initialization.

RefineEvo uses distinct planning, evolution, and reflection roles with a bidirectional experience pool. LabBook gives one agent a rewritten notebook and read-only access to exact experiments, without a population controller.

EvoDuet refines web queries to acquire external knowledge for program proposals. LabBook instead retrieves exact code and measured outcomes from its own run; the distinction is new evidence acquisition versus selective experimental recall.

LabBook rewrites within-run memory and chooses exact experiment records before proposing a program. MUSE freezes cross-task memory before testing and gates implementation advice at tool-return events during an ongoing coding trajectory.

EvoPINN diagnoses neural-PDE training trajectories to guide representation and training edits. ConflictGuide explicitly distinguishes those diagnostics from qualified probes of competing behaviors used for guidance and guarded retention.

GoalEvolve localizes unmet final objectives to physical-design stages. ConflictGuide instead identifies a coupled behavioral conflict and qualifies probes of its two sides before using their changes to guide model-code evolution.

Component Feedback associates changed functions and constants with existing metric deltas. ConflictGuide designs and qualifies behavior-specific probes; one improves the record of edits, while the other changes what is measured.

Search to Signal retains CALM's search transitions and GRPO backend while implementing alternative reward mappings. Shared-record and reset-search audits separate effective learner credit from archive growth and endpoint performance.

CALM interleaves heuristic evolution with generator updates from current candidate groups. PCPO additionally maintains structurally curated, instance-bucketed elites and alternates fresh on-policy learning with regularized off-policy replay.

PCPO deliberately gives replayed verified elites nonnegative rank-based credit. Search to Signal holds CALM's group normalizer fixed and audits when peer-relative positive credit differs from actual parent or frontier improvement.

ReEvo uses LLM-written reflection on candidate differences. Component Feedback instead extracts changed functions and constants mechanically and pairs each edit set with measured metric deltas, without claiming component-wise causal credit.

E2OC searches combinations of interacting MOCO operators under a fixed controller. HEMO makes retrieval, targeting, parent selection, and candidate evolution inside that controller editable while protecting evaluator interfaces.

SimpleEvol compresses history to guide one heuristic-design trajectory. HEMO retains an external record of evaluated operators across controller states and evolves the policy deciding which records become active context.

ShinkaEvolve rejects code-near-duplicate proposals before expensive evaluation. HoliDivEvolve uses code distance to choose island seeds and complementary migrant references, intervening in search diversity at different stages.

EvoMem retrieves provenance-backed lessons from successful code mutations for later evolutionary proposals. MUSE uses successful and failed tool trajectories and gates implementation-level advice during an agent's execution.
AEL and FunSearch independently established LLM-guided evolutionary search for algorithm or program design in late 2023.
EoH extends algorithm evolution with a joint representation of natural-language ideas and executable heuristic code.
EoH-S changes the output from one heuristic to a complementary set that covers varied instance distributions.
MuEvo keeps the ensemble-level design object introduced by EoH-S but adds reversible component management and explicit co-evolution for interacting heuristic components.
MuEvo retains ReEvo's reflective LLM-guided crossover and mutation loop, then extends it with dynamic component management and ensemble-aware co-evolution for multi-heuristic frameworks.

The AST study replaces EoH's semantic crossover and mutation with structural AST disruption followed by LLM repair; it then evaluates this operator in EoH, ReEvo, and EoH-S rather than extending the heuristic-set objective itself.
AlphaEvolve broadens evaluator-guided program evolution into a coding-agent system for scientific and infrastructure tasks.
ShinkaEvolve retains island-based program evolution while targeting fewer evaluations through novelty rejection, prioritization, and a meta-scratchpad.
PoH turns ReEvo-style reflective suggestions into actions in an MCTS plan, adding lookahead and backpropagated rewards to iterative reflection.
PoH and MCTS-AHD were contemporaneous tree-search approaches: one plans reflective actions, while the other preserves heuristic lineages as nodes.
A2DEPT expands tree-structured search from bounded heuristic components to complete solver programs with hierarchical edits and dependency repair.
LaF-MCTS applies hierarchical tree search to large-scale CVRP solver design, extending the tree-search formulation established by MCTS-AHD.
PartEvo converts the diversity concern highlighted by HSEvo into explicit feature-space niches with niche-level search-budget allocation.
CDEoH groups algorithms by semantic categories, whereas BehaveSim measures diversity from aligned problem-solving trajectories rather than code form.
CEoH supplies problem-specific context; A-CEoH exposes the surrounding A* implementation so generated heuristics can reason about their host algorithm.
Knowledge-first design operationalizes strong priors as retrieved and structured domain knowledge that guides proposals before evaluation.
CALM updates the proposal model online from evolutionary rewards, whereas AAD Fine-tuning learns offline from diversity-aware preference pairs.
LLMOPT learns a shared representation for defining and solving problems; ORLM instead trains customizable models on synthesized OR instructions.
EquivaMap adds explicit variable mappings and verification for deciding whether alternative optimization formulations preserve the same problem.
EquivaMap complements outcome-based formulation evaluation with explicit variable mappings and structural checks of semantic equivalence.
HeuriGym broadens EoH-style heuristic evaluation into a shared agentic benchmark with separate generation, execution, and task-level scoring.
AFL expands automatic routing design from specializing a solver backbone to multi-agent construction and repair of complete constrained VRP solvers.
Evolved-ALNS broadens generated neighborhood operators into joint evolution of the seven interacting modules of an adaptive LNS solver.
CoupleEvo and CoEvo independently study co-evolution for coupled optimization, using different representations and coordination mechanisms.
STABLE broadens paired component co-evolution into semantics-aware bilevel design for reusable multicomponent algorithms.
RAISE targets robust generalization by actively searching adversarial instances, whereas EoH-S evaluates complementarity over a fixed diverse pool.
AutoPort adapts executable heuristic evolution to joint antenna-port selection and beamforming under communication-system constraints.
LLaMEA-HPO separates LLM-generated algorithm structure from numerical hyper-parameter tuning performed inside the evolutionary loop.
Teacher-Aware evolution adds behavioral guidance from learned optimization policies to EoH-like heuristic program search.
RedAHD builds on EoH-family evolutionary heuristic search while replacing the manually supplied algorithm framework with LLM-generated problem reductions.
MTHS generalizes within-task heuristic evolution into a cross-task hierarchy with shared metaheuristics and task-specific executable programs.
BEAM expands the design object into a bilevel solver structure, separating high-level architecture search from function-level realization.
Code Graph replaces whole-candidate inheritance with reusable code subgraphs that preserve corrections and partial algorithmic structure across proposals.
LLM-SR searches discrete scientific programs with language-model priors, whereas LHS optimizes programs through a learned continuous latent manifold.
AILS-AHD instantiates the platform-style separation of search, task, and evaluation modules for ruin-heuristic design inside a CVRP solver.
LLaMEA-BO adapts LLM-driven evolutionary design from heuristic functions to complete Bayesian optimization algorithm programs.
Beyond Algorithm Evolution makes the prompt strategy a co-evolving artifact alongside the optimization algorithm rather than a fixed search instruction.
CodeEvolve combines archives and several LLM variation operators; Mutation Without Variation isolates repeated mutation to expose structural attractors.
REFLEX extends reflective program evolution with visual diagnosis, separated code synthesis, and persistent experience memory.
The EPS benchmark makes evolutionary search itself the design variable, in contrast to EoH's coupled proposal-and-selection workflow.
ReEvo augments evolutionary heuristic generation with short- and long-term reflective feedback distilled from comparisons between candidate programs.
LLM4AD turns the EoH workflow into reusable interfaces for methods, problems, evaluators, and language models rather than one fixed experiment pipeline.
HSEvo takes a diversity-oriented search route, using harmony-search memory and genetic variation where EoH relies on language-model evolutionary operators.
MEoH replaces single-objective fitness with Pareto-based evolution so the generated heuristics can trade solution quality against computational cost.
CEoH injects explicit problem context into the proposal loop, helping the model reason about unfamiliar optimization structures before writing code.
InstSpecHH moves from one broadly optimized heuristic to generation and selection of specialized heuristics for different instance clusters.
HeurAgenix expands EoH-style heuristic generation into a portfolio whose members are selected online from the current solver state.
Hercules adds elite-structure abstraction and efficiency-oriented feedback to iterative LLM heuristic generation.
DASH replaces endpoint-only heuristic scoring with convergence-trajectory and runtime profiling to design specialized solver behavior.
TIDE adds an inner continuous parameter-tuning loop to EoH-style structural evolution instead of asking the LLM to optimize both at once.
DyACE moves heuristic evolution from a pre-deployment phase into the active solution search, redesigning heuristics from observed trajectory features.
HMACE distributes proposal, critique, and memory across heterogeneous agents while retaining population-based heuristic evolution.
Strong Priors tests EoH-family search under richer initial algorithmic scaffolds and shows how prior structure changes the value of LLM evolution.
CALM goes beyond textual reflection by updating the proposal model itself from evolutionary rewards, coupling model learning with algorithm search.
PyVRP+ adapts reflective heuristic evolution to a production hybrid genetic search, separating diagnosis, hypothesis formation, and code revision.
MLES broadens reflection beyond scalar and textual signals by using rendered behavior as multimodal feedback for evolving control programs.
MeEvo makes reflective reasoning heritable across generations and combines it with a separate natural-evolution population process.
CALM learns the proposal model from evolutionary rewards, whereas AHD Agent trains a multi-turn policy for deciding when to inspect, design, and evaluate.
CogMCTS adds cognitive guidance and explicit use of failed search experience to the lineage-preserving tree search introduced for heuristic evolution.
PathWise enriches tree-structured planning with a learned world model and routed critics that estimate the consequences of design actions.
E2OC moves multi-objective evolution from selecting whole heuristics to jointly designing interdependent operators inside a multi-objective solver.
LLM-SR adapts evaluator-guided program search to scientific equation discovery, using executable programs as structured symbolic expressions.
CodeEvolve generalizes evaluator-driven program evolution into an open coding agent with archives, multiple variation operators, and task-defined harnesses.
CodeEvolve provides an open implementation of coding-agent evolution with configurable archives and operators for reproducible algorithm discovery.
CliffSearch co-evolves theoretical explanations with code and uses reviewers to gate both artifacts, extending discovery beyond executable candidates.
Vesper studies the harness around coding agents as a primary design variable, showing how persistent branches and evaluation structure affect discovery.
AutoSG broadens heuristic generation into executable solver construction from task prompts under expensive black-box evaluation.
AHD-Network adapts LLM-based heuristic design to noisy production constraints in 5G decoding, where each candidate requires costly system evaluation.
ARS transfers LLM-guided heuristic design into an end-to-end routing solver with retrieved constraint knowledge and executable evaluation.
LLMOPT broadens platform-style algorithm design from heuristic components to jointly defining and solving general optimization models.
G-LNS adapts executable heuristic evolution to a paired destroy-and-repair neighborhood mechanism for large-neighborhood search.
CDEoH retains EoH's thought-code representation but reorganizes the population around semantic categories to preserve conceptual search coverage.
CoupleEvo broadens EoH from one generated heuristic to cooperating heuristics for coupled optimization components.
MLES explicitly uses an EoH-style evolutionary backbone, then adapts the thought-code loop to executable control policies for visual environments.
PartEvo directly retains EoH's thought-code representation while adding feature-space niches and explicit search-budget allocation.
PartEvo replaces FunSearch's random-island diversity mechanism with feature-based niche construction and niche-level resource allocation.
PartEvo inherits and extends ReEvo's language-gradient feedback for deciding which weaknesses should guide the next proposal.
PathWise extends EoH's population-based search with entailment-graph state, planning actions, and structured interactions between candidate ideas.
PathWise replaces ReEvo's static single-level reflection with policy and world-model critics whose feedback is stored in a structured graph memory.

CoupleEvo and STABLE address multicomponent coordination around the same period, with CoupleEvo studying coupled heuristics and STABLE using semantic bilevel component search; the accepted-version dates overlap the same line.
STABLE generalizes E2OC's interdependent operator coordination to bilevel design of broader multicomponent algorithm structures.
LHS takes a continuous learned latent-manifold route for program search, contrasting with ReEvo's discrete code mutations and verbal reflection.
LHS replaces the tree-structured heuristic lineage used by MCTS-AHD with latent-space optimization of executable programs.
BehaveSim adapts evolutionary program discovery with trajectory-level behavior feedback, adding a diversity signal beyond FunSearch's scores.
AST-Evo modifies the variation operator inside EoH-S by combining AST crossover or mutation with LLM repair; it does not change the set objective.
AHD Agent uses an explicit multi-turn tool policy, contrasting with AAD Fine-tuning's offline generator updates from candidate-quality preferences.
Knowledge-first inverts EoH's thought-code balance: code becomes an experiment for evolving domain knowledge rather than a co-equal search object.
AlphaEvolve and DGM appeared in the same research period but pursue different coding-agent goals: scientific algorithm discovery versus self-modifying agents.
The OR survey provides context for the VVenC study's LLM-generated rate-distortion heuristics in a production video encoder.
The planning study is a neighboring OpenEvolve route that evolves MAP-Elites C++ heuristics for transfer across symbolic-planning domains.
The AHD survey provides context for Successor-Generator's problem-level LLM-synthesized heuristic and planner integration.
TrajEvo is a neighboring LLM-plus-evolution route for trajectory prediction; its cross-generation sampling and statistics feedback are task-specific.
The mechanism-design framework uses FunSearch-style evolution for allocation rules and adds strategy-proofness repair for a new design domain.
AutoPBO explicitly contrasts direct EoH-style generation with multi-agent optimization of an existing PBO solver and its local-search components.
This work adapts FunSearch executable evolution to priority-function discovery for Feynman integral reduction.
The code-generator study transfers the FunSearch/AlphaEvolve program-evolution pattern to web caching and congestion-control policies.
OR-Agent extends ReEvo's verbal gradients and reflection with a structured research tree, multi-agent search, and backtracking.
The tensor-network case study adapts OpenEvolve-style executable evolution to contraction-order design and compares several coding-agent systems.
The AHD survey provides context for GenePlan's executable generalized-PDDL planner synthesis.
The participatory-budgeting framework adapts LLM-guided evolution to allocation rules while evaluating both utility and fairness.
OpenEvolve-style executable evolution is transferred from heuristics to programs that generate pattern collections for classical planning.
Magellan applies the AlphaEvolve coding-agent loop directly to LLVM and XLA compiler optimization heuristics.
The Pareto-grid method extends MEoH's multi-objective heuristic design with Pareto-front grids, runtime awareness, and structural diversity.
EvoPH extends EoH's fixed prompting by co-evolving prompts and heuristics from execution experience.
MEMOIR extends tree-based AHD with branch-local and global memory for transferring useful discoveries across search branches.
The OR survey provides context for Order Matters' proxy-guided evolution of macro-placement ordering policies.
ReVEL extends reflective heuristic evolution with behavior-aware, group-wise, multi-turn performance feedback.
UH-NAS is a neighboring LLM-evolution route for hardware-aware neural architecture co-design, rather than a direct EoH extension.
EvoOptiGraph takes a weakness-driven graph co-evolution route, contrasting with ORLM's learned model-generation framework and fixed training distribution.
FrontierOR generalizes optimization-modeling evaluation to large-scale, structurally complex algorithm-design tasks and test-time evolution.
SCOE builds on ReEvo's reflective evolution while expanding the artifact from one heuristic to a cooperative operator ensemble.
VRPAgent adapts LLM-guided search to discover VRP-specific destroy and repair operators within a fixed routing solver backbone.
The multi-island dispatching-rule method extends ReEvo with personalized islands, semantic reflection, and offline/online evolution stages.
The AHD survey provides context for PACE's primitive-level representation and its attempt to preserve reusable code during executable program evolution.
This survey places EoH among the documented LLM-based algorithm-design methods.
This OR survey contextualizes EoH within a broader review of LLM-assisted optimization and algorithm design.
This overview cites EoH while surveying the intersection of language models and optimization rather than proposing an EoH-derived method.
The CUDA feedback-to-plan study cites EoH as adjacent evolutionary context; its contribution is attribution analysis rather than EoH inheritance.
The optimization overview provides context for PathPlan-LLM's natural-language formulation, solution generation, and iterative route verification.
The programmatic-bottleneck work cites EoH while evolving explanatory programs, a neighboring use of LLM evolution rather than solver design.
DGS extends EoH-style evolutionary heuristic design with learned operator-parent selection before expensive LLM generation.
RefineEvo extends ReEvo's reflective heuristic evolution with planning, operator refinement, and trajectory-grounded bidirectional experience.
SeaEvo extends EoH-style evolutionary heuristic search with a persistent strategy-space archive and diversity-aware navigation.
A2DEPT and ATLAS independently move LLM-based AHD beyond component synthesis toward open-ended solver synthesis and scaffold-free full-algorithm synthesis, developed concurrently.
Clade-AHD retains MCTS-AHD's heuristic tree and LLM-based expansion while replacing node-level UCT estimates with clade-level Bayesian beliefs and Thompson sampling.

SimpleEvol retains execution feedback and accumulated guidance but uses a single agent trajectory instead of ReEvo’s explicitly managed evolutionary and reflective operators; the comparison concerns how much search structure remains hand-designed.

Both reduce expensive program evaluations, but Janus evolves proxy evaluator programs from actual outcomes whereas BiFE screens branching rules with a fixed strong-branching imitation objective before full solver evaluation.

HeurEvo explicitly separates plans, executable implementations, and a reusable component library. ATLAS organizes complete algorithms in an embedding-guided archive; HeurEvo instead makes the high-level plan an independently revisable search state.

HADA discusses empirically validated self-improvement in the DGM line, but separates an editable hyper-agent from a task agent that modifies a MetaBBO project. The distinction is which design machinery can change, not a claim that HADA reuses DGM code.

ReEvo supplies reflective verbal guidance from search outcomes. QuantForge makes explanatory claims into preregistered controls and requires verdicts to cause checked code responses, distinguishing plausible advice from experimentally tested mechanisms.

The game-search study explicitly builds on AlphaEvolve and separates reusable search mechanisms from game-specific knowledge, using distinct credit and evaluation rules to evolve algorithms across games.

LLaMEA-BO designs reusable Bayesian optimization algorithms offline. OnDesign synthesizes and selects algorithms while optimizing the target task, with feedback credited to both algorithm candidates and state-analysis guidelines.

ArchAgent v2 evolves hardware prefetchers within the cache hierarchy, while Presage inserts software prefetches into application code and evaluates executable patches. Their editable layers and implementation constraints are different.

MCTS-AHD uses a search tree over heuristic candidates. AlgoEvo organizes measured experience cards in a derivation tree and retrieves them with situation-conditioned UCB, separating experience reuse from direct heuristic-lineage selection.

RouteRepair replaces undifferentiated improvement advice with a frozen diagnosis of parent-specific failure cases and explicit non-failure protection. A proposed repair must pass measured recovery and collateral-damage checks before normal population admission.

Both constrain regressions during targeted revision. ReForge protects historical traffic-family scores, whereas RouteRepair protects parent-defined non-failure instances using one-sided collateral loss; improvement and protection are measured at different granularities.

QuantumEvo explicitly uses ReEvo to evolve CUDD variable-reordering functions, evaluating candidates through downstream reversible-circuit quantum cost rather than only the size of the decision diagram.

LLM-HCJG broadens thought/code heuristic evolution to a shared blueprint and jointly generated initialization/penalty functions. Full-pair evaluation and component-swapping tests address compatibility between interacting routing components.

Both design interacting routing components, but LLM-HCJG evolves an initialization/penalty pair together, whereas RideSkill trains a skill library, freezes it, then evolves a combiner and finally a repositioner. Joint and staged credit assignment are distinct choices.

ES-AHD uses elite core insights and correlated temperature perturbations to control subsequent heuristic generation, contrasting with EoH’s predefined exploration and modification operators. Its evolution-strategy analogy is not an explicit covariance-matrix adaptation.

MacroAgent explicitly adopts EoH-style thought/code evolution and prompt operators for the contour-generation component of macro legalization, while clustering, assignment, and the surrounding placement pipeline remain fixed.

Both separate generated structure from numerical tuning. LLaMEA-HPO configures generated optimizers, while Bi-EZP nests CMA-ES inside a search over zero-cost-proxy aggregation code and ranks structures by held-out Kendall correlation.

SeisEvo explicitly situates seismic reconstruction in evaluator-guided executable program discovery, including AlphaEvolve. It emphasizes a domain-specific boundary: editable classical mechanisms and physical admissibility checks must prevent meaningless score improvements; no backbone reuse is asserted.

GoalEvolve traces frozen end-to-end physical-design goal shortfalls back to source mechanisms. MacroAgent instead evolves a bounded contour component using legalization-specific regularity/displacement feedback, illustrating different feedback granularity within physical-design algorithm discovery.

Both assemble task-specific criteria from predefined primitives. FeatureHospital diagnoses data and assigns catalog losses and weights; Bi-EZP generates aggregation programs over four proxy signals and separately optimizes their numeric parameters.

EvoMem emphasizes provenance-backed extraction and retrieval of successful mutation knowledge. ε-MemEvo instead learns whether to skip retrieved advice, provide a hint, or inject stronger guidance, addressing when memory should affect search.

ReEvo accumulates reflective guidance within an evolutionary run. EvoMem persists parent–child mutation evidence across runs and tasks and retrieves bounded, provenance-linked advice while leaving the host evaluator and selection rules unchanged.

ELMER trains requested mutation strength against measured behavioral displacement. ES-AHD controls sampling through temperature and elite guidance; sampling variability and calibrated behavioral step size are different mechanisms.

ArchAgent v2 uses AlphaEvolve to search hardware prefetcher implementations, adding staged and joint cache-level evolution, storage-budget auditing, and short-trace search followed by longer-trace validation.

The simulation-trace study grounds revision hypotheses in queryable scheduling events and operational states, rather than relying on aggregate better/worse scores alone. A fixed policy executes within each run, and repeated simulation decides promotion.

Janus explicitly builds on AlphaEvolve-style island search and adds evolving proxy-evaluator programs, region-conditioned credit, and provisional candidate queues. Only real-valid outcomes enter the target population or update the incumbent.

MOSAIC generates instances that expose relative strengths of specialist pairs. PIAC values instances by gains accessible through perturbations of the current portfolio, distinguishing discriminative difficulty from estimated improvement potential.
RelayEvolve uses a common ShinkaEvolve backend and adds a Grow–Deepen scheduler, quality-diverse seed-bank curation, and adaptive cheap-to-strong population handoff under measured inference budgets.

EvoPINN edits executable representation/training modules and verifies generated changes. ADSL-PDE searches typed solver descriptions compiled deterministically into implementations, moving many validity constraints into the representation itself.

DyCA explicitly extends EoH-S complementary population management with inverse-cluster-size weights, dynamic response-based instance clustering, and coordinated specialist pools to reduce majority-instance bias.

MOSAIC organizes specialists and generated instances in a grid of structural features. DyCA instead periodically clusters instance responses to anchor algorithms and balances complementary and specialist pools, changing how specialization regions are defined.

MOSAIC contrasts scalar better/worse reflection with two region-specific specialization insights and a hybridization insight grounded in discriminative instances. These insights persist in archive cells even when their specialist changes.

FunL2O explicitly uses a FunSearch-style program-evolution loop for feature functions. Each candidate must satisfy a semantic contract and retrain a fixed learning-to-optimize pipeline before downstream performance determines fitness.

CostAda prices local/global frontier progress and tactic interventions throughout search. RelayEvolve allocates short cheap-model trajectory blocks and then hands a curated population to a stronger model, controlling cost at a different level.

LLaMEA-MOBO explicitly follows LLaMEA-HPO’s separation of generated code and hyperparameter optimization, adapting it to complete multi-objective Bayesian optimizers evaluated by normalized hypervolume.

QDEvo preserves quality/runtime alternatives through semantic niches and local Pareto survival. AITE organizes multiple executable implementations per explicit idea and maintains a global performance–complexity frontier, giving different meanings to diversity.

QDEvo explicitly develops reflective guidance into immediate comparisons, multi-generation summaries, and error-focused repair memory. Unlike ReEvo’s single-quality search setting, these signals support quality/runtime trade-offs and semantic-niche survival.

QDEvo defines niches through canonicalized code embeddings and Pareto competition. MOSAIC defines niches through instance structure and local specialist performance, contrasting program-space diversity with coverage of problem regimes.

RelayEvolve controls trajectory growth and depth online before population handoff. Evolution or Illusion instead reconstructs an offline seeds-by-iterations frontier from logged runs; the latter diagnoses allocation sensitivity but does not provide an online controller.

When AI Designs AI maps code to human-derived module coordinates to measure structural difference. AI4AI-Bench categorizes training-repository changes by the layer they modify and independently reruns submitted code; both distinguish measured quality from the nature of the design change.

When AI Designs AI assesses empirical performance and module-level design differences. TCSAlgBench asks whether computational guarantees can be justified by natural-language proofs, adding a separate evaluation axis whose verifier acceptance is not formal correctness.

Both expose typed executable components to constrain composition. ADSL-PDE compiles solver descriptions; EvoSkillRec represents recommendation architectures as skill genomes and promotes validated code inventions into a reusable second-tier library.

Janus evolves proxies online and requires real target evaluation before promotion. JET freezes a judge learned on source trajectories and adapts agent programs without target reward access, making evaluator trust and validation fundamentally different.

Both generate tasks in response to current algorithm capability. PIAC uses perturbation-based potential gain to evolve a heuristic portfolio; KernelZero rewards Torch modules near a half-correct coder frontier and alternately trains proposer and coder weights.

FormuEvo stores condition–strategy–effect evidence for solver-efficient formulation evolution. OptiSkill separates general modeling procedures from local corrective experiences and validates skill additions/repairs at batch boundaries before reuse.

EvoMem persists provenance-linked mutation advice, while EES specifies task-indexed lessons about executable procedures, failures, and ensembles. EES’s development ledger does not isolate a measured causal benefit of the proposed memory mechanism.

Both evolve solver-facing model programs. Constraint Model Reformulation selects diverse runtime profiles and checks returned satisfaction answers; FormuEvo diagnoses presolve/relaxation/search-tree behavior and checks optimization objectives on development instances.

GraphIR extracts descriptive architecture state from code to guide later edits, with tracing and static fallbacks. ADSL-PDE makes typed descriptions the source of deterministic compilation; descriptive context and prescriptive representation provide different validity boundaries.

AITE searches implementations of wireless algorithm ideas against a supplied evaluator. WARA extends the workflow boundary from problem formulation through algorithm design to evidence and manuscript artifacts, while its reported comparative scoring is primarily manuscript-level.
LaGO generalizes EoH-style heuristic evolution into a modular program optimization framework that can update multiple executable heuristic roles.
SpecAHD broadens automated heuristic design from whole-instance scoring to within-instance specialization across heterogeneous repair regions.
AutoSND extends evolutionary heuristic discovery by compiling execution quality, runtime, and failure evidence into structural policies for search.
AutoSND extends tree-search-based heuristic discovery with execution-evidence archives and explicit reuse, avoidance, and boundary policies.
DGA2D and A2DEPT both pursue system-level algorithm design, but DGA2D uses directed operator graphs and path-dependent credit while A2DEPT uses program trees.

papers.title: Algorithm Evolution Using Large Language Model
papers.summary: AEL explicitly frames algorithm-level evolution with a large language model as an automatic algorithm design process, using evolutionary search to generate constructive TSP algorithms without model training.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Algorithm design traditionally depends on repeated manual experiments by people who understand both a problem domain and the mechanics of heuristic search. AEL asks whether an LLM can participate at the algorithm level: not merely tune a model or fill in a small code fragment, but propose and evolve complete optimization procedures.

The paper was publicly posted on arXiv on 26 November 2023. Together with FunSearch's December 2023 publication, it marks the early public emergence of LLM-guided evolutionary algorithm and program design. The chronology is represented as a concurrent-work relation rather than as a claim that one paper extends the other.

Paper cover and opening figure. Source: Liu et al., AEL; included for research navigation and linked to the original paper.

Core method

AEL uses an evolutionary loop in which an LLM generates candidate algorithm ideas and executable implementations. Candidate algorithms are evaluated on optimization instances, selected according to their performance, and fed back into later generations. The LLM is therefore used as a proposal mechanism inside a measurable search process rather than treated as an unchecked oracle.

The initial demonstration focuses on constructive heuristics for the Traveling Salesman Problem. The generated algorithms are compared with simple hand-crafted rules, direct LLM-generated heuristics, and domain-specific learned solvers.

Contributions

  • It names and demonstrates algorithm evolution using LLMs as an explicit automatic-design setting.
  • It searches at algorithm level without fine-tuning the language model.
  • It highlights scalability across problem sizes as a desirable property of generated constructive algorithms.

Strengths and limitations

The most important strength is conceptual clarity: a candidate is an executable algorithm with measurable behavior, not only a text answer. The main limitations are a narrow initial problem family, reliance on evaluator design, and limited analysis of how the evolutionary representation controls diversity and credit assignment.

Future work can separate the algorithm object from the search controller, test transfer across task distributions, and record behavioral as well as objective similarity between candidates.

Connections

See the concurrent-work relation with FunSearch and the later EoH extension in the research map.

papers.title: Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models
papers.summary: FunSearch pairs a pretrained language model with a systematic evaluator and evolves programs in function space, demonstrating new mathematical constructions and improved algorithmic heuristics.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Large language models can propose plausible but incorrect ideas. FunSearch addresses that weakness by coupling creative program proposals to an evaluator that decides whether a candidate actually works. The result is an evolutionary procedure that searches for executable programs instead of asking an LLM to state a final answer directly.

Paper cover and opening figure. Source: Romera-Paredes et al., FunSearch; see the original Nature article.

Core method

FunSearch starts with a program skeleton and evolves the part containing the problem-specific logic. A frozen pretrained LLM proposes mutations using best-performing programs as examples. The evaluator executes each candidate and returns an objective score, allowing an evolutionary database to preserve high-performing discoveries and revisit promising branches.

The paper demonstrates the approach on the cap set problem in extremal combinatorics and on online bin packing. The latter is particularly relevant to LLM4AD because the output is an interpretable heuristic program rather than a raw solution vector.

Contributions

  • A reusable LLM-plus-evaluator evolutionary procedure for program search.
  • Demonstrations that search can produce new mathematical constructions beyond the model's nominal answer.
  • An algorithmic application that discovers improved online bin-packing heuristics.

Strengths and limitations

The evaluator gives the loop a verifiable feedback channel and the program representation makes discoveries inspectable. The approach still depends on a good skeleton, an efficient evaluator, and a search budget. It also leaves open how to move from a single task-specific program to a transferable algorithm system.

Connections

The atlas places FunSearch beside AEL as a late-2023 concurrent work. Later systems can be explored through the system, search, and feedback filters.

papers.title: When Large Language Model Meets Optimization
papers.summary: An overview of how language models can define, search, and improve optimization models and algorithms.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

The overview connects language-model reasoning with optimization modeling, search, evaluation, and human oversight.

Core method

This survey organizes language-model use in optimization modeling, solver construction, heuristic search, and evaluation. It is included as background for the atlas and should not be read as a new AHD method.

Contributions

  • A conceptual bridge between language models and optimization workflows.
  • Discussion of modeling, search, evaluation, and human oversight.
  • Terminology for positioning later automatic-design systems.

Strengths and limitations

This is an overview rather than a new AHD system. Its claims should be read as a snapshot of the field at publication time.

What to improve

Useful follow-ups include stronger behavioral deduplication, cross-task evaluation, and explicit accounting of model and verifier cost.

Connections

The relation atlas records only method-level links supported by the paper's method or experiments.

papers.title: Evolution of Heuristics: Towards Efficient Automatic Algorithm Design Using Large Language Model
papers.summary: EoH co-evolves natural-language thoughts and executable heuristic code inside an evolutionary search framework for automatic heuristic design.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Hand-designed heuristics encode years of domain experience but are expensive to create and difficult to transfer. EoH makes the design object explicit: a heuristic has a natural-language idea, or “thought,” and an executable implementation. Both can evolve instead of treating code generation as a one-off step.

Paper cover and opening figure. Source: Liu et al., EoH; see the ICML version.

Core method

The framework alternates between exploration and exploitation operators. The LLM generates a thought, translates it into code, and evaluates the resulting heuristic. Strong candidates provide material for later prompts, while the evolutionary population keeps multiple candidate ideas alive. The algorithm therefore searches in a mixed space of language-level reasoning and executable behavior.

Experiments cover TSP, online bin packing, and flow-shop scheduling. EoH reports strong results under a relatively small number of LLM queries and studies how generated heuristics compare with hand-crafted baselines and other AHD systems.

Contributions

  • A co-evolutionary representation that keeps ideas and code connected.
  • Explicit exploration/exploitation prompt strategies for LLM-based AHD.
  • An empirical demonstration across several combinatorial optimization tasks.

Strengths and limitations

The thought/code split gives researchers a useful explanation surface and makes the evolutionary operators easier to discuss. It can also create duplicated or syntactically different candidates with similar behavior. Performance remains sensitive to the evaluator, prompt operators, population management, and task-specific scaffold.

What to improve

Useful next steps include behavioral deduplication, cross-task representations, budget-aware search, and a clearer separation between structure discovery and parameter tuning.

Connections

EoH is connected to AEL as a later representation extension. The atlas intentionally does not create a direct EoH–FunSearch edge in the first release.

papers.title: Understanding the Importance of Evolutionary Search in Automated Heuristic Design with Large Language Models
papers.summary: This benchmark isolates the contribution of evolutionary search in LLM-based automatic heuristic design across methods, models, and tasks.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Early LLM-based evolutionary program-search papers used different tasks, models, budgets, and baselines, so higher headline scores did not establish whether evolution itself helped. This study creates a common experimental frame and asks which search components survive controlled comparison.

Core method

The benchmark reimplements four LLM-based EPS methods plus a simple baseline, evaluates four AHD problems, spans nine open and closed LLMs, and repeats each setting five times. Performance is aggregated relative to domain baselines, while separate studies examine evolutionary operators, prompt strategies, model choice, query budget, and initialization.

The main result is nuanced: evolutionary search generally matters, but method rankings vary with the LLM and problem, and simple components can explain part of the reported progress. All implementations and model interfaces are released in one repository.

Contributions

  • A cost-conscious, repeated benchmark across methods, tasks, and nine LLMs.
  • Component analyses that distinguish the value of search from the value of the underlying model and prompt.
  • A unified open implementation for subsequent EPS research.

Strengths and limitations

The controlled matrix is much more credible than isolated method results and exposes sensitivity hidden by single-model evaluations. Its four tasks still cover a narrow part of algorithm design, and rapidly changing models can make exact rankings stale. Aggregation may also hide task-specific failure modes.

What to improve

Extend the suite to full algorithms, coupled components, and modeling agents; record prompt tokens, wall time, and failed executions; and maintain versioned leaderboards rather than treating one model snapshot as permanent evidence.

Connections

This is an evaluation paper rather than another search method. It directly stress-tests FunSearch-style and ReEvo-style EPS claims and provides the fairest basis in the atlas for comparing their search mechanisms.

papers.title: A Systematic Survey on Large Language Models for Algorithm Design
papers.summary: A taxonomy and review of how large language models participate in automatic algorithm design.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

The survey is useful as a map of the field: it separates what is being designed, how candidates are searched, how feedback is supplied, and how methods transfer across tasks.

Core method

This survey classifies LLM-based algorithm design by representation, search, feedback, and generalization. It provides terminology and comparisons for the methods in this atlas, but does not introduce a new search algorithm.

Contributions

  • A controlled vocabulary for LLM-based algorithm-design methods.
  • A comparison of representations, search strategies, feedback, and transfer settings.
  • Open questions that connect individual methods into a research agenda.

Strengths and limitations

As a survey, its value depends on coverage and categorization choices rather than a new benchmark result. The taxonomy should be revisited as agentic and multimodal methods develop.

What to improve

Useful follow-ups include stronger behavioral deduplication, cross-task evaluation, and explicit accounting of model and verifier cost.

Connections

The relation atlas records only method-level links supported by the paper's method or experiments.

papers.title: ReEvo: Large Language Models as Hyper-Heuristics with Reflective Evolution
papers.summary: ReEvo introduces language hyper-heuristics and reflective evolution, using short- and long-term LLM reflections as verbal gradients for open-ended heuristic search.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Evolution can preserve high-scoring candidates without explaining how to improve a weak one. ReEvo adds a reflective channel that turns evaluation outcomes into natural-language feedback. It frames the broader research direction as language hyper-heuristics: LLMs generate heuristics in an open-ended space with little manual definition of the search space.

Paper cover and opening figure. Source: Ye et al., ReEvo; see the project repository.

Core method

ReEvo maintains a population of generated heuristics and uses an LLM to reflect on candidate behavior. Short-term reflections focus on recent search outcomes; long-term reflections accumulate lessons that can guide later generations. The resulting verbal gradients complement objective scores and help the search move through a large open-ended heuristic space.

The paper evaluates multiple algorithm types and combinatorial optimization problems, including both white-box and black-box settings. The emphasis is on broad applicability and LLM query efficiency rather than a single handcrafted heuristic template.

Contributions

  • The language hyper-heuristic framing for LLM-generated heuristics.
  • Reflective evolution with short- and long-term memory.
  • Broad experiments across problem types, COPs, and solver visibility settings.

Strengths and limitations

Reflection provides a human-readable search trace and a natural way to turn failure into a next-step suggestion. Its quality depends on the fidelity of the reflection prompt and the evaluator feedback. Reflection can also concentrate the population too quickly if diversity is not measured explicitly.

What to improve

Future systems should combine reflection with behavioral diversity, tree or archive-based exploration, and explicit compute accounting so that verbal improvement does not hide expensive trial-and-error.

Connections

The atlas treats ReEvo as an extension of the feedback channel in the AHD line and links forward to HSEvo's analysis of diversity versus objective quality.

papers.title: LLM4AD: A Platform for Algorithm Design with Large Language Model
papers.summary: LLM4AD packages search methods, design tasks, model interfaces, and a secure evaluation sandbox into one reusable platform.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Research systems for LLM-based algorithm design often mix search logic, prompts, evaluators, and task code. LLM4AD makes those parts explicit and reusable, lowering the cost of reproducing and comparing methods.

Core method

The platform exposes modular blocks for search, algorithm-design tasks, and LLM calls. A common sandbox evaluates executable candidates, while tutorials, examples, and a GUI make new task adapters easier to add.

Contributions

  • A unified implementation interface for LLM-assisted algorithm design.
  • Reusable search and task modules across optimization, machine learning, and scientific discovery.
  • A secure evaluation sandbox and practical support material.

Limitations and extensions

The platform standardizes interfaces but does not solve budget allocation or evaluation noise by itself. Future extensions could add reproducible experiment manifests and native relation metadata for research atlases.

papers.title: An Interpretable Automated Mechanism Design Framework with Large Language Models
papers.summary: Mechanism design has long been a cornerstone of economic theory, with traditional approaches relying on mathematical derivations. Recently, automated approaches, including differentiable economics with neural networks, have emerged for designing payments and allocations.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Mechanism design has long been a cornerstone of economic theory, with traditional approaches relying on mathematical derivations. Recently, automated approaches, including differentiable economics with neural networks, have emerged for designing payments and allocations.

Core method

The framework evolves interpretable mechanism rules in a FunSearch-style program-search loop. Generated rules are evaluated against mechanism-design criteria and repaired when they violate strategy-proofness or other formal constraints.

Contributions

  • A concrete LLM-based design loop for the target artifact.
  • An evaluator or verifier that supplies feedback to subsequent proposals.
  • Experiments that expose the method's transfer or scaling behavior.

Strengths and limitations

The method makes the design artifact executable and lets task feedback guide later proposals. Its conclusions remain tied to the evaluator, search budget, and task scaffold; transfer outside the reported settings is therefore an open question.

What to improve

Useful follow-ups include stronger behavioral deduplication, cross-task evaluation, and explicit accounting of model and verifier cost.

Connections

The relation atlas records only method-level links supported by the paper's method or experiments.

papers.title: Planning of Heuristics: Strategic Planning on Large Language Models with Monte Carlo Tree Search for Automating Heuristic Optimization
papers.summary: PoH models heuristic refinement as planning over executable states and language actions, using Monte Carlo Tree Search to compare multi-step improvement trajectories.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Direct iteration or population updates make local decisions from the current candidate, even when a reflective suggestion may lead to a poor longer-term trajectory. PoH treats heuristic refinement as planning so alternative futures can be searched before the final heuristic is selected.

Core method

PoH defines an executable heuristic as a state, a natural-language improvement suggestion as an action, and solver performance as the reward. A base LLM writes heuristic code; an optimizer LLM reads the code, results, and trajectory context to propose suggestions.

These transitions form an MCTS tree. UCT follows promising branches, expansion generates several suggestion-conditioned children, and greedy simulation continues from the strongest child for additional transitions. Rewards are backed up along the trajectory, and the output is the best node on the highest-reward path rather than simply the deepest node. Experiments use Guided Local Search for TSP and flow-shop scheduling.

Contributions

  • A planning formulation that maps heuristic states, language actions, transitions, and solver rewards to an executable MDP.
  • An MCTS controller that compares multi-step improvement trajectories.
  • Experiments on TSP and flow-shop scheduling, including search-strategy and cross-LLM comparisons.

Strengths and limitations

Explicit action semantics make the search trace inspectable, while lookahead preserves alternatives that greedy updates may discard. The evidence is narrower than the paper's broad claim: experiments cover two tasks under Guided Local Search, reported runtime excludes LLM design cost, and search controllers use different numbers of explored heuristics. Full token and API-cost accounting and significance tests are also limited.

What to improve

Future work should match heuristic evaluations, queries, tokens, and wall-clock time when comparing MCTS, greedy, and beam search. Behavioral deduplication, uncertainty-aware values, and tests beyond GLS could reduce redundant branches and expose cross-task transfer.

Connections

PoH builds on ReEvo's reflective improvement direction and is recorded as a search-level relation to that line. It is concurrent with MCTS-AHD: both use trees, but PoH makes free-text suggestions searchable actions and uses multi-step simulation, whereas MCTS-AHD emphasizes a structured action set and lineage preservation. CogMCTS later couples cognitive feedback to expansion; PoH's distinctive contribution is reflection-as-action.

papers.title: ARS: Automatic Routing Solver with Large Language Models
papers.summary: ARS generates constraint-aware routing heuristics inside a backbone solver and is evaluated on 1,000 VRP variants in RoutBench.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Real routing systems combine capacities, time windows, precedence, pickup-delivery, and many other constraints. A solver generator that succeeds only on a few named VRP variants does not demonstrate general constraint handling. ARS pairs automatic solver construction with a benchmark designed to expose that gap.

Core method

ARS retains a backbone metaheuristic and asks LLM agents to generate the constraint-aware components it needs. From a natural-language problem description, the system identifies relevant attributes, retrieves representative constraint examples from a database, synthesizes compatible code, and uses execution feedback for repair. This narrows the generation problem without requiring a separate hand-written rule for every variant.

RoutBench systematically combines 24 routing attributes into 1,000 variants. Against seven LLM-based methods, ARS reports over 90% success on common VRPs and over 60% on RoutBench, at least 30 percentage points above compared methods in success rate.

Contributions

  • A retrieval-augmented agent pipeline for constraint-aware routing code.
  • RoutBench, a 1,000-variant benchmark derived from 24 practical attributes.
  • Separate evidence on solver success, constraint coverage, and solution quality.

Strengths and limitations

The backbone gives generated code a stable execution contract and the benchmark is substantially broader than standard CVRP tests. That same backbone limits the algorithm structures ARS can discover. Success rates also depend on the correctness and coverage of the constraint database and checker.

What to improve

Analyze compositional failures when individually familiar constraints interact, verify feasibility with independent solvers, and compare retrieval against longer in-context libraries under matched token budgets.

Connections

ARS and AFL both automate constrained routing solvers. ARS specializes a stable metaheuristic through retrieved constraint knowledge; AFL delegates more of the end-to-end design and repair process to collaborating agents.

papers.title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Develop Heuristics for Emerging Optimization Problems
papers.summary: CEoH adds explicit problem context to EoH for optimization domains with little public heuristic knowledge.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters
