The reported suite spans 81 workloads and includes large multi-file applications. Results are hardware-specific; tests and LLM review do not prove semantic equivalence. The pruning of combinations also relies on assumptions about how independently discovered proposals interact.

What to improve

Measure portability and patch durability after software changes, and strengthen automated correctness checks without hiding manual review costs.

Connections

ArchAgent v2 evolves hardware-prefetch logic across cache levels. Presage instead modifies application-side software prefetches. The shared optimization target exposes a concrete design-boundary trade-off, not a claim that their implementations derive from one another.

papers.title: Toward Quantum Software Automation: A Quantum-Aware Harness for LLM-Guided Evolution
papers.summary: Wraps program evolution in quantum-specific low-cost verification, static and execution-state feedback, and rewards tailored to compiler transformations and runtime policies.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Quantum-software candidates are expensive to score through simulation or hardware execution. Generic code-and-score prompts also hide the circuit transformations and resource interactions that explain performance.

Core method

QSA uses OpenEvolve as its program-search engine. Preliminary evolution identifies difficult circuit scales; a verification coreset preserves circuit-type diversity at those scales. Lightweight structural proxies replace repeated expensive fidelity estimation during search, while final programs are checked on the full suite.

Static circuit profiles expose width, depth, gate counts, and DAG features. Instrumented operators provide intermediate snapshots so mutation prompts can localize harmful transformations. Compiler-oriented rewards combine normalized quality/cost metrics. For a runtime policy, quantum jobs or bundles—not candidate programs—receive Pareto ranks; the selected jobs' average rank and the policy's correlation with ground-truth ranks across the job pool form a scalar program reward. Engineers specify the initial component, implementation, and objectives; the harness automates subsequent revisions and evaluation.

Contributions

IBM Quantum experiments examine multiprogramming and error-mitigation software across three benchmark suites, with repeated evolution trials and harness ablations. The method reports improved fidelity/utilization and markedly reduced mitigation time, while accounting separately for API cost and elapsed evolution time.

Strengths and limitations

The coreset and proxies make quantum evaluation tractable, but proxy rankings can fail outside the measured circuit scales or noise regimes. The system is semi-automated and component-scoped, not autonomous creation of arbitrary quantum software. Generalization to other hardware requires suitable measurable objectives and exposed execution feedback.

What to improve

Use uncertainty-triggered full-fidelity checks, audit cross-platform proxy calibration, and compare complete verification costs including coreset construction.

Connections

AlphaEvolve supplies the program-evolution paradigm explicitly described in QSA's background. QSA implements that loop through OpenEvolve, retains program-database selection and LLM mutation, and adds quantum-specific verification, execution snapshots, and rewards. This is domain adaptation through OpenEvolve, not a claim that QSA uses AlphaEvolve's proprietary implementation.

papers.title: QuantForge: Discovering Residual Decompositions for MXFP4 Post-Training Quantization
papers.summary: Turns controlled experiments about quantization errors into checked program revisions, discovering a staged MXFP4 quantizer.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A quantizer's score does not identify why an edit helped. Coordinate transforms, legal low-bit encoding, and downstream residual correction interact, so a mistaken explanation can send the next edit in the wrong direction.

Core method

QuantForge maintains two records: useful executable programs and unresolved explanations of their remaining errors. Before an experiment, it records competing explanations and their predicted responses to controls. It then selects a low-cost set of comparisons that distinguishes those predictions under a frozen evaluation contract.

The result is compiled into a requirement for a successor program. Changed code and an execution probe check whether that requirement was implemented. A successful program can be retained even if its original explanation is rejected. Remeasuring the revised program determines the next unresolved error.

The resulting HiRes quantizer combines coordinate shaping, legal code-assignment refinement, and attention/MLP path correction, always measuring residuals after earlier stages. Search experiments compare four feedback schemes at 240 evaluator calls; QuantForge spends some calls on controls and compliance checks instead of new candidates.

Contributions

  • Distinguishes program selection from validation of the explanation guiding its revision.
  • Provides controlled-search and post-discovery component ablations, plus a frozen quantizer tested across model families.

Strengths and limitations

The matched-budget study reports better held-out transfer despite fewer newly evaluated programs. However, MXFP4 is simulated in PyTorch: native-kernel latency, throughput, and memory savings are not demonstrated. The ability to formulate distinguishing controls is also specific to the available quantization interface.

What to improve

Measure end-to-end hardware costs of HiRes and test whether the same evidence-to-code procedure helps other algorithm families where causal controls are harder to construct.

Connections

ReEvo turns performance comparisons into natural-language reflection. QuantForge takes a different feedback route: pre-registered competing explanations, executed controls, and checked implementation obligations. This connects two specific forms of feedback, without claiming direct method inheritance.

papers.title: LLM-Driven Algorithm Design for Quantum Circuit Synthesis based on Binary Decision Diagrams
papers.summary: Adapts reflective program evolution to CUDD variable-ordering heuristics, scoring the quantum cost of synthesized circuits rather than BDD size.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A smaller binary decision diagram need not yield the cheapest reversible circuit. Optimizing an intermediate representation can therefore miss the downstream objective.

Core method

QuantumEvo explicitly builds on ReEvo's reflective evolutionary search. Each candidate is a compiled C function using the CUDD library to reorder a BDD. The population starts from sifting, genetic-algorithm, and simulated-annealing heuristics, giving the LLM several algorithmic families to recombine.

Candidate orderings pass through a fixed reversible-synthesis procedure. Fitness averages relative quantum circuit cost against the best classical baseline for each search instance; stochastic candidates receive repeated evaluation. A separate validation set selects among evolutionary runs before a final benchmark of 148 functions. The selected HGA-QE heuristic combines genetic search and local refinement, rather than generating a bespoke quantum circuit directly for each input.

Contributions

  • Connects generated ordering code to the final circuit-cost objective.
  • Tests initialization diversity, LLM guidance, and the choice of downstream versus proxy fitness separately.

Strengths and limitations

Search, validation, and final benchmark functions are separated. Non-LLM evolution remains competitive, so the added inference cost is not automatically justified. Only variable ordering is evolved; the fixed synthesis procedure still controls other resource trade-offs, including ancilla use.

What to improve

Study selective LLM invocation and joint circuit-resource objectives, with complete discovery-cost accounting and alternative synthesis backends.

Connections

ReEvo is a documented methodological source. QuantumEvo adapts its reflective search to compiled BDD ordering and changes feedback to downstream circuit cost.

papers.title: RideSkill: A Hierarchical Algorithm for Generalized Ride Sharing with LLM-Driven Automatic Evolution
papers.summary: Evolves executable dispatch skills, a context-dependent skill combiner, and an idle-vehicle repositioner for ride-sharing deployment without runtime LLM calls.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Sharing multiple orders expands dispatch decisions, while policies trained for one fleet or reward definition may not transfer to another.

Core method

First, LLM-assisted evolution builds atomic order-scoring skills with explicit contracts. A combiner is then evolved on top of the frozen skill repository. It probes a supplied reward function using basic events, combines standardized skill scores, and adapts weights to vehicle and environmental context. A third phase evolves a repositioner, processing idle vehicles sequentially while updating effective regional demand to avoid sending everyone to the same hotspot.

Mutation and crossover propose code; compilation, field checks, and simulation determine validity and fitness. Randomized environments and generated objectives diversify training. Repositioner fitness measures improvement over matched reposition-off runs. These are staged design phases, not a claim that all components are co-evolved simultaneously. Final execution uses the resulting programs without LLM calls.

Contributions

Separates reusable dispatch primitives, objective-aware combination, and supply repositioning, with transfer experiments in a Manhattan ride-sharing simulator.

Strengths and limitations

Executable deployment avoids repeated model latency. Simulator and reward-design assumptions limit external validity; optional income rescaling is a heuristic, not a fairness guarantee.

What to improve

Test new cities and arrival processes, and isolate the value of reward probes from the skill library under matched discovery budgets.

Connections

LLM-HCJG keeps interacting routing functions together in each evolutionary individual. RideSkill instead freezes lower-level skills before evolving their combiner and repositioner, exposing a joint-versus-staged component-design trade-off rather than direct inheritance.

papers.title: RouteRepair: Instance-Level Failure Diagnosis and Targeted Repair in LLM-Based Automated Heuristic Design for Routing Optimization
papers.summary: Diagnoses each routing heuristic's instance-level weaknesses and validates bounded repairs against both failure recovery and collateral degradation.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

An average score can conceal a useful routing heuristic's recurring failures on particular instance structures. Replacing it wholesale may erase behavior that already works well.

Core method

For each selected parent, within-scale performance ranks define failure cases and representative strengths. All non-failure instances form a larger protection set. A diagnosis expert combines these outcomes with spatial, demand, route-behavior, and code evidence to identify a bounded edit target. Its reviewed brief is frozen before a separate repair expert changes the permitted scoring function or edge-prior matrix.

Parent and child are reevaluated with matched instances, seeds, solver settings, and budgets. Verified repair requires sufficient recovery on failure cases and limited one-sided degradation over the protection set: improvements elsewhere cannot cancel new damage. Importantly, verification is distinct from admission to the outer population; a useful aggregate trade-off need not qualify as a successful repair. Outcome-aware memory records both successes and failures.

Experiments retain fixed constructive, GLS, and ACO backbones for TSP and CVRP.

Contributions

  • Converts instance-wise outcomes into parent-specific diagnosis and bounded code edits.
  • Explicitly measures preserved behavior instead of relying only on mean fitness.

Strengths and limitations

Matched validation makes local improvement claims testable. Nevertheless, the diagnosis is a hypothesis rather than established causality, and protection only covers the sampled instance distribution and chosen tolerances. The editable interfaces remain domain-specific.

What to improve

Evaluate repairs on a separate distribution-shift set and study whether repeated reuse of protection cases gradually overfits the acceptance test.

Connections

ReEvo uses comparative feedback to guide heuristic revision. RouteRepair offers a more localized alternative: a parent's failure profile, a frozen repair contract, and an external collateral-damage test replace unconstrained reflection as the principal guide.

papers.title: From Search to Signal: Online Post-Training in Automatic Heuristic Design
papers.summary: Intervenes on reward construction inside a fixed CALM loop to distinguish archive utility, normalized training credit, and genuine search improvement.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

An evaluated program can be useful to a search archive without immediately improving the frontier. Likewise, positive group-relative training credit need not mean that a program beats its parent.

Core method

The study fixes CALM's evolutionary operators, context construction, population transitions, grouping, and optimizer, then changes only the record-to-reward mapping. Alternatives separate validity and quality, concentrate weight on the pre-generation upper tail, or probe residual information from counterfactual parent exposure. GRPO normalization can erase additive offsets and almost erase positive rescaling, so different reward formulas do not necessarily imply different updates.

Shared-record and matched-token experiments trace advantages into parameter changes. Live runs, frozen-generator controls, and population-reset checkpoint evaluations then separate model adaptation from accumulated search state. Timing-derived extra-search budgets provide an additional, explicitly approximate resource comparison.

Contributions

  • A normalizer-aware audit of online AHD training signals.
  • Separates validity, valid-only quality, contextual improvement, and frontier discovery rather than reporting only the best endpoint.

Strengths and limitations

The main three-seed cohort uses TSP and one 7B model. Other tasks mainly provide mechanism checks. No reward mapping uniformly dominates; online updates do not consistently beat additional frozen search under the timing-derived budgets. Those budgets are not exact realized-time matches.

What to improve

Repeat with larger groups, additional hosts and models, and timestamped end-to-end resource accounting.

Connections

The intervention preserves CALM's co-evolutionary loop while replacing and auditing its reward construction. PCPO instead curates replayed elites and adds periodic positive off-policy updates, changing the training-data and update organization as well as credit assignment.

papers.title: SimpleEvol: An Agent-Loop Framework for LLM-Driven Automated Heuristic Design with Minimal Human Priors
papers.summary: A single-trajectory heuristic-design agent uses execution feedback and compressed history, studying how framework complexity affects gains from stronger language models.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A more elaborate search framework need not make better use of a stronger LLM. This paper asks how much improved model capability translates into improved heuristics, rather than comparing frameworks with only one backbone.

Core method

SimpleEvol keeps one evolving trajectory and a best-so-far heuristic. The agent receives the task, elite code, recent attempts, and compressed working notes, then proposes executable code with a short explanation. Evaluation returns objective values, runtime, and execution errors. Every few iterations, history is summarized into useful and unsuccessful design patterns; older records are removed. There is no explicit population selection or separate crossover/mutation controller.

The paper also defines AHI from orchestration components, invocation types, and call counts. ICE is a fitted slope relating heuristic performance to an external model-capability score across backbones—not a direct measure of intelligence or a causal effect. Experiments use constructive TSP heuristics, CVRP heuristic matrices inside ACO, and FSSP perturbation rules inside GLS, with ten LLMs and a common generated-heuristic budget.

Contributions

  • A compact feedback-driven alternative to explicitly orchestrated evolutionary operators.
  • A cross-model evaluation protocol, including cost comparisons and ablations of memory, metadata, and elite retention.

Strengths and limitations

The experiments report favorable performance and ICE across the three settings. Removing history summaries or elite context degrades results. However, the relationship between AHI and ICE is observational, depends on the chosen index and model panel, and does not establish that removing structure always helps. Equal candidate counts also do not mean equal token expenditure.

What to improve

A useful follow-up would hold dollar and evaluator budgets fixed while varying one orchestration component at a time, and test whether the fitted scaling trend predicts genuinely unseen backbones.

Connections

ReEvo uses explicit short- and long-term reflection within population search. SimpleEvol instead incorporates execution history into one autonomous trajectory. This is an alternative organization of feedback and search, not an extension claim.

papers.title: TCSAlgBench: Benchmarking Automated Proving for Research-Level Theoretical Computer Science
papers.summary: Evaluates research-level algorithmic proof discovery using versioned theorem challenges with necessary context but withheld target constructions and proofs.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

An algorithmic improvement requires a valid argument about correctness and complexity, not only favorable empirical results.

Core method

A source-processing pipeline extracts theorem dependencies from STOC/COLT papers and constructs self-contained challenges. Definitions and assumptions are restored without supplying the target proof; when algorithm construction is part of the challenge, the construction is withheld while the required guarantees remain. An offline sandbox exposes only permitted cited prior work.

Provers return natural-language proofs. A citation-organizing step checks referenced statements, and separately sampled verifier votes determine acceptance. Workflow comparisons match model-call opportunities while reporting token costs separately. A supplementary pipeline compiles provisional Lean theorem statements and checks their intended meaning; it does not formally prove the generated natural-language solutions.

Contributions

Builds refreshable, source-versioned evaluation for theoretical algorithm discovery and compares discussion, decomposition, and planning workflows.

Strengths and limitations

Carefully withheld constructions make some tasks genuine design-and-proof problems. Main scores remain LLM-verifier acceptance with limited expert auditing, and published source material leaves contamination risk; this is a theoretical-adjacent benchmark, not executable heuristic search.

What to improve

Expand independent proof audits and formal verification, and distinguish algorithm-construction tasks from lower-bound proofs when reporting algorithm-design capability.

Connections

When AI Designs AI evaluates empirical performance and design differences. TCSAlgBench adds a distinct assessment axis—whether a proposed computational improvement can be justified with a checkable argument—without claiming that proof acceptance measures implementation quality.

papers.title: AdaEva: Accelerating LLM-Driven Algorithm Design with Adaptive Partial Evaluation
papers.summary: Allocates instance-wise evaluation depth through successive halving or statistical racing while retaining the host framework's program-generation machinery.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Fully evaluating every weak candidate can consume the budget needed to explore better programs. AdaEva treats comparison precision as a resource to allocate, not a fixed cost paid uniformly.

Core method

At a selection event, parents and offspring form a candidate pool. Cached results are reused while survivors are evaluated on additional shared training instances. AdaEva-S raises evaluation depth geometrically and discards a scheduled fraction by accumulated performance, retaining at least the required population size. AdaEva-R adds small batches, waits for a minimum depth, then uses a Friedman test with Conover post-hoc comparisons to eliminate sufficiently inferior candidates. Racing can collect fresh stochastic evaluations after exhausting the instance pool and stops when enough survivors remain or no elimination occurs for a configured number of rounds. The host's generation operators and per-instance evaluator remain unchanged; the main experiments also leave prompts unaware of partial feedback.

Contributions

  • Separates evaluation allocation from the underlying LLM search controller.
  • Tests EoH, HiFo-Prompt, and LLaMEA across packing, routing, scheduling, and BBOB, with five seeds.
  • Evaluates held-out performance at multiple budget checkpoints and examines racing-test and allocation sensitivity.

Strengths and limitations

Matched evaluation counts exclude the extra LLM calls made possible by cheaper comparisons. Adaptive allocation is not uniformly best: shallow fixed evaluation can win when instances rank candidates identically. Several choices are sensitive on BBOB, and the experiments do not fully separate framework effects from benchmark effects. Early elimination remains vulnerable to noisy or unrepresentative evidence.

What to improve

Optimize combined inference and evaluation cost, test fixed-target stopping, and adapt both the allocation strategy and its statistical safeguards to observed uncertainty.

Connections

EvoAlloc also decides how much evaluation a candidate deserves. AdaEva applies explicit halving or statistical-racing rules over a shared instance pool; EvoAlloc evolves natural-language allocation policies and validates them through future disagreements and audits.

papers.title: ADAPT for Science: A Multi-Agent System for Self-Evolving Scientific Optimization
papers.summary: Co-designs initialization-selection policies and executable optimizers using historical detector designs, simulation traces, and independent held-out validation.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

For costly constrained scientific objectives, a better optimizer cannot compensate for every poor starting point. Initialization and update dynamics should be designed together under the actual evaluation budget.

Core method

ADAPT retrieves 64 structurally similar detector designs from a cleaned historical library and transfers parameters by semantic component matches, using training-set priors for unmatched values. A selection evolver rewrites the policy that probes, prunes, and allocates compute among these starts. An optimizer evolver then rewrites update rules, state handling, schedules, and numerical safeguards.

Candidate policies run in a differentiable physics simulator. Traces guide LLM revisions through a pool of existing evolutionary workflows; quality, anytime progress, feasibility, and improvement guide optimizer selection. The chosen procedures are frozen before evaluation on eight withheld topologies. The discovered optimizer retains Adam but shortens momentum memory, applies remaining-time-dependent update scaling, and transactionally rejects non-finite parameter/state updates.

Contributions

The paper separates “where to search” from “how to search” as two executable design objects. Its complete policy obtains mean held-out loss 0.204 versus 0.452 for the best evaluated fixed optimizer; ablations test selection, optimizer evolution, and scientific guidance.

Strengths and limitations

The historical library and independent validator make transfer testable. Evidence remains within one simulated scientific domain, and performance depends on library coverage. Matched scientific evaluation budgets do not eliminate the extra cost of discovering policies.

What to improve

Report amortization across repeated targets, test genuinely out-of-distribution topologies, and extend validation to non-differentiable simulators and physical measurements.

Connections

ShinkaEvolve is one of the explicitly used program-evolution backends. ADAPT adds scientific retrieval, semantic parameter transfer, and separate initialization-selection and optimizer tasks around that backend rather than proposing a replacement evolutionary controller.

papers.title: Training Numerical Intelligence via Auto-Diagnosis and Skill Discovery
papers.summary: Converts solver traces into tested numerical diagnoses, then retrieves, audits, and implements literature-backed methods as reusable solver-improvement skills.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A residual or runtime score can reveal a failing solver without identifying stiffness, poor conditioning, or another actionable numerical cause. Blind code revision does not guarantee acquisition of the right mathematical method.

Core method

An agent first builds and freezes a baseline solver and records public-case trajectories. Literature screening identifies symptom–condition claims; full-paper evidence is grouped into executable diagnostic probes. Hypotheses developed on diagnosis subsets become deterministic detectors and must pass a separate public verification pool before guiding improvement.

For each verified diagnosis, the agent retrieves relevant numerical methods, records assumptions and page-level evidence, and performs a separate theory audit. Candidate implementations are tested before being frozen into skill packets containing code, instructions, and a claim dossier. The same base agent then receives its original solver plus these packets to construct an improved solver. Private cases remain outside the development loop, and off-the-shelf solver implementations are prohibited.

Contributions

Power flow, AC optimal power flow, stiff ODEs, and heterogeneous diffusion PDEs test the diagnosis-to-implementation pipeline. Ablations compare with direct and recursive self-improvement under the evaluated agent budgets; transfer tests change grid topology and operating regimes.

Strengths and limitations

The method makes numerical evidence and implementation provenance explicit. A detector's high empirical support is not a causal theorem, and theoretical audits still depend on agent reasoning. Results rely on a curated literature database and the baseline-generation restrictions; complete discovery cost matters alongside final solver runtime.

What to improve

Audit diagnostic false positives, test contradictory or inapplicable literature, and isolate the effects of retrieval, theory checking, and executable skill reuse.

Connections

Knowledge-first evolves algorithmic principles before generating code. ADSD instead grounds acquisition in diagnosed numerical failures and audited literature. OptiSkill validates an evolving bank of formulation experiences; ADSD freezes literature-backed executable solver skills before private evaluation, offering a different source and validation lifecycle for reusable knowledge.

papers.title: AGAR: a reinforcement learning substrate for LLM program evolution
papers.summary: Factorizes program-evolution control into replaceable RL-inspired text modules and updates persistent guidance without training the code-generating model.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Search controllers combine parent selection, exploration, attribution, and memory, making it difficult to determine which decision mechanism helps. AGAR gives these mechanisms explicit interfaces while exposing where an RL interpretation exceeds the implemented evidence.

Core method

The decision-process action is the modular text prefix supplied to a frozen code generator, not the generated program itself. Credit assignment, value estimation, and exploration modules construct that prefix; retrieved experience is additional context. Execution and population replacement provide the transition. Persistent module guidelines are revised with separate critics rather than model-weight gradients. An initial unconditional TextGrad-style rewrite failed to accumulate stable rules; the repaired operator permits at most one addition and one edit/removal per period, followed by deferred validation. Only the credit and memory guidelines are actually edited in this repair. A streaming scheduler consumes completed evaluations immediately, with the controller as sole population writer. Value estimates remain textual/statistical heuristics: the implementation does not learn Bellman backups from observed returns.

Contributions

  • Defines interchangeable controller components and reports integration and asynchronous-state pitfalls.
  • Compares variants over 19 tasks, two backends, and nominally three seeds, plus a five-task substrate ladder.
  • Documents a failed guideline-update operator and a bounded, auditable replacement.

Strengths and limitations

Gains concentrate in competitive programming; some tasks lack all three completed seeds. The component ladder is not monotonic and does not isolate each module's causal contribution. Asynchronous rollouts use stale population snapshots without importance correction. The formal discounted objective is not evidence that empirical long-horizon RL training has been achieved.

What to improve

Test learned return estimates, report larger leave-one-module-out studies, and validate guideline changes with explicit delayed-credit and staleness controls.

Connections

CALM changes the program generator through online reinforcement learning. AGAR instead keeps that model frozen and improves modular text controls, separating prompt-level policy adaptation from parameter-level learning.

papers.title: AgentDiscover: Autonomous Discovery with Minimal Search Scaffolding
papers.summary: Lets a coding agent choose its search through graph-database queries, local experiments, and fresh sessions backed by persistent ideas and candidate lineage.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A capable code generator can still be restricted by the candidates and history a fixed search controller chooses to expose. AgentDiscover transfers those selection decisions to the agent while retaining external evaluation and structured memory.

Core method

A sandboxed coding agent can issue read-only queries over a graph of ideas, candidates, sessions, and lessons, write experimental tools, and submit programs. The server validates database writes through dedicated interfaces, evaluates submissions outside the worktree, and returns fitness with steering information such as remaining candidate allowance. Idea membership and lineage make classical selectors expressible as queries—for example, retrieving the best candidate per idea—without forcing the agent to use them. When a session stalls or becomes costly, a fresh agent inherits the database, tools, and skills but not its conversation. An optional meta agent reads prior transcripts and measured outcomes after each session, then writes skills about the search process for later sessions.

Contributions

  • Combines agent-selected retrieval, experiment planning, persistent graph memory, and protected evaluation.
  • Tests 24 problems, including official AtCoder system tests and model-spend-controlled comparisons.
  • Corrects several inherited evaluators that allowed reward hacking and separately studies parallelism and meta guidance.

Strengths and limitations

Each main-table result is a single run, and some comparisons use published candidate-count budgets rather than matched total cost. Reset associations alone do not prove a causal benefit; the meta-agent fork study is more controlled. Four workers improve wall time but not clearly model-spend efficiency. The paper does not analyze which search rules agents actually adopt.

What to improve

Replicate cost-matched runs, log and classify actual selection policies, and separate the effects of queryable memory, resets, and agent-driven planning.

Connections

SLA also separates durable records from short-lived sessions. AgentDiscover lets each agent query arbitrary relevant history and choose experiments; SLA's harness constructs restricted role-specific contexts and an Advisor assigns explicit work. This isolates an autonomy-versus-context-control trade-off.

papers.title: AgenticEvolve: Evolutionary Program Search with Persistent Language Model Agents that Design and Run Experiments
papers.summary: AgenticEvolve runs a persistent experimental agent on each evolutionary island, combining self-designed analyses with formal evaluation, MAP-Elites archives, and elite migration.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

One-shot mutation sees code and scores but cannot inspect behavior through its own experiments. This paper isolates whether giving the variation operator experimental agency improves discovery.

Core method

Each island retains a conversation and editable candidate program. Before committing a candidate, the agent can write and run a separate analysis script, generate task instances, inspect outputs, and revise code. The formal evaluator remains separate and hides its inputs; a commit consumes evaluation budget and returns restricted metrics or diagnostics. All commits enter shared storage, successful programs compete within the island's MAP-Elites grid, and ring migration adds neighboring elites to future archive summaries. Agents choose whether to retrieve and use those programs. Context compaction preserves a research summary and persistent artifacts. A matched No-analysis ablation disables only the experiment tool, retaining agent persistence, archives, migration, and budgets.

Contributions

  • Separates autonomous experimental work from formal scoring and directly ablates the former.
  • Reports better heuristic quality across three models and increased equation-structure recovery on twelve selected LLM-SRBench problems.

Strengths and limitations

The scheduling test changes random seeds but not scenarios; symbolic-regression cases are a selected subset. Cost gains depend on model pricing and prompt caching, so fewer formal evaluations do not imply universally lower total cost. Execution restrictions are protocol-level rather than operating-system isolation, which limits strong claims of inaccessible evaluation data.

What to improve

Use enforced sandboxes, include experiment runtime in cost frontiers, and evaluate distribution shifts beyond fresh seeds and selected symbolic cases.

Connections

AHD Agent provides diagnostic actions for heuristic design. AgenticEvolve instead lets persistent island agents author arbitrary analysis scripts while retaining explicit population archives and migration; the distinction is self-designed experiments within an evolutionary scaffold.

papers.title: Building AI Research Teams for Autonomous Discovery of Linear Attention Architectures
papers.summary: Allocates architecture experiments among persistent discipline-grounded research agents using shared evidence, private histories, review, and discounted UCB selection.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Expensive architecture experiments make both idea diversity and allocation of research opportunities consequential. Independent prompts alone do not preserve the reasoning that connects successive discoveries.

Core method

Sixteen agents share a model and tools but receive different scientific profiles and private persistent histories. A shared idea tree stores proposals, results, and links; periodic synthesis records lessons. Discounted UCB selects the next researcher using improvement over the incumbent team-best utility, while retaining opportunities for less-tested agents.

The selected agent proposes a falsifiable mathematical change. Technical and novelty reviewers screen it before a separate implementation agent codes and repairs the architecture. Candidates must satisfy integration and speed checks, then train from scratch under matched FLOPs. Language modeling, reasoning, and retrieval metrics determine utility. Every outcome, including rejection, feeds private reflection and shared evidence.

Contributions

An 80-iteration search at approximately 150M parameters discovers Context-First DeltaNet: a recurrent vector first explains shared information, then matrix memory fits residual prediction error. Validation at 1.3B improves the reported category-level metrics over the compared attention architectures. Organizational ablations test profiles, memory, and allocation.

Strengths and limitations

Larger-scale validation supports transfer beyond search scale. Results concern one architecture family and expensive training regime. Search uses reduced versions of several final benchmark families, so their full evaluations are not wholly task-disjoint holdouts; real-world retrieval is excluded from search.

What to improve

Repeat team-level searches, measure end-to-end research cost, and test whether disciplinary diversity helps under different evaluators and architecture families.

Connections

AlphaEvolve allocates search around candidate programs, whereas this team also allocates opportunities to persistent researchers using discounted improvement credit. Private histories preserve the reasoning behind unsuccessful experiments rather than representing search state solely through executable candidates and their scores.

papers.title: Are you Synthesizing or Recalling? Evaluating LLMs on Algorithmic Code Retrieval
papers.summary: Measures reproduction of named algorithms across languages and input representations, separating this operational task from claims of novel algorithm synthesis.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Successfully implementing a familiar named algorithm is useful, but does not by itself show algorithmic invention or robust correctness.

Core method

AlgoREval poses 599 entries covering 77 classical algorithms, seven languages, and several graph representations. Prompts specify the algorithm, interface, concrete input, and required output. Generated code is compiled when needed and run under a timeout; normalized output matching determines success, with static, runtime, timeout, and wrong-output failures reported separately.

Fifteen models are evaluated zero-shot. Further experiments add retrieved implementations or structured hints, then compare supervised fine-tuning and execution-reward GRPO on algorithm-level held-out splits. Timing and implementation comparisons probe whether different outputs resemble known legitimate algorithm variants.

Contributions

The benchmark isolates interface-sensitive reproduction of established algorithms and shows that language and input encoding materially change measured reliability.

Strengths and limitations

Executable checks expose runnable but incorrect code, and algorithm-level splits reduce training/evaluation overlap in adaptation experiments. However, one fixed test input does not establish general correctness. The authors cannot verify per-algorithm pretraining exposure, so behavior cannot conclusively distinguish internal retrieval from synthesis; fine-tuning gains also vary across splits.

What to improve

Add property-based and adversarial tests, broaden representation coverage, and use controlled training corpora to test retrieval explanations directly.

Connections

When AI Designs AI measures distance from human design choices. AlgoREval supplies a complementary boundary case: accurate reconstruction of a named algorithm is deliberately the target, not evidence of novelty. DivAlgo instead asks whether correct outputs span multiple strategies.

papers.title: When Algorithmic Exploration Becomes Cheap: A Case Study of Agentic Research in EDA
papers.summary: Reports eight agentic EDA research trials with fixed substantive acceptance gates, independent evaluation, and explicit failures of practical tool transfer.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A valid construction or locally faster component can still fail to improve an established design tool. Research acceptance must distinguish those endpoints.

Core method

Agentic Research Trials (ART) specify demanding endpoints without prescribing the algorithmic route. Agents pursue extended attempts, while separately prepared feasibility checks, measurements, and adversarial proof review decide acceptance. Human organizers can redirect the question or reject an inadequate comparison; search instructions are not mathematical assumptions.

Eight trials span spanning trees, logic optimization, placement, contraction, clock trees, remapping, rewriting, and FPGA optimization. The artifact may be a theorem, a counterexample, an algorithm, or integrated tool code, each judged against its original substantive gate.

Contributions

Cases include a researcher-reconstructed approximation argument and useful tool changes, alongside placement campaigns missing their whole-tool improvement target and exact surrogate improvements that worsen physical results. A separate publication-corpus study characterizes computational research loops; it does not measure private AI usage.

Strengths and limitations

Failed branches and continuing integration work prevent early milestones from being mistaken for completed research. However, the trials are heterogeneous case studies without matched-budget controls, human-time estimates are retrospective, and proof review is not equivalent to machine-checked formalization.

What to improve

Publish complete intervention and cost ledgers, compare fixed acceptance protocols across teams, and follow improvements through independent whole-tool reproduction.

Connections

The paper explicitly situates ART beside AlphaEvolve's executable discovery loop, but shifts attention to human-set acceptance authority and the gap between validated local artifacts and useful end-to-end EDA systems.

papers.title: Beyond Experience: Knowledge-Guided Evolution for NPU Kernel Generation
papers.summary: Grounds diverse Ascend kernel search and mechanism-level recombination in retrieved platform documentation, toolkit headers, and measured local evidence.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

An agent cannot reliably discover unfamiliar accelerator mechanisms by remembering only code it has already tried.

Core method

A versioned shared knowledge base indexes platform documents, toolkit headers, and operator repositories. Task-local records retain hypotheses, parentage, failures, measurements, and lessons. Demand-driven retrieval supplies small evidence slices for proposal, repair, and optimization; local measurements can override a documented expectation without rewriting shared facts.

The first stage explores distinct implementation-strategy trees, retaining failures and backtracking when necessary. The second combines a strong base with donor mechanisms selected for its diagnosed weakness, checks compatibility, and reevaluates the resulting kernel.

Contributions

On 53 CANN-Bench operators, AscendEvolve reports a composite score of 71.39, 11.6% and 17.2% above Reflexion and OpenEvolve. Knowledge-base ablations show particularly large effects on intermediate-complexity tasks.

Strengths and limitations

The knowledge is operationally grounded rather than an unverified narrative summary. However, the score is not a speedup ratio, overall correctness does not exceed every baseline, and hardest-level correctness remains 35%. Validity is established by tests, not semantic proof; knowledge and measurements depend on hardware and toolchain versions.

What to improve

Evaluate new toolchains and operators, publish retrieval and device-cost accounting, and test stale or conflicting source evidence systematically.

Connections

Knowledge-first evolves knowledge hypotheses and tests them through generated code. AscendEvolve instead treats external platform evidence as a versioned resource constraining code search, exposing different roles for knowledge in heuristic design.

papers.title: Auto-Research Arena: Benchmarking and Advancing Auto-Research in Language Modeling
papers.summary: Benchmarks executable language-model research across nine resource objectives while separately enforcing model-quality and non-target-resource constraints.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A research harness that improves validation loss may not discover improvements in memory, data use, or inference latency. Changing the objective can expose different design ideas.

Core method

A fixed language-modeling environment evaluates editable model, optimizer, training, and inference programs. Each of nine tracks minimizes one resource metric subject to validation BPB below 1.05, correctness, and track-specific resource limits. Every GPU-started experiment counts, including failures; the best recorded admissible candidate is reported even if the harness discards it.

Six LLM harnesses use two foundation models, with a restricted TPE baseline in one model group. Searches receive 100 charged experiments, with up to 600 seconds of candidate training on an A100. Sequential Search retains one incumbent; Beam Search retains several directions. Logged histories support cross-objective reuse and longer-training checks.

Contributions

The benchmark separates admissibility from improvement and measures how objectives shape both harness rankings and reusable program changes. A simple sequential baseline ranks second with both backbones.

Strengths and limitations

Independent measurement and charged failures improve comparability. Selected discoveries transfer beyond ten-minute training, but some advantages disappear by sixty minutes as horizon-specific schedules decay. Small language models, fixed seeds, noisy system timings, and interpretive idea categories limit broader scientific-novelty claims.

What to improve

Repeat searches and retraining across seeds, report token and GPU costs together, and test larger models without retuning the discovered programs.

Connections

AI4AI-Bench separates development from final algorithm verification. Arena instead separates quality admissibility from the resource being optimized. Its appendix explicitly places evaluator-guided research in the program-search context of AlphaEvolve.

papers.title: Have an LLM Write Your Anomaly Detector: Autonomous Discovery of Compact, Interpretable Detectors for Time Series
papers.summary: Searches compact NumPy anomaly detectors against synthetic training-region anomalies, retaining full research history while selecting the best final program.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Accurate anomaly detection need not require a large learned model. An executable detector can be inexpensive and inspectable, provided its discovery objective reflects useful anomaly mechanisms without leaking test labels.

Core method

The agent edits a single short function mapping training and test segments to timestamp scores. A fixed harness injects synthetic anomalies into a held-out slice of the training region and supplies validation performance. The generator covers magnitude changes, frozen segments, and in-range contextual or rhythmic changes; real anomaly labels are excluded from search.

There is no automatic hill-climbing acceptance gate: unsuccessful edits remain in the trajectory and can inspire later proposals. The best-scoring program over the session is returned. Single-principle prompting favors compact mechanisms. The strongest univariate and multivariate discoveries compare local spectral descriptions with normal training windows using covariance-aware distances, then map multi-scale window novelty to timestamp scores.

Contributions

TSB-AD and TAB evaluate separate univariate and multivariate detectors. The paper compares driving models and a matched ShinkaEvolve search, provides executable code, and measures CPU inference efficiency rather than only predictive metrics.

Strengths and limitations

Programs are readable and require no neural training at deployment. Rankings depend on metric and dataset: the method does not dominate every TAB univariate measure. The synthetic generator supplies substantial human prior knowledge, and inference-time efficiency excludes discovery cost. Search-controller comparisons show no consistent accuracy winner.

What to improve

Repeat independent searches, vary synthetic anomaly families, and evaluate unseen industrial processes and region-level detection objectives.

Connections

ShinkaEvolve maintains an evolutionary population; this agent retains a single editable trajectory, including regressions, and returns its session-best program. The paper observes different artifact complexity under matched prompts without establishing universal accuracy superiority for either search organization.

papers.title: AutoNovo: Agentic Program Search Discovers Transferable Nucleic Acid Design Algorithms
papers.summary: Uses agentic tree search to rewrite sequence-design algorithms, with distinct optimization and evaluation oracles encouraging transfer beyond one predictive model.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A DNA sequence can exploit artifacts of its design oracle. The question is whether searching the designer program itself can produce algorithms whose outputs transfer to independent predictors.

Core method

The ERA harness expands a UCB-guided program tree. Each generated Designer stores a queryable oracle and a starting ACGT sequence, searches within a wall-clock budget, and returns its best sequence. Seeds reimplement established gradient and discrete designers. Crashes, forbidden exception handlers, and budget overruns incur penalties.

The outer search evaluates each program on three starting sequences. In most configurations it combines the designer's accessible oracle score with an orthogonal score hidden from the inner designer. Selected code is frozen before testing on twenty starts and alternate oracle roles. Discovered programs combine straight-through gradient updates, discrete incumbent preservation, and budget-aware restarts or sparse mutations.

Contributions

A family of sixteen programs supplies the best observed means across three direct and six cross-oracle tasks; no single program wins everywhere. The study distinguishes transferring an algorithm to a new oracle from transferring its designed sequences to another predictor.

Strengths and limitations

Some experiments withhold an oracle from both loops, but an oracle hidden only from the designer is still visible to outer selection. All evidence is in silico for one phenotype; it does not establish biological effectiveness. Code audits reveal oracle-identity shortcuts, stale gradients, missing random seeds, and an out-of-memory failure.

What to improve

Evaluate independent biological assays, remove identity shortcuts, standardize reproducibility, and ablate the individual mechanisms responsible for transfer.

Connections

AlphaEvolve makes execution scores the arbiter of program evolution. AutoNovo's concrete alternative is a nested evaluator: an evolved optimizer sees one oracle while outer program selection can use another, separating optimization success from transfer quality.

papers.title: Less is more: learning what to profile for GPU kernel optimization
papers.summary: Evolves a deterministic profiling decision tree offline so one downstream kernel rewrite receives selectively gathered hardware evidence.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

More profiler counters can consume budget and distract a kernel optimizer. Which evidence to collect is itself a design decision.

Core method

AutoProfiler starts with a roofline-style tree separating compute- and memory-related regimes. An LLM proposes REWRITE operations that change a leaf's metric bundle and SPLIT operations that partition kernels using measured thresholds.

Paired kernel optimization trials evaluate each tree edit; a conservative reward retains useful changes. Learning occurs offline on CUDA-Agent-Ops data. At deployment the deterministic tree gathers kernel-conditioned evidence and invokes the kernel rewriter once, without another model deciding which counters to query.

Contributions

On unseen KernelBench tasks and RTX 4090D hardware, the reported configuration reaches 87.2% accuracy and 1.704× average speedup, compared with 1.570× for the strongest reported fixed profiling competitor. Experiments demonstrate that adding counters does not monotonically improve optimization.

Strengths and limitations

The learned object is an evidence-acquisition policy, not merely a better kernel prompt. However, offline training cost must be separated from cheap deployment. Comparators make different numbers of model calls, and a single hardware family limits portability. Oracle profiling analyses describe headroom, not a deployable policy.

What to improve

Report amortized training cost and equal-token comparisons, test compiler and device transfer, and quantify whether tree decisions remain useful after kernel revisions.

Connections

TileCas attributes measurements across editable programming levels. AutoProfiler addresses the preceding feedback decision—what measurements to acquire—while keeping the downstream rewrite interface fixed.

papers.title: Optimizing the Optimizer: Language Models Discover Faster Molecular Relaxation Algorithms
papers.summary: Rewrites the Sella molecular optimizer to reduce force evaluations, admitting changes only when training and validation costs improve without losing energy recovery.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Force evaluations dominate expensive molecular relaxation. A seemingly faster optimizer can merely stop at a worse geometry, so improvement must preserve scientific fidelity rather than minimize iteration counts alone.

Core method

An agent edits a consolidated Sella implementation while a protected evaluator measures per-molecule relative force calls, energy recovery, convergence, and failures. Each iteration proposes one coherent change from the current champion and reads both numerical records and narrative history. Crashes and rejected mechanisms remain in the record, not the accepted program.

Candidates must reduce training force cost without errors or reduced mean energy recovery. The same gates then apply on a validation split before promotion. Two independent 66-hour searches produce AutoSella-F and AutoSella-A. Important changes include curvature models and coordinates, disconnected-fragment handling, and reuse of previous gradient information. Selected optimizers are tested on new molecules and potentials not used for discovery.

Contributions

AutoSella-F reduces force calls across the reported held-out molecular sets and transfers from GFN2-xTB search to GFN-FF and DFT evaluation. Ablations remove groups of optimizer changes to identify their contribution rather than attributing all gains to more proposals.

Strengths and limitations

Energy gates explicitly discourage premature stopping. Mean recovery is not a per-molecule fidelity guarantee; geometry checks are supplementary. The validation split is repeatedly queried during selection. AutoSella-A regresses on solvated PubChem, so gains are not uniform across variants or chemical domains.

What to improve

Use fresh confirmation splits, report molecule-level failure and fidelity distributions, and compare force-call savings with total wall time and discovery amortization.

Connections

ADAPT for Science co-designs historical starting-point selection and update dynamics. AutoSella holds the molecular benchmark inputs fixed and modifies an established optimizer behind force-cost and energy gates, distinguishing solver-mechanism improvement from better initialization retrieval.

papers.title: Auditing LLM Program Search for Bermudan Stopping with Primal--Dual Certificates
papers.summary: Audits generated Bermudan exercise policies with frozen selection, paired payoff comparisons, and evaluator-owned primal–dual estimates, finding no reliable improvement.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Searching a noisy score can reward lower measurement variance or selection luck rather than a better policy. A valid bound can also be too loose to detect genuine progress.

Core method

Candidates expose Python fit/predict policies, while a trusted evaluator controls paths, causal exercise, payoffs, and a shared dual upper bound. A planner–proposer pipeline and direct generation produce 24 attempts with matched no-generation controls. Public search feedback is a paired payoff-improvement lower confidence bound.

Selection freezes before evaluation on fresh contracts and seeds. A separate six-pair ablation varies structured versus scalar memory under fixed parents and operators. Reported payoff, raw primal–dual gap, and uncertainty-augmented selection score are kept distinct; the latter can improve merely because its error margin shrinks.

Contributions

The audit retains failures and the original reference, separates improvement testing from near-optimality certification, and calibrates dual looseness against binomial references.

Strengths and limitations

No selected generated program consistently improves on Ridge LSMC beyond Monte Carlo uncertainty. Structured memory shows no benefit in the small ablation. About 99% of Ridge's estimated gap on six one-dimensional puts comes from the dual, and those contracts offer little improvement headroom. Three seed blocks, small budgets, and asymptotic confidence bounds preclude broad negative conclusions about program search.

What to improve

Use positive controls with weaker parents, contracts with larger headroom, candidate-specific tighter duals, and larger paired evaluations.

Connections

The paper explicitly places AlphaEvolve and FunSearch in context: an exact construction verifier differs fundamentally from a noisy policy evaluator whose apparent gains require independent statistical checks.

papers.title: God Does Not Play Dice: Enforcing Batch Invariance in Agentic Kernel Generation
papers.summary: Adds contract-based static analysis and cross-batch bitwise tests to kernel agents before speed measurements can reward a candidate.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Ordinary correctness tests may accept a kernel whose output for one request changes when other requests join its batch. Serving reproducibility therefore requires a separate property.

Core method

BIEvolve is a plug-in evaluator rather than a new search algorithm. A task contract identifies batch-varying inputs and protects sample-local reductions, indexing, and randomness. Static dependency analysis screens suspicious dataflow; native correctness tests and dynamic checks then compare an unchanged sample across batch contexts at bitwise precision.

Only passing candidates reach timing. Rejection diagnostics return to the host agent's existing repair loop. Integrations retain the original KSearch, Iterative, and Evolve search mechanisms.

Contributions

The artifact audit confirms violations in 19 of 83 batch-applicable released kernels. Across three frameworks on H100 serving workloads, BI-aware generation raises the reported batch-invariance pass rate from 67.6% to 91.9%, retaining 91.8% of baseline geometric-mean speedup.

Strengths and limitations

The study distinguishes numerical tolerance from bitwise invariance and measures both missed violations and false rejections. Static support is limited to particular source patterns, and finite dynamic contexts do not prove invariance. The contract must correctly identify independent sample semantics; some operations intentionally couple examples.

What to improve

Expand language and cross-file coverage, independently validate contracts, and test unseen batch sizes and production batching policies.

Connections

Kernel Proofs pursues conditional semantic equivalence and parallel safety through proofs. BIEvolve adds a distinct cross-context property using static screening and finite execution tests; neither guarantee subsumes the other.

papers.title: Recursive Code Evolution for Task-Oriented Semantic Communications
papers.summary: Recursively edits executable communication systems while a protected evaluator tests accuracy, channel use, computation, and statistically gated improvements.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Semantic communication usually optimizes weights inside a fixed architecture. Moving computation across the transmitter–receiver boundary or changing the transmitted representation requires changing the program itself.

Core method

The LLM receives the accepted encoder, channel adapters, decoder, loss, training policy, diagnostics, and proposal history. It writes four candidate revisions per generation. Valid candidates receive proxy training; the top two are trained from scratch with three seeds. A score combines accuracy over public SNRs with logarithmic rate and FLOP penalties.

Acceptance requires both a minimum score improvement and a positive paired-bootstrap lower bound. Only accepted code and configuration become the next parent; trained weights are never inherited. Protected channels, manifests, budgets, integrity checks, and withheld post-search tests constrain evaluator manipulation. Rejected proposals still contribute textual history.

Contributions

The original CIFAR-100 lineage discovers an attention-pooled 32-symbol design, compared with 256 symbols initially. Ten-search repetitions distinguish executable inheritance from textual history and memoryless proposals; transfer includes fresh training on Tiny-ImageNet and withheld fading channels.

Strengths and limitations

The repeat study supports an advantage over memoryless proposals, but not a statistically conclusive advantage over the history-equipped non-recursive agent. Equal training steps do not imply equal FLOPs or wall time. Simulated image-classification channels omit practical modulation, estimation, latency, and energy costs.

What to improve

Increase independent search repetitions, evaluate digital communication and adaptive rates, and account separately for transmitter and receiver deployment costs.

Connections

AlphaEvolve maintains a diverse candidate population; ComRSI instead follows one statistically accepted code lineage with explicit public/hidden evaluation boundaries. This trades breadth of exploration for controlled cumulative changes and stronger acceptance checks.

papers.title: Coral Discovery: The Division of Cognitive Labor in Autonomous Research
papers.summary: Coral Discovery allocates autonomous agents across verified algorithmic directions using direction-local credit, estimated improvement yield, and an exploration option.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A shared leaderboard can make collaborating agents converge on the same promising mechanism. Useful but initially weaker directions then receive too little effort to mature.

Core method

Agents independently edit and evaluate programs in shared versioned storage. Each attempt declares a method-level change, while an independent verifier reads its diff to assign a mechanism-level direction. A direction board estimates improvement per evaluation, shrinks sparse estimates toward a shared prior, and adds an exploration bonus. Credit requires improvement over the parent, cited inspiration, and that direction's own best, so copying another line does not manufacture progress. A separate NEW option estimates the value of opening a direction. Suggested agent counts are advisory, with claim caps and duplicate checks. Agents finish an ongoing line before consulting the board, submit one evaluation per round, and record an insight afterward.

Contributions

  • Makes direction-level diversity and local progress explicit rather than equating diversity with different program ancestors.
  • Evaluates nine kernel, packing, mathematical, inference, and systems tasks with controlled model, agent budget, and evaluator-access rules.

Strengths and limitations

Best-of-three reporting gives six wins, one tie, and two losses against the reproduced strongest baseline configuration. Exploration consumes evaluations: directions that never produce a global record hurt LLM-SQL and transaction scheduling. Direction labels depend on a model verifier, and cited published results use different web/grader access conditions.

What to improve

Report uncertainty across more runs, test verifier consistency, and learn when direction-level exploration should yield to sustained work within one mechanism.

Connections

ShinkaEvolve promotes novelty through candidate filtering and adaptive evolutionary sampling. Coral Discovery intervenes at a coarser unit: it credits and budgets research directions while persistent agents choose their own edits.

papers.title: CVaR-RMD: CVaR Selection Pressure for Robust Metaheuristic Discovery
papers.summary: CVaR-RMD changes evolutionary program selection from mean loss to empirical tail-risk, using shared heterogeneous evaluation conditions and tail-case diagnostics to discover more robust heuristics.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A heuristic with a good average can fail badly on particular instance families, seeds, or scales. Those adverse cases are easily hidden when the evolutionary loop ranks candidates only by a mean.

Core method

Each generated program implements a fixed interface and is evaluated on conditions specifying an instance family, scale, instance seed, and execution seed. Candidates within a generation share the evaluation batch. Invalid code, timeouts, and infeasible solutions receive fixed loss penalties. The fitness is empirical CVaR: the average of the worst chosen fraction of outcomes, with fractional boundary weighting when needed. Tail records identify difficult conditions and optionally guide LLM mutation. Rank-biased parent sampling and elitist parent–offspring replacement use this risk score; accumulated losses can require minimum evidence before archive entry. The selected program is frozen for deployment without further LLM calls.

Contributions

  • Isolates risk-sensitive selection through a Mean-RMD comparison that retains the same generator, archive, validator, and search budget.
  • Reports fifteen discovery seeds in packing, routing, and flow-shop scheduling, including larger-instance and curated within-domain transfer tests.

Strengths and limitations

The experiments support lower tail loss and failures while retaining competitive means, not guaranteed robustness to arbitrary shifts. Tail-level choice controls a practical mean–risk trade-off, and finite samples can miss rare failures. Only three problem domains are studied. Acceptance is disclosed in official metadata; the displayed month follows first arXiv submission because the acceptance month is not supplied.

What to improve

Quantify uncertainty in estimated tails, adapt evaluation effort to rare events, and assess risk choices under genuinely different generators.

Connections

RAISE searches for nearby adversarial instances in an inner loop. CVaR-RMD instead keeps a specified heterogeneous evaluation distribution and ranks its adverse quantile across instances, scales, and seeds: robustness comes from risk-sensitive selection rather than adaptive instance generation.

papers.title: D2K-Bench: Can LLM Agents Turn Expert Designs into Efficient GPU Kernels?
papers.summary: Tests how expert algorithm, dataflow, and low-level guidance changes generated-kernel correctness, speed, and implemented design properties.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Slow generated kernels may lack the right algorithm, fail to realize a good design, or both. Runtime alone cannot distinguish these causes.

Core method

Twenty-six tasks with 85 workloads pair a PyTorch reference with expert-derived guidance at three dependent levels: algorithmic transformations, dataflow, and execution techniques. Guided and unguided agents receive identical tools, Triton interfaces, B200 hardware, and 350-turn budgets; neither receives expert source code.

Candidates compile, run correctness checks, and receive timing and profiling feedback. The best fully valid submission is retained. Separate runtime-blind LLM assessments score independent design proposals and evidence in generated code. Cumulative L1, L1+L2, and L1+L2+L3 ablations respect dependencies rather than pretending the levels are independent interventions.

Contributions

The protocol connects stated designs, realized implementation properties, and measured performance. Across five models, guidance raises correctness from 93.1% to 98.5% and the all-task performance score from 1.46 to 1.95.

Strengths and limitations

Pairing makes guidance effects inspectable, but the tasks, hardware, expert selection, and model-based rubrics restrict generalization. The performance score penalizes invalid tasks and is not always a raw speedup. Judge agreement at model-aggregate level does not establish causal attribution for individual techniques.

What to improve

Repeat runs, audit rubric judgments with experts, and test guidance transfer across hardware and unseen workload shapes.

Connections

Strong Priors supplies algorithmic starting code; D2K-Bench supplies structured design explanations without source code. The contrast separates useful prior knowledge from the remaining burden of implementing it efficiently.

papers.title: DecompGym: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Designing Decomposition Algorithms
papers.summary: Audits generated Benders and column-generation solvers for prescribed information flow as well as execution, feasibility, and objective quality.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

An optimal-looking answer does not show that a generated solver actually implements its prescribed decomposition or justifies its optimality claim.

Core method

Agents write standalone Python solvers for 81 synthetic instances from five Benders and four column-generation families. The task contract requires operative master–subproblem information flow and forbids a monolithic fallback. Evaluation applies a 60-second, single-thread execution limit, numerical feasibility checks, a source-reading LLM method judge, and an objective within 1% of a stored optimum.

Independent regeneration and reflection share their first attempt. Reflection receives the failed code and a separate diagnosis informed by execution and the method judge's rationale. Up to ten attempts are allowed, with failures, time, and tokens recorded.

Contributions

The method-conformance gap isolates plausible answers produced by nonconforming algorithms: 93 of 108 method-audit rejections would pass output-only checks. The study also distinguishes repairable, localized defects from objective gaps with less informative feedback.

Strengths and limitations

First-attempt success is 87.8% across twelve model–tool combinations. Reflection converts 66% of retries into successes versus 39% for regeneration, but this is not an equal-token comparison. Instances are moderate-sized, each setting has one trajectory, and accepted programs were not independently audited; a single judge may favor its own model.

What to improve

Add expert-reviewed accepted cases, repeated seeds, larger instances, and solver-bound diagnostics that locate objective-gap failures.

Connections

FrontierOR allows agents to choose full solution methods. DecompGym instead fixes a decomposition contract and checks its implementation, exposing an evaluation distinction that output quality alone cannot resolve.

papers.title: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting
papers.summary: Periodic whole-team restarts discard agent sessions and search history but preserve the best evaluated program, reducing historical anchoring during long-budget discovery.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

More tokens or collaborating agents do not necessarily yield more varied ideas: accumulated histories can anchor all workers to increasingly small edits. The paper tests forgetting as a separate scaling mechanism.

Core method

Each agent edits a candidate, submits it to a judge, and stores the code, score, and feedback as a versioned commit. Team members can asynchronously inspect peers' candidates before proposing changes, without direct dialogue. A reducer controls which filesystem records and session history each agent receives. Search is divided into rounds; at a boundary it removes every session and candidate-history record from the active workspace, retains only the team-wide best program and its score, and restarts all agents with the original instructions. Communication resumes within the new round. Thus it resets both conversational and external search context rather than merely compressing the transcript.

Contributions

  • Separates parallelism, candidate-mediated communication, and whole-history forgetting within one agent harness.
  • Compares matched spending on four tasks spanning combinatorial programming, a VLIW kernel, and small-language-model training, with three runs per configuration.

Strengths and limitations

The team-with-forgetting configuration performs best on the tested tasks, but evidence uses one model and a small task set. Most improvement follows the first reset; later returns diminish. Fixed round boundaries and incumbent-only retention can discard useful negative evidence or complementary candidates, so the best forgetting policy remains unresolved.

What to improve

Learn reset timing from stagnation, compare selective retention policies, and test whether recovered exploration offsets repeated mistakes on longer, noisier tasks.

Connections

SimpleEvol compresses search history to preserve usable experience. This method deliberately removes both sessions and the visible archive at resets, making the amount of retained history—not population size alone—the central experimental variable.

papers.title: Harnessing LLMs with Direction-Scope Control for Combinatorial Solver Refinement
papers.summary: Groups representative failures and progressively narrows permitted code changes as solver feasibility increases, reducing repair-induced regressions.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A revision may fix current failures while breaking previously feasible instances, even when the aggregate pass rate improves. DiSH explicitly controls both which failures guide an edit and how extensive that edit may be.

Core method

Every demonstration instance passes through execution/resource, output-format, and constraint checks; the record identifies its first failed stage or feasible objective. The current feasible fraction chooses a semantic revision mode: broad algorithm replacement at low feasibility, then progressively narrower strategy and parameter edits, with protected behavior at full feasibility. These are prompt-level instructions, not a proof that edits cannot violate constraints. Direction control groups failures by stage and normalized diagnostic signature. Alternatives select one representative per group, prioritize cross-round regressions, or focus on high-coverage groups according to current scope. Successful cases remain as anchors. The selected evidence and scope instruction accompany the current solver in the next generation prompt.

Contributions

  • Measures instance-level feasibility oscillation rather than only net pass-rate changes.
  • Separates scope control from representative-evidence construction and tests their interaction.
  • Evaluates nine combinatorial benchmarks and four backbones, reporting held-out quality/yield and demonstration-set stability.

Strengths and limitations

The policy primarily protects feasibility, so its increasingly conservative edits may inhibit quality improvement after all demonstrations pass. Thresholds and representative-selection rules are hand-designed. Prompt compliance is empirical, and feasibility on demonstrations does not establish correctness on unseen inputs. Quality components can be computed on different verified subsets across methods.

What to improve

Learn quality-aware scope rules, retain regression protection while allowing major improvements, and report quality on common feasible test subsets as well as yield.

Connections

RefineEvo adapts operator choice from population statistics and retrieves trajectory-conditioned lessons. DiSH instead derives a separate pre-generation edit-scope restriction directly from feasibility and compresses failures by diagnostic groups, emphasizing regression prevention over broad evolutionary exploration.

papers.title: DivAlgo: A systematic evaluation of algorithmic diversity for code generation models
papers.summary: Builds a human-grounded algorithmic-diversity benchmark and distilled similarity metric to test whether generated solutions cover distinct computational strategies.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Correct programs can repeatedly instantiate one familiar algorithm. This matters both for diversity-preserving search and for interpreting claims of algorithmic originality.

Core method

DivAlgo filters correct C++ submissions from CodeContests+ using dependency-graph and embedding distances, then LLM-ensemble pair judgments. Its 7,623 problems include two representative solutions and retained human pools. An ontology separates programming paradigms, techniques, and data structures.

A distilled code encoder approximates algorithmic similarity. The Vendi score of its similarity matrix measures population diversity; ontology overlap measures coverage of the two references. Twenty-four models are tested with ordinary sampling, higher temperature, verbalized sampling, iterative constraints, and human-strategy guidance. Correctness and matched sample sizes remain separate controls.

Contributions

The benchmark combines fine-grained strategy labels with a scalable population metric and shows that stronger diversity prompting helps more than merely pooling model outputs.

Strengths and limitations

Unconditioned generations recover only a fraction of human diversity; the best tested strategy reaches about 70.5% on a matched 25-sample subset. This is a metric- and subset-specific result. LLM-derived labels, imperfect encoder agreement, C++ concentration, and two-reference coverage constrain interpretation; a Vendi score is not a literal count of proven distinct algorithms.

What to improve

Expand expert validation and reference families, test more languages, and measure whether diversity improvements increase downstream search quality.

Connections

DivAlgo explicitly discusses and validates against BehaveSim. It trades execution-trace specificity for scalable static embeddings and ontology labels, enabling broader coverage while introducing a different approximation.

papers.title: Dream-COP: Guiding Algorithm Discovery for Combinatorial Optimization Problems in an Experience World
papers.summary: Dream-COP learns executable search-allocation policies by replaying historical revision trees before deploying them to guide new heuristic and solver discovery.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A good program generator still wastes evaluations if its controller repeatedly extends unproductive branches. This paper makes the controller itself a design object and uses completed searches as inexpensive evidence for improving it.

Core method

A discovery agent generates either heuristic components or complete solvers, while an independent evaluator records feasibility and development-set quality.
