Each round forms a tree with alternative revision chains. A second LLM agent writes a Python policy that chooses a new root branch, extends a current leaf, or stops. Candidate policies are replayed on earlier trees: they observe only outcomes revealed by their own actions, and replay performs neither fresh LLM generation nor solver evaluation. Selection maximizes the mean of the top five feasible scores minus a request-cost penalty. Four sequential policy-proposal calls use replay feedback; the winning policy controls the next real round, whose results expand the history. Model weights remain fixed.

Contributions

  • Separates solver discovery from executable allocation-policy discovery, with matched replay and deployment interfaces.
  • Tests component design on TSP, knapsack, online packing, and flow-shop scheduling, plus complete two-dimensional packing solvers and cross-problem policy transfer.

Strengths and limitations

Three-run comparisons support better quality with fewer discovery requests; policy-learning tokens are accounted for separately. Replay can reveal only recorded continuations, so it is not a predictive world model for unseen edits. The top-five reward and cost penalty are design choices, and some reward ablations use a single run.

What to improve

Test replay-policy transfer across more heterogeneous solvers, quantify sensitivity to incomplete historical trees, and compare controllers under equal end-to-end monetary and execution budgets.

Connections

MCTS-AHD uses a prescribed tree-search rule to allocate heuristic revisions. Dream-COP instead searches executable branching and stopping rules using historical replay; the contrast is the allocation mechanism, not merely their benchmark comparison.

papers.title: DuoDiscover: Scaling Autonomous Discovery Beyond the Evaluation Bottleneck
papers.summary: DuoDiscover jointly discovers optimization targets and cheap proxy evaluators, continually checking proxy ranking fidelity against expensive true evaluations.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

When a true evaluation takes hours, increasing proposal throughput alone cannot scale discovery. The system must find changes that matter and an inexpensive way to judge their local progress.

Core method

Each worker chooses a code region and writes a tailored executable proxy, or yardstick, that returns a score and correctness flag. It hill-climbs that proxy in a fast inner loop and periodically submits promising states to the fixed expensive evaluator. After each true evaluation, a fidelity test compares proxy and true rankings using Kendall correlation on pairs separated beyond measured noise. A drifting proxy is invalidated and rebuilt or abandoned. A lightweight orchestrator terminates stalled workers, starts new targets, briefs active workers, and transfers or combines only confirmed changes. Neither a central task decomposition nor a user-marked edit region is required.

Contributions

  • Treats cheap evaluation as a discovered artifact coupled to its optimization target.
  • Tests repository and GPU/TPU suites plus extended engineering cases, reporting re-evaluated final candidates rather than the maximum noisy score observed during search.

Strengths and limitations

Main benchmark results are single-run, with repeated-run checks restricted to subsets. When no faithful proxy exists the method falls back to expensive search; proxy construction and fidelity warmup can dominate short budgets. A proxy may be used before enough paired evidence exists to validate it, so true evaluation remains essential.

What to improve

Study uncertainty-aware proxy admission, account for failed proxy construction and all hardware cost, and expand repeated-run evidence for expensive cases.

Connections

ArchAgent v2 reduces hardware-search cost with prescribed shortened traces before longer validation. DuoDiscover instead lets agents construct target-specific proxies and repeatedly invalidate them when their rankings cease to match true evaluations.

papers.title: Researcher-in-the-Loop Evolutionary Discovery of Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Code Families
papers.summary: Evolves finite-code search programs, then combines researcher-led family generalization with exact checks, nonexistence certificates, and Lean-checked algebra.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A valid finite construction does not establish an infinite family, an optimality claim, or autonomous mathematical discovery. This study separates those evidential steps.

Core method

AlphaEvolve edits a designated block of an annealing-style search program. The resulting program proposes matrices; an exact oracle computes code parameters and rewards promising entanglement-assisted quantum codes. Four campaigns contain 401 program evaluations with 240-second allocations.

Researchers inspect the finite outputs, derive a family formula, extend it to prime-power fields, and check the underlying algebraic certificate in Lean. Magma checks finite constructions, while checked DRAT proofs support ten nonexistence results. Later prompts incorporating the discovered formula are distinguished from the initial discovery campaigns.

Contributions

The family and entanglement lifting close 54 gaps in archived tables. A separate eight-block comparison tests iterative versus independent program generation: validation-selected programs transfer to unseen lengths with held-out success rates of 46.1% and 31.6%, versus 19.5% and 3.1%.

Strengths and limitations

Programs, finite codes, mathematical generalization, and proof artifacts have separate provenance. However, the primary controlled effect is not statistically significant at the generation-block level; equal proposal counts are not equal token budgets. Exact verification scales poorly, and the results concern algebraic code parameters, not hardware error rates. Human generalization is essential.

What to improve

Increase independent generation blocks, compare token- and compute-matched controls, and evaluate physical decoding and circuit costs.

Connections

AlphaEvolve supplies the program-evolution mechanism, adapted to exact quantum-code evaluation. Weight-Five BB also evolves generators, but emphasizes catalogue certification and connected-component reduction rather than researcher-derived infinite families.

papers.title: EdgeKernelBench: Unified LLM-Driven Kernel Generation for Edge Backends
papers.summary: Uses a shared graph–tensor–schedule IR and layered agent search to compare correctness and speed across heterogeneous edge backends.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Backend-specific source languages make it difficult to share algorithmic decisions or compare generated kernels across constrained edge devices.

Core method

EdgeKernelBench defines 331 canonical tasks spanning operators, subgraphs, and compact models. A unified IR exposes graph, tensor, and schedule decisions, while a compiler interface handles backend lowering. The reference TVM path performs legalization rather than silently optimizing the agent's decisions.

The Layered Edge Kernel Agent (LEKA) projects context to the active level, keeps candidate histories, and routes hardware evidence to the responsible layer. Progressive lowering fixes upper-level choices before refining lower-level ones. Evaluation covers mobile CPU, Jetson GPU, and Mali GPU backends.

Contributions

Best single-attempt correctness is 64.5%, but only 25.5% of outputs beat the reference. On the 69-task agent subset, LEKA reaches 43.5% Fast@1.0 versus 26.1% for Claude Code under the same base model and optimization budget.

Strengths and limitations

Shared semantics expose the correctness–performance gap across backends, and the agent comparison controls key budgets. However, the agent subset is smaller than the benchmark, supported compiler paths constrain the design space, and results do not establish portability to NPUs or heterogeneous execution within one program.

What to improve

Test unseen backend versions, broaden end-to-end agent workloads, and measure the performance cost of fixing upper-level decisions too early.

Connections

TileCas preserves editable alternatives across high- and low-level representations, including rollback. LEKA instead organizes search through a common layered IR and progressive lowering, exposing a concrete trade-off between revisitable abstractions and structured backend portability.

papers.title: EliteTable: Self-Improving Program Search for Executable Control Policies
papers.summary: Uses a fixed elite table to condition new, edited, and remixed control programs, then tests selected winners on fresh episodes.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

An archive can make program search improve in-run while repeatedly fitting the same evaluation episodes. Fresh-episode tests are needed to distinguish those outcomes.

Core method

EliteTable freezes a ten-program table each generation. Fifty candidate slots propose new programs, edits, or remixes of up to three parents, using a 20/40/40 mixture after initialization. Even nominally new proposals see the elite context; they are not independent-sampling controls.

Duplicate checks and bounded repair attempts precede evaluation on ten fixed episodes. The best ten incumbent and candidate programs form the next table. After ten generations, selected first- and last-generation winners are frozen and evaluated on one hundred new episodes. Each of six Gymnasium tasks has ten independent searches.

Contributions

All ten paired held-out endpoints improve in four tasks. The report also preserves important failures: six Acrobot searches decline, CartPole saturates in generation one, and BipedalWalker and CarRacing remain below their reporting targets.

Strengths and limitations

Held-out episodes and paired search endpoints strengthen the descriptive evidence. There are no independent-sampling, non-LLM, archive-size, or operator-mixture controls, so the study cannot attribute gains or establish relative performance. The search controller and model weights do not themselves evolve.

What to improve

Add budget-matched controls, ablate archive conditioning and remixing, and test robustness beyond the selected episode distributions.

Connections

FunSearch uses archived programs to condition further executable proposals. EliteTable explores a simpler fixed-table, new/edit/remix design for control policies; the relevant contrast is archive organization, not evidence of general recursive self-improvement.

papers.title: Epi: Towards a Persistent, Self-Improving Agent for Autonomous Research
papers.summary: Épi sustains research through persistent versioned branches, hierarchical lessons, and independent review; its turbo configuration applies the same continuity mechanisms to budgeted solver development.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Long investigations lose experimental state and rationale when a model session ends. Algorithm development also requires preserving executable alternatives, not merely a textual summary of the best result.

Core method

A campaign fixes a task-specific evaluation contract, feasibility tolerances, and improvement threshold before search. The agent runs experiments on versioned branches, preserves abandoned approaches with reasons, and can resume or fork earlier implementations. Code and detailed artifacts stay in a filesystem; a separate memory store retains reusable lessons and dead ends. Session handovers select the state and evidence needed for continuation. An independent model reviews research direction, while an isolated verifier checks artifacts. Épi-turbo reuses this persistence for standalone optimization solvers, supplies the quality–runtime scoring formula, reserves call costs before execution, and stops when further sessions do not improve the verified score. Review and extra validation were disabled in its reported short-task runs.

Contributions

  • Connects cross-session continuity to inspectable code, experiments, branch history, and certificates.
  • Evaluates solver development on thirty FrontierOR tasks with matched model and per-task spending limits, separately from its mathematical record campaigns.

Strengths and limitations

The higher aggregate solver score is mainly a runtime benefit, not uniformly better solution quality: the comparator wins direct objective comparisons on more instances. The benchmark uses one run per system and task, so it does not establish statistical significance. Released results and certificates should not be confused with release of the complete agent implementation.

What to improve

Repeat the solver experiments, report quality and runtime separately, and isolate the effects of memory, branching, stopping, and independent review.

Connections

Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting keeps only the incumbent when restarting. Épi takes the complementary approach of preserving alternative code branches and selectively retrieving lessons; the trade-off is escaping historical anchoring versus retaining recoverable research evidence.

papers.title: EPOCH: Coverage-Aware Evolution with Experiential Preference Optimization for LLM-based Automated Heuristic Design
papers.summary: EPOCH uses per-instance coverage to control heuristic evolution and trains its generator with preference pairs plus distillation of teacher-guided improvements.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Average fitness obscures specialist heuristics that solve different instances well, while prompt-only reflection is lost when the generator receives no hint. This EPOCH addresses both gaps in one online search.

Core method

Each heuristic has a per-instance optimality-gap vector. The pool's coverage objective averages the best available gap on each instance; expert counts and vector differences guide parent choice, complementary crossover, operator rewards, and stagnation recovery. A persistent expert archive survives pool resets. The generator produces unhinted candidates, a fixed teacher critiques their successes or failures, and the generator produces a second hinted batch. Evaluations create within-batch preference pairs and cross-round pairs where hinted candidates actually improve. Periodic LoRA updates combine DPO with a negative-log-likelihood reflective self-distillation term on those improvements, conditioned on the original unhinted prompt. The result is a complementary set of executable heuristics, not solely one average-best rule.

Contributions

  • Extends coverage from survivor selection into parent selection, operator allocation, and recovery.
  • Transfers verified reflective improvements into generator weights and evaluates both single rules and best-of-set portfolios across three constructive optimization domains.

Strengths and limitations

Portfolio scores take the best result over multiple executed heuristics; they are not evidence of a free perfect selector. The teacher remains fixed, and experiments cover step-by-step construction rather than local-search or ant-colony controllers. Training compute, teacher calls, and portfolio deployment cost all affect practical efficiency.

What to improve

Learn inexpensive instance routing, jointly optimize teacher feedback, and compare under complete search-plus-deployment resource budgets.

Connections

EoH-S makes complementary heuristic sets the design object. EPOCH extends that coverage objective through search control and adds online preference learning and reflective distillation. It is distinct from EPOCH-Evidence, which governs research claims rather than training heuristic generators.

papers.title: EPOCH: Reliable Discovery through Evidence-Governed Search
papers.summary: Uses explicit task contracts, typed trial records, falsification, admission gates, and frozen-endpoint replay to bind discoveries to their supported scope.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Passing an evaluator, checking a finite certificate, and proving a general theorem support different claims. EPOCH records these distinctions during search rather than treating a high score as sufficient evidence of discovery.

Core method

A task contract fixes public and terminal data, evaluators, budget, editable artifacts, and allowed claim scope. Each proposal includes a candidate, mechanism hypothesis, predicted effect, references to prior evidence, and an intended falsifier. An append-only ledger records artifact/evaluator identity, objective, correctness, resource use, and failure attribution; the model receives a bounded projection. Explore, refine, recover, and finalize phases use that evidence without claiming a learned optimal schedule. Candidate admission requires all applicable correctness, challenge, resource, and scope gates to pass; failed and unresolved checks remain distinct and cannot replace a verified incumbent. After selection, independent replay evaluates the frozen artifact without feeding results back into that run. A sealed record binds the claim to its contract and receipts.

Contributions

  • Separates useful failure evidence from eligibility to become the retained endpoint.
  • Evaluates a 12-task AlgoTune subset, internal Math14, and AgentHPO component ablations.
  • Audits executable constructions and mathematical artifacts with explicit finite-check, formal-proof, and unresolved-bridge boundaries.

Strengths and limitations

The safety invariant is only relative to the registered checkers and their coverage. Official-test replay covers a different eligible endpoint population from the development aggregate; scores should not be read as identical-sample effects. Resource accounting and paired replication remain limited, and some mathematical claims still need external review or proof bridges. No public framework-code URL is supplied.

What to improve

Release replayable artifacts and complete resource ledgers, enlarge paired evaluation, and independently audit the alignment between formal statements and generated objects.

Connections

Lean Runtime pursues machine-checked asymptotic runtime certificates for generated randomized algorithms. EPOCH instead governs heterogeneous empirical, finite, and formal evidence through scoped admission. Both constrain what can be claimed, but only the former makes a particular runtime-proof target central. This EPOCH is unrelated to EPOCH-Coverage.

papers.title: Evo-B&B: Behavior-Aware LLM-Guided Joint Evolution of Branching and Node Selection Policies for MILP
papers.summary: Jointly evolves branching and node-selection programs with behavior-probe diversity, island search, and selective continuous-parameter tuning.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A branching rule changes which subproblems exist; node selection changes which are explored first. Optimizing them separately can miss their interactions, while syntactically different code can still make identical decisions.

Core method

Each individual contains two executable scoring functions and continuous parameters, integrated through a fixed SCIP interface. LLM mutation and crossover operate across islands using parent code, rationales, solving feedback, and operator instructions. End-to-end training-instance solves measure time and node-count ratios.

Fixed decision probes collected from default SCIP record top choices and relative scoring preferences for both policies. Behavioral similarity removes redundant candidates unless they Pareto-dominate their closest counterpart; quality–diversity selection handles capacity. Islands exchange design information and reset on stagnation. Retained candidates near the island-best fitness receive ten bounded Gaussian parameter-tuning steps with code structure held fixed.

Contributions

The paper turns two coupled B&B decisions into one design object. Four MILP classes at three scales test the policies; the method has the lowest average runtime in six of twelve settings. Ablations distinguish behavioral diversity from AST similarity and joint search from independently evolved components.

Strengths and limitations

Behavior probes target decision diversity rather than textual novelty. Fixed default-solver states may not cover states visited by evolved policies, and runtime and node count can disagree. Gains are not uniform across all scales or problem classes; full solves and tuning remain expensive.

What to improve

Refresh probes with policy-induced states, account for tuning and failed candidates in total budgets, and test heterogeneous real-world MILP collections.

Connections

TIDE separates island-based structural evolution from numeric tuning. Evo-B&B explicitly uses that design pattern for coupled SCIP policies, replacing structural-diversity emphasis with matched behavioral probes and tuning only promising retained candidates.

papers.title: EvoAlloc: A Self-Evolving Resource Allocation Agent for Efficient Program Evolution
papers.summary: EvoAlloc evolves an explicit evaluation-allocation strategy from observed decisions and audits randomly chosen rejected programs to expose false-pruning feedback.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

An allocator learns only from programs it evaluates, so an overly conservative policy can hide its own mistakes. The paper makes evaluation allocation an evolving, auditable component of program search.

Core method

A fixed LLM reads the candidate, parent and sibling evidence, budget, an explicit strategy, and accumulated experiences. It selects full evaluation, discard, or—where available—a partial test followed by continuation or stopping. Periodic consolidation records supporting and contradicting cases with tentative, active, or stale status. A challenger strategy is compared with the incumbent on future disagreements; the union of requested evaluations is executed so neither policy censors the other's evidence. Adoption first minimizes missed new bests, then full and partial evaluation cost. Independently, a fixed probability sends rejected candidates to full evaluation, and those counterexamples inform later strategy updates and can re-enter the program archive.

Contributions

  • Separates an evolving allocation policy from the unchanged program generator and evaluator.
  • Implements the mechanism inside ShinkaEvolve and reports five-seed comparisons on AIME reasoning-harness optimization and circle-packing programs.

Strengths and limitations

The two tasks provide contrasting partial-evaluation access but limited domain breadth. Allocation experience is confined to one run, and the challenger check stops after only two fully observed disagreements. Efficiency is reported in full evaluations and LLM tokens rather than a universal hardware-cost measure. The initial strategy summarizes 50 cases from five baseline runs, whose acquisition cost is excluded from reported search costs. Code is promised upon acceptance.

What to improve

Calibrate the rejected-candidate audit rate, use stronger uncertainty estimates for strategy adoption, and test cross-run experience transfer and heterogeneous evaluator costs.

Connections

ShinkaEvolve supplies the underlying archive and evolutionary pipeline. EvoAlloc extends its evaluation stage with strategy revision and counterfactual checks, while keeping generation and the task evaluator fixed.

papers.title: ExpEvolve: Structuring and Reusing Experience for Open-Ended Discovery
papers.summary: ExpEvolve extracts interpretable idea factors from unexplained program-score differences and uses bandit-selected factor edits and plateau interventions to guide further program discovery.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A code archive or prose summary may preserve examples without identifying which high-level choices explain their performance. ExpEvolve seeks reusable, testable design factors rather than only surface edits.

Core method

The system annotates archived programs with binary or categorical idea factors. A pairwise ranker predicts which program should score better; large unexplained score contrasts trigger an LLM to propose missing factors. Candidate factors are annotated across the archive and admitted only with adequate support and score separation. Factors become edit actions such as add, remove, or set a mechanism. A bandit assigns idea-guided proposal slots using evaluation rewards normalized against same-generation open-search proposals, while reserving other slots for broad exploration. At plateaus, the system identifies properties shared by leading programs, masks actions that reinforce that background, and supplies more diverse exemplars to create new contrasts.

Contributions

  • Turns learned representations of algorithmic ideas into explicit search actions rather than passive memory.
  • Evaluates eleven mathematical tasks with 200-program budgets and three seeds, and integrates the mechanism into six MLS-Bench tasks.

Strengths and limitations

The sample-efficiency argument assumes a faithful factor representation; the practical LLM annotations do not establish causal effects. Experiments use relatively inexpensive, small-scale verification, and factor discovery itself incurs model overhead. The paper states that it extends CausalEvolve (arXiv:2603.14575), which should not be mistaken for an unrelated lineage.

What to improve

Audit factor annotations and intervention faithfulness, report all factor-learning costs, and test with noisy or expensive scientific evaluators.

Connections

EvoMem retrieves lessons associated with successful edits. ExpEvolve additionally tests whether categorical factors explain score ordering and makes add/remove/set actions over those factors the search controller's choices.

papers.title: FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution
papers.summary: Assigns strategy exploration to an expensive model and repeated implementation to a cheaper one, with prompt-prefix reuse and cost-budgeted evaluation.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A search that produces better programs per iteration may still be less useful per dollar. FrugalEvo assigns model capability by role and measures the entire best-so-far quality curve over model spend.

Core method

A cheap model first improves the starter until progress stops, establishing the incumbent. A strong model analyzes the task/evaluator and proposes several concrete modification strategies in one call. The cheap generator implements one trial per strategy, ranks them by execution scores, and refines strategies in that order. During a refinement round, the strategy and parent stay fixed while failed attempts contribute feedback; an improvement updates the incumbent and starts another round on the same strategy, whereas an unsuccessful round advances to the next strategy. Island-based MAP-Elites stores code, scores, strategies, and failures. Prompts place invariant task content first, slower-changing elite context next, and new feedback last to increase cacheable prefix overlap. Search stops at the model-spend allowance; BA-AUC integrates best-so-far quality over that budget.

Contributions

  • Combines explicit ideation/implementation roles with cheap cold start and sequential repair.
  • Reports final quality and cost-curve area on 20 mathematical, systems, and algorithmic tasks.
  • Ablates model-role pairing, cold start, and sequential feedback under fixed model-cost budgets.

Strengths and limitations

The budget measures model charges, not evaluator or other execution compute. Savings depend on provider prices, cache behavior, and the suitability of the cheaper implementation model. Experiments use small budgets and hand-crafted strategy instructions. Circle-packing scores include radius adjustments within evaluator tolerance, so tiny numerical improvements need stricter independent validation.

What to improve

Report uncached and full-compute costs, evaluate longer budgets, and validate near-record numerical artifacts with tighter independent feasibility checks.

Connections

SpecEvo also combines cheap and expensive models but assigns them differently: cheap speculators explore code while a stronger navigator periodically synthesizes or redirects search. FrugalEvo instead pays for strong strategy proposals and delegates repeated implementation to the cheaper model.

papers.title: Generative Adversarial Loops
papers.summary: Alternates agentic adversarial benchmark generation with algorithm repair, retaining earlier tests to expose and correct approximation failures.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

An algorithm can improve on a fixed benchmark while retaining systematic blind spots. GAL makes discovering the next informative failure an explicit search problem alongside editing the algorithm.

Core method

The discriminator searches for valid inputs that a current approximate-inference algorithm fails, then appends them to a cumulative benchmark. The generator edits the algorithm against that enlarged benchmark while retaining earlier requirements. In long-context tasks, discriminator outputs are executable data-generation programs with answers known by construction; a control using unapproximated inference helps reject intrinsically unsolvable examples. The two searches use agentic/evolutionary harnesses, not adversarial gradient training. In the demonstrated closed loops, GEPA generates counterexamples and coding agents revise the approximation code. For example, a ledger-retrieval failure prompts chunk-stratified KV allocation, followed by a second counterexample that motivates combined key-distinctiveness, attention, and value-norm scoring.

Contributions

  • Finds interpretable failure patterns across KV compression, sparse video generation, sparse attention, and context extension.
  • Runs two complete benchmark-generation/algorithm-repair rounds in KV compression and context extension, with separate standard-benchmark checks.
  • Measures the search cost needed to expose a failure under a specified adversary.

Strengths and limitations

The closed-loop evidence covers two domains and two rounds, not all four discriminator tasks. Some standard-benchmark gains are modest or non-monotonic across generations. The proposed cost certificate depends on the adversary, model, budget, and evaluator; it is not a universal robustness guarantee. Finite-convergence reasoning also requires assumptions about the task space and successful repairs.

What to improve

Run longer replicated loops, reserve unseen adversarial generators for testing, and include generator, discriminator, and execution costs in the same budget.

Connections

RAISE also changes the inputs used to judge a generated algorithm. Its adversarial instance search targets robustness within a prescribed uncertainty set; GAL evolves structured benchmark generators and repairs approximate-inference algorithms against a growing archive of counterexamples.

papers.title: Evolving in Thought Space: Training a Small Model at Test Time Unlocks Better Discoveries
papers.summary: Trains a small guidance policy on verifier rewards while a larger frozen executor implements its parent-conditioned strategic changes.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Updating a model that writes entire programs makes test-time learning costly and mixes strategic quality with implementation reliability. Guidance-TTT places adaptation in short, explicit proposed changes instead.

Core method

A parent-linked archive stores executable solutions, verifier scores, solution summaries, and summaries of changes from their parents. A PUCT rule selects parents using best-child quality, a rank prior, and expansion counts. An 8B or 14B guidance model sees compact summaries and samples a sibling group of natural-language modifications. The frozen executor receives each modification and the exact parent code, then produces a complete child program. Verifier rewards update only the guidance policy with an entropic, group-relative RL objective; adaptive within-group reward weighting emphasizes high-scoring candidates. Eligible evaluated children and their summaries return to the archive. Thus the learned action is strategic text, while code generation and implementation capacity remain in a separate fixed model.

Contributions

  • Combines archive reuse with trainable guidance and frozen implementation.
  • Evaluates packing, AHC058, Lasso-path solvers, and TriMul kernels, including held-out Lasso tests and kernel-environment transfer.
  • Includes frozen-guidance and direct-code-training controls, with a practical large-executor cost comparison.

Strengths and limitations

The flagship comparisons mix published references, differently budgeted baselines, and distinct model configurations. The reported 58% cost reduction also uses different rollout counts and training schedules, not a strictly equal-compute intervention. Executor mistakes still contaminate the guidance reward. Extra parent context helps one tested task and hurts another, so more information is not uniformly beneficial.

What to improve

Replicate independent searches at matched total training, inference, and evaluation budgets; separate poor guidance from failed implementation when assigning credit.

Connections

HarnessTTT also trains a proposer while leaving execution frozen. Guidance-TTT learns a parent-conditioned strategic change; HarnessTTT learns the broader harness, including prompts, skills, tools, and middleware. This changes the action space and the credit-assignment problem.

papers.title: Harmony Harness: Multi-Objective Self-Evolution of Agent Harnesses
papers.summary: Evolves repository-scale agent harnesses through objective-decomposed populations and separately editable general and environment-specific components.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A harness can improve benchmark accuracy while becoming less safe or less transferable. Treating the entire harness as one scalar-scored artifact hides these trade-offs.

Core method

Harmony Harness keeps one incumbent for each preference vector in a decomposition-based multi-objective search. Scalarized shortfalls guide replacement among neighboring preferences. The editable artifact includes orchestration, tools, skills, and repository logic, except for a minimal required interface.

Failure-derived hypotheses guide component edits, followed by validation, repair, or rollback. Operators distinguish general mechanisms from environment-specific adaptations; a generalization operator can change that boundary. At inference, selected components are composed into an execution DAG.

Contributions

Across SecRepoBench and BaxBench, held-out studies report improvements in functionality and security, including 66.7% jointly functional-and-secure performance in a cross-benchmark setting versus 36.7% for its baseline. Ablations test objective decomposition and factorized editing.

Strengths and limitations

Separate splits and joint metrics help expose grader exploitation. However, some observed fronts collapse to a candidate strong on both objectives, so the experiments do not establish difficult Pareto trade-offs. A perfect training score was exploitable; operational component labels do not prove transferability or security.

What to improve

Use independently maintained security evaluators, harder conflicting objectives, and cost-matched transfer tests that freeze component selection before final evaluation.

Connections

DGM archives self-modifying coding agents as whole implementations. Harmony Harness makes an alternative design choice: objective-decomposed selection and explicit component boundaries support multi-objective search and recomposition.

papers.title: HarnessTTT: Learn to Optimize Harness at Test-Time for Scientific Discovery
papers.summary: HarnessTTT trains a separate proposer to generate executable search harnesses, scoring their budgeted rollouts with a frozen executor and retaining explicit transferable harness artifacts.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Updating the solver model stores adaptation in its weights; editing context alone requires repeatedly reinterpreting experience. HarnessTTT instead trains the model that designs the procedure around a frozen solver.

Core method

A proposer samples harness revisions containing prompts, skills, Python tools, middleware, and execution controls. Validated, deduplicated harnesses all start from the same incumbent program and each receive a bounded executor rollout. Best valid rollout scores produce gap-normalized rewards; within-parent leave-one-out advantages, near-tie filtering, and softmax sharpening guide a clipped, KL-regularized LoRA update on proposer tokens only. Executor parameters remain unchanged. The next round retains the best solution, its harness, a diversity-preserving runner-up, and a bounded experience digest. Static checks, restricted interfaces, sandboxed tool tests, and repair screening guard the generated tools without constituting a formal safety guarantee.

Contributions

  • Makes the complete executable harness a learned, inspectable action rather than merely a rewritten prompt.
  • Evaluates fourteen task settings and separately studies transfer to stronger executors and replay of fixed learned harnesses.

Strengths and limitations

The paper quarantines LLM-SQL and transaction-scheduling results, so aggregate frontier counts require that caveat. Stronger-executor transfer also adds further search, and fixed-harness replay uses one search seed. Reward shaping is a heuristic surrogate rather than an unbiased gradient of the best-of-group objective; some trajectory audit artifacts are unreleased.

What to improve

Explain and resolve quarantined task protocols, release audit artifacts, repeat searches, and separate harness transfer from extra compute and executor strength.

Connections

CALM updates the model generating heuristic code. HarnessTTT routes evaluation reward into a separate harness proposer while freezing the executor, changing both the trained object and the transferable artifact.

papers.title: HEMO: Harness Self-Evolution for Multi-Objective Combinatorial Optimization
papers.summary: Evolves the operator-design controller through local module replacements, using downstream quality–runtime trade-offs and persistent search records.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A search procedure can keep generating new operators while its own retrieval, parent selection, and generation policy remain fixed. HEMO makes these controller decisions editable without allowing edits to the evaluator.

Core method

An outer scheduler selects one of four modules: experience retrieval, target selection, parent selection, or candidate evolution. A proposer writes its replacement blueprint, a realizer implements it, and an executor runs the resulting harness from a common seed pool. Evaluator interfaces, archive rules, diagnostic tools, and record writing remain fixed.

The harness score averages negative hypervolume and runtime over its final operator archive. A child replaces the current harness unless its parent dominates it; normalized improvement updates discounted UCB credit for the edited module. All evaluation records persist, even for rejected children. Periodic summaries and stagnation reports support later retrieval. A selected harness is subsequently frozen for inference and related-task transfer.

Contributions

  • Separates editable search decisions from a protected execution and evaluation scaffold.
  • Tests harness evolution on eight multi-objective tasks with SEMO and NSGA-II backbones.

Strengths and limitations

Experiments include four-run comparisons and memory/scheduler ablations. Transfer concerns the harness, not accumulated task-specific memory. Nested evaluation and proprietary proposer models add substantial cost; advantages are task-dependent, with the neural comparator stronger on bi-objective CVRP.

What to improve

Measure amortized harness-training cost across repeated tasks and test memory transfer with safeguards against incompatible task assumptions.

Connections

E2OC searches interacting operator combinations inside a fixed controller. HEMO changes the controller itself. SimpleEvol instead keeps one compact generation trajectory with compressed history; HEMO preserves external records across evolving controller states. These are design contrasts, not claims that HEMO reuses their implementations.

papers.title: Holistic Diversity Management in LLM-Guided Evolutionary Search
papers.summary: Coordinates diverse island initialization, budget-aware island scheduling, and migration of complementary programs in LLM-guided search.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Separate islands can still explore almost identical programs. Diversity depends on their starting points, computational budgets, and exchanged references—not simply on maintaining several populations.

Core method

The method generates an initial candidate pool and selects island seeds by a max–min code-embedding distance criterion. Its scheduler combines normalized population quality, recent improvement, and an exploration bonus. Remaining budget shifts emphasis from growth toward current quality.

When an island grows slowly relative to others, it receives non-best programs from a faster-growing donor, prioritized by distance from its own best program. The recipient retains that best program as the parent and uses migrants as references. Migration therefore changes mutation context without pretending that copying a program is a locally discovered improvement. Initialization and subsequent generations share one budget.

Contributions

  • Treats initialization, scheduling, and migration as coupled diversity controls.
  • Evaluates six mathematical and systems tasks, with controlled diversity and scheduler studies.

Strengths and limitations

The experiments inspect descendant diversity as well as final scores. GPT-5 comparator results come from a prior paper rather than fresh matched reruns; component studies concentrate on signal processing. Embedding distance does not guarantee different execution behavior, and a qualitative migration example does not establish causality by itself.

What to improve

Rerun all methods under matched token and evaluator budgets, and compare code distance with behavioral diversity on held-out tasks.

Connections

ShinkaEvolve rejects code-near-duplicate proposals before evaluation. HoliDivEvolve instead uses code distance to choose seeds and complementary cross-island references. The contrast concerns where diversity is enforced, not merely which baseline wins.

papers.title: JANUS: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models
papers.summary: JANUS uses an evolving research graph and a reflective world-model agent to rank, refine, and prune experimental proposals before expensive implementation and evaluation.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Reactive execute-and-revise loops waste long experiments on weak branches. This JANUS tries to predict not only immediate improvement but also what an experiment could teach or enable later.

Core method

The orchestrator creates open proposal nodes by modifying, extending, or combining earlier research. A world-model agent compares proposal pairs on expected performance improvement, information gain, and future exploration utility; a sparse tournament yields normalized Bradley–Terry scores. Progress and remaining budget determine how those criteria are weighted. The agent can debate refinements, prune weak proposals, or revisit branches before the selected proposal is implemented and truly evaluated. Closed nodes retain code and results. Successful and failed trajectories then update intra-task and cross-task research skills, prediction/exploration skills for the world model, and coordination protocols. Adaptation is expressed in those evolving skills rather than demonstrated online weight training.

Contributions

  • Combines pre-execution proposal assessment with retrospective correction in one persistent graph.
  • Evaluates thirty MLS-Bench-Lite tasks and longer training, attention-kernel, and genotype-prediction investigations.

Strengths and limitations

Value and information-gain estimates are model judgments, not guaranteed calibrated forecasts. Pruning can censor alternatives whose true value is never observed. Reported sample efficiency does not by itself price proposal comparisons and reflection, and the three extended case studies provide limited evidence about broad long-horizon reliability.

What to improve

Measure forecast calibration and false-pruning rates, audit rejected proposals, and compare full compute and model cost across repeated searches.

Connections

PathWise uses a learned predictive representation to plan heuristic discovery. JANUS instead maintains a research DAG and updates explicit prediction and coordination skills from experiments while ranking proposals on immediate and downstream value. This is not the earlier repository entry named Janus.

papers.title: JustGoal: With Only a Goal, the AI Baseline Is Above the Expert Kernels
papers.summary: Tests a general-purpose goal-only coding agent against expert kernels and specialized harnesses, with independent final timing and correctness checks.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A specialized workflow's benefit can disappear when the underlying model improves. Released kernel artifacts alone cannot isolate the contribution of the harness that produced them.

Core method

JustGoal gives a general-purpose coding agent an optimization objective, target hardware, and constraints, but no kernel-specific knowledge base or prescribed search workflow. The agent constructs its own compilation, testing, and timing loop. The prompt still supplies important constraints, including numerical-tolerance guidance.

Authors independently recheck final kernels with the relevant FlashAttention or FlashInferBench procedures, including cold-cache and CUPTI measurements. Additional experiments hold the base model and single-shape scope fixed while varying harness components.

Contributions

On B200, retained kernels beat library implementations on eight of ten operators and the fastest available specialized-agent artifact on five of nine comparisons. In the controlled single-shape setting, KDA-0.5 reaches 0.95× JustGoal's performance.

Strengths and limitations

The same-model control is more informative than the headline artifact comparison, whose models and discovery budgets differ. Broader multi-shape scope can favor specialized infrastructure. Results do not establish that domain knowledge is universally useless, nor that finite numerical checks make kernels production-ready; reproducing the complete KDA workflow was also limited.

What to improve

Repeat with fully reproducible harnesses, equal end-to-end budgets, more devices, and whole-workload correctness and performance requirements.

Connections

D2K-Bench injects expert design explanations under controlled generation conditions. JustGoal supplies the complementary test: whether such assistance or predefined machinery adds value beyond the same model's independently constructed loop.

papers.title: Kernel Autoresearch for Open-Ended Model Discovery
papers.summary: Searches machine-learning kernel components under positive-semidefinite construction contracts, retaining behaviorally distinct candidates in a quality-diversity archive.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A fixed kernel grammar limits discoverable inductive biases, but a numerical PSD test cannot establish that arbitrary covariance code is a valid kernel. These are machine-learning kernels, not GPU compute kernels.

Core method

Agents generate feature maps, nonnegative spectral constructions, input transforms, or closure expressions. A trusted interpreter assembles their outputs into PSD-preserving kernels. Tiered acceptance checks execution, numerical behavior, and construction contracts, including determinism and consistency under input-batch changes. The backend, not the agent, tunes declared numerical parameters.

Search alternates new roots and revisions of archive elites. MAP-Elites cells combine behavior niches, dimensional growth, and novelty bands. Centered normalized Gram-matrix fingerprints compare candidates with known and discovered kernels; near-duplicates receive soft penalties rather than unconditional rejection. Meta-validation selects one frozen program before sealed test evaluation.

Contributions

The paper combines open component generation with algebraically controlled assembly. Experiments cover held-out black-box optimization families, forecasting, enzyme mechanisms, and glucose patients. Human refinement of a discovered kernel is reported separately from autonomous discovery.

Strengths and limitations

Construction gives stronger validity evidence than sampled PSD checks. The guarantee still requires finite, dimension-correct, pure component outputs; runtime consistency checks are not universal proofs of arbitrary Python purity. The optimization benchmark is small-data and at most eight-dimensional, and some programs fail at dimension sixteen.

What to improve

Enforce dimension-generic interfaces, strengthen purity restrictions, and test larger datasets and mixed-input domains without weakening the validity contract.

Connections

LeanPlan requires a generated proof for each heuristic's admissibility. Kernaut instead relies on trusted PSD-preserving assembly plus component checks: a concrete contrast between per-program proof search and validity by restricted construction.

papers.title: Proving LLM-Generated GPU Kernels Correct and Safe: Floating-Point Verification in Lean and VerCors
papers.venue: NeurIPS Workshop on AI for Verifiable Coding
papers.summary: Feeds Lean semantic proofs and VerCors parallel-safety checks back to kernel generation, with explicit translation and floating-point assumptions.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Passing selected numerical tests does not establish that a generated parallel kernel implements its specification for every supported input.

Core method

A deterministic translator turns a supported PyTorch FX specification into TorchLean. Generated CUDA is translated through a restricted Clang-based path into Velvet's sequential model. The agent constructs Lean proofs of floating-point semantic equivalence and separately supplies VerCors permissions and annotations for race freedom and memory safety.

Failed proof attempts or counterexamples guide revisions. The two verification branches are complementary: the sequential semantic argument assumes race freedom, while the parallel checker addresses that obligation. Transcendental operations use explicit shared-behavior assumptions rather than unrestricted real-number identities.

Contributions

Across thirty supported KernelBench tasks, two model configurations jointly discharge both verification branches on 11 and 22 tasks, respectively. The study demonstrates proof-guided generation over floating-point computations rather than only idealized arithmetic.

Strengths and limitations

Guarantees are conditional on the modeling assumptions, supported language subset, translators, and declared automation trust boundary. They are not a proof of the entire compiler or physical device. Import-failure retries differ from counted generation rounds; one campaign per configuration and no performance objective limit comparative claims.

What to improve

Verify translation passes, reduce trusted automation and operation assumptions, and measure proof coverage and speed together on broader kernels.

Connections

D2K-Bench combines execution tests with a design-adherence judge; this framework instead targets semantic and parallel-safety proof obligations under explicit assumptions. BIEvolve later tests the separate property of cross-batch bitwise consistency. These checks answer different reliability questions.

papers.title: Agentic Algorithm Design: LLMs that Propose, Formalise, and Prove Runtime Bounds for Evolutionary Algorithms in Lean
papers.summary: A staged LLM pipeline designs black-box optimizers and potential functions, then uses Lean-checked drift certificates to establish expected query-runtime bounds without empirical fitness comparisons.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Empirical success on benchmark instances does not establish that a generated optimizer is efficient for an entire problem class. This work couples algorithm invention with machine-checked expected-runtime analysis.

Core method

Starting from a formal problem card and a random-search baseline, the agent first proposes informal algorithm alternatives, then formalizes state, initialization, query, and transition functions in Lean. Proof guards enforce properties including measurability, reachability, use of randomness, and dependence on oracle fitness; failed formal stages trigger repair or backtracking. The agent next invents a normalized potential function and certifies that its zero set corresponds to optima. It defines improvement, worsening, and direct-hit events and proves their probability bounds. A pre-proved additive-drift result combines those certificates into an expected-runtime bound. The completed algorithm and bound can seed another generation; numerical benchmark scores never select designs.

Contributions

  • Demonstrates a single pipeline producing both algorithm definitions and checked stochastic runtime guarantees.
  • Reports completion in 12 of 15 frontier-model runs across eight problem classes, including an O(n²) CycleUncover design and integer-valued submodular minimization.

Strengths and limitations

The proofs certify the stated black-box query model, not unrestricted wall-clock efficiency: two successful designs use uncharged offline exact solving. Nine completed runs give polynomial bounds without that loophole. Simplified additive drift yields loose bounds, searches are restricted to bitstrings, open-weight models failed, and costly runs prevent a strong statistical study.

What to improve

Charge internal computation explicitly, provide richer drift theorems, audit specifications for unintended witnesses, and repeat designs across seeds and models.

Connections

LLaMEA-HPO selects executable optimizers using empirical performance and tuning. This pipeline pursues the same optimizer-design goal with formal drift certificates instead of measured fitness, trading practical breadth for conditional mathematical guarantees.

papers.title: LeanPlan: Optimal Planning with LLM-Generated Heuristics and Admissibility Proofs
papers.summary: Jointly generates domain-specific planning heuristics, checked task assumptions, and Lean admissibility proofs, using planner performance as the optimization signal.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

An effective learned heuristic need not be admissible, so using it in A* can sacrifice optimality. Numerical success on training tasks cannot establish the required universal property.

Core method

A deterministic translator compiles a unit-cost STRIPS domain into Lean definitions. The coding agent develops a reusable heuristic, a certificate checking its required domain assumptions, and proofs of goal awareness and consistency on reachable states. Compilation failures, proof failures, and measured planner runs guide revisions.

An independent controller rejects proof shortcuts and new axioms, rebuilds the artifacts, checks theorem dependencies and training-task certificates, and reruns planning. Acceptance also requires at least the baseline's training coverage and fewer total expansions on shared solved tasks. New instances must pass the certificate before the heuristic is used. Shared grounding and search theorems connect the compiled heuristic to returned-plan validity and conditional optimality.

Contributions

Heuristics and proofs are generated for ten IPC and three new domains. Tests include instances much larger than training tasks; the planner improves aggregate coverage and typically reduces expansions, without dominating every domain.

Strengths and limitations

Proofs concern executed heuristics rather than an unrelated mathematical surrogate. Guarantees apply only when certificates pass and returned plan cost is below the stated bound; unsolvability is not certified. Parser, formalized semantics, and Lean infrastructure remain trusted. Support is limited to unit-cost STRIPS.

What to improve

Expand to action costs and richer PDDL, audit the trusted parsing boundary, and measure proof-development cost across models and difficult domains.

Connections

A-CEoH supplies host-A* context and selects heuristics by time-limited solution quality. LeanPlan instead requires domain certificates and machine-checked goal-awareness and consistency before comparing planning performance. The contrast concerns acceptance conditions for generated A* heuristics, not framework inheritance.

papers.title: Long Text to Predictive Features: LLM-Guided Blockwise Feature Engineering via Executable Program Search
papers.summary: Builds deployable text-feature programs through immutable block additions, downstream validation, depth-calibrated rollback, and diverse parallel trajectories.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Long texts contain useful predictive information, but per-record LLM inference may be too costly. An offline-discovered feature program can convert that information into ordinary structured-model inputs.

Core method

The LLM generates complete code with a marked new block; extraction checks reject changes outside that region. Execution and text-feature screening precede local Bayesian tuning of the new block's parameters. A lightweight XGBoost evaluator measures its conditional validation-AUC gain alongside existing structured features. Positive additions are accepted and frozen.

Each trajectory maintains a block tree and an archived best program. Recent child successes and failures form a Beta-Bernoulli estimate, partially pooled with other blocks at the same depth. Low predicted expansion opportunity triggers rollback rather than endless extension. Multiple trajectories share only fixed descriptions of their exploration direction, not code or feature outputs; their final frozen programs are jointly used by the downstream model.

Contributions

Four datasets test predictive quality and inference cost. Production monitoring covers five risk-control applications and 2.69 million users, with reported improvements over the previous text-feature strategy. Deployment executes ordinary feature code without online LLM inference.

Strengths and limitations

The append-only contract protects accumulated behavior and makes rollback auditable. It can also preserve suboptimal early decisions, and independent trajectory scoring misses cross-program interactions until final fitting. Two datasets and deployment evidence are private; monitoring is not a randomized intervention.

What to improve

Evaluate cross-program feature redundancy, audit temporal drift and repeated-validation selection, and compare rollback with controlled edits to earlier blocks.

Connections

MCTS-AHD allocates expansions among heuristic-program nodes. LLM-BlockFE makes nodes immutable appended blocks and uses depth-relative child-success estimates for backtracking, trading unrestricted rewrites for stable incremental construction.

papers.title: Multi-Task Evolution for Zero-Shot Cross-Problem Generalization using LLMs
papers.summary: Combines task-conditioned populations using measured transfer gaps and selects a complementary heuristic set solely from source-task feedback.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Related constraints can create many unseen problem variants, making separate heuristic search for every combination impractical. MECo tests whether source-only evolution can supply useful heuristics for new combinations without target-side redesign.

Core method

Source tasks each activate one constraint attribute and provide an initial population. Task-level search pairs populations that contribute different attributes, prioritizing unexplored unions and low symmetric transfer gaps measured by cross-evaluating populations on their constituent source datasets. The LLM receives the combined specification and parent heuristics, then composes compatible mechanisms, resolves conflicting rules, explores under-covered source dimensions, or mutates for transfer. Combined-task candidates are still evaluated only on available source datasets, not instances of the combined target problem. Nondominated source-score fronts, crowding, and decision-behavior differences preserve complementary candidates. After evolution, greedy marginal coverage over combinations of source scores selects four frozen heuristics. Common feasibility masks allow their decision rules to operate across variants.

Contributions

  • Separates task-combination search from within-task heuristic evolution.
  • Evaluates 32 routing and scheduling variants, using only single-constraint variants for design feedback.
  • Tests native EoH, ReEvo, and HSEvo engines inside the multi-task framework, with additional ten-run scheduling comparisons.

Strengths and limitations

The shared decision interface and feasibility masks provide substantial domain structure. Reported Best4 is the lowest whole-target-dataset mean among four heuristics, not a learned selector fixed before seeing target results. Proposal matching does not equal evaluation cost, and the main experiments cover two compositional families with three runs. No own-method code link is supplied; listed GitHub repositories are baselines or task resources.

What to improve

Learn source-only deployment selection, include the cost of cross-task evaluations, and test task families with incompatible decision interfaces and genuinely new constraints.

Connections

EoH-S searches for complementary coverage across instances. MECo instead organizes interacting populations around task combinations and selects a set using source-combination coverage for unseen problem definitions. Population Evolution provides another transfer route: replaying model-code interventions with fresh training and promoting them across scales.

papers.title: MoSAIC: Learning DAG Scheduling Heuristics from Optimal Schedules through Motif-Aware Recovery and LLM-Guided Reasoning
papers.summary: Recovers compact priority rules from exact DAG schedules with Bayesian optimization and trains an LLM to select ready tasks using motif-aware evidence.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Exact scheduling is expensive, but its solutions can supervise reusable decisions rather than being discarded after solving each small instance.

Core method

CP-SAT produces optimal schedules for small DAGs. Bayesian optimization fits linear priority weights over fixed structural features such as rank, depth, fanout, indegree, and communication cost. The resulting motif-linked rules and optimal traces populate a knowledge base.

The paper then reports supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning of an LLM that selects the next ready task from structured context. Thus Bayesian optimization recovers the numeric heuristic parameters, while the LLM learns scheduling decisions; the method does not evolve arbitrary executable heuristic source.

Contributions

Reported decision accuracy rises from 67.5% after fine-tuning to 80.8% after reinforcement learning. Synthetic-task makespan gap averages 2.1%, compared with 5.6% for HEFT, with additional PolyBench and MachSuite studies.

Strengths and limitations

Optimal supervision provides a concrete target and interpretable feature weights. Evidence is concentrated on two-processor systems, with costly small-instance oracle generation and a fixed feature family. The claimed model fine-tuning procedure and implementation details are insufficiently specified for independent reproduction; larger heterogeneous and dynamic settings remain untested.

What to improve

Release the complete training recipe and artifacts, separate BO-only and LLM-policy contributions under matched budgets, and test processor-count and graph-distribution transfer.

Connections

EoH searches executable heuristic programs with natural-language explanations. MoSAIC instead fixes the priority-feature family and learns weights and next-task decisions from exact supervision. It is distinct from the repository's unrelated MOSAIC.

papers.title: MUSE: Multi-Level Memory with Selective Runtime Injection for Scientific Coding Agents
papers.summary: Supplies scientific coding agents with frozen multi-level experience and selectively injects implementation advice during tool execution.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A problem-level memory search may miss a useful numerical or implementation warning that becomes relevant only after code is written.

Core method

Completed source attempts yield approach lessons and implementation lessons linked to their code and observed outcomes. Consolidation builds a global bank; all banks are frozen before testing. Each target starts with global guidance and five problem-matched approaches.

After designated tool returns, four retrieval routes query implementation lessons, historical submissions, and errors using the current message, arguments, and output. Duplicate sources and already supplied references are excluded. A tool-free LLM gate selects at most one source, adds a concrete review suggestion, or injects nothing. The coding agent's weights and tool interfaces are unchanged. Hidden final assessments are not fed back to the agent.

Contributions

  • Connects task-level planning memory with operation-level checks.
  • Separates verified outcomes from suggested alternatives and evaluates both successful and failed source experience.

Strengths and limitations

Four benchmarks cover PDE solvers, kernels, and scientific repository repair. Gate and memory-level ablations support the design, and kernel memory transfers across two benchmarks. Results use one agent/model configuration and frozen banks; continual updates and broader transfer remain untested.

What to improve

Report retrieval/gating overhead against gains, test additional backbones, and evaluate how outdated numerical or library assumptions are retired.

Connections

EvoMem retrieves lessons from successful parent–child mutations to guide later code evolution. MUSE instead extracts successful and failed tool trajectories and decides whether to intervene at a particular implementation step. Both preserve source evidence, but their retrieval unit and timing differ.

papers.title: Network World Models as Environments for Algorithm Design on Complex Systems
papers.summary: Uses an action-conditioned network world model to evaluate executable intervention algorithms and return rollout diagnostics, marginal action credit, and counterfactual probes.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A network intervention matters through the diffusion it triggers. Repeated Monte Carlo evaluation of candidate algorithms is expensive, and final reward alone does not explain which action should change.

Core method

The world model applies an intervention's known graph/state changes exactly, then predicts subsequent diffusion with action-conditioned learned dynamics. A coding agent receives classical algorithm implementations as context and writes complete candidate intervention algorithms. Validity checks precede rollout scoring.

Candidates and incumbents use common sampled trajectories with fresh seeds each round. Promotion requires mean improvement larger than the paired estimate's standard error. Feedback includes temporal spread diagnostics, leave-one-action-out credit, and agent-requested counterfactual interventions. Exploration gives way to refinement over search. Final discovered algorithms are evaluated independently with the trusted Monte Carlo simulator, not just the learned evaluator.

Contributions

Eight tasks and five diffusion models test the generated algorithms, including cross-network transfer. The paper reports matching or exceeding the strongest listed comparison in 138 of 141 settings and analyzes how transition error and search suboptimality bound selection regret.

Strengths and limitations

Matched rollouts reduce sampling noise, while trusted final simulation checks surrogate transfer. The regret bound assumes error control over the reachable state-action support, which average prediction accuracy does not establish. Leave-one-out credit incurs additional evaluations and does not fully resolve action interactions; real-world dynamics can differ from the modeled diffusion families.

What to improve

Audit adaptive exploitation of world-model errors, incorporate uncertainty-triggered trusted evaluation, and test partially observed or changing diffusion processes.

Connections

TRACE extracts compact diagnostics and surrogate tools from observed execution logs. This work instead makes a learned simulator queryable for counterfactual actions and trajectory credit, contrasting retrospective extraction with intervention-based feedback.

papers.title: OptScientist: Automated Discovery of Optimization Laws
papers.summary: Infers compact symbolic objectives and constraints behind observed choices by learning an optimization landscape and then distilling its components.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

An input-output equation describes what happened; an optimization law additionally proposes what objective and constraints could have produced the observed choice.

Core method

OptScientist first learns a structured neural optimization model from contextual outcomes using preference or distributional evidence. Objectives and constraints form an explicit bottleneck. It then freezes the learned components and distills them into symbolic expressions, balancing fit against expression complexity and removing context-only constants where appropriate.

An optional LLM agent layer retrieves theoretical priors, selects variables, configures experiments, critiques candidate mechanisms, and proposes new observations. The core OptFeynman evaluation tests the model without this agent assistance. The output is an explanatory optimization problem, not a newly invented numerical optimizer.

Contributions

OptFeynman contains 99 physics-derived inverse-optimization tasks. The model perfectly recovers discrete preference order on 88 tasks and continuous order on 78 across tested candidate-set sizes. Risky-choice and monetary-policy studies examine held-out prediction with compact recovered laws.

Strengths and limitations

Order-based validation addresses equivalence beyond literal expression matching. Nevertheless, observational choices need not identify a unique objective, and predictive success does not establish causal mechanism. The optimization assumption, selected variables, symbolic language, and synthetic observation process constrain discoveries.

What to improve

Test observationally equivalent laws using interventions, expand misspecified and noisy settings, and isolate the agent layer's benefit at matched cost.

Connections

LLM-SR searches expressions that directly describe observed relations. OptScientist changes the design object to objectives and constraints whose induced choices explain those observations, adding an inverse-optimization identification problem.

papers.title: Organon : From Evolutionary Search to Recursive Self-Improving Agents for Scientific Discovery
papers.summary: Organon lets a persistent discovery agent revise its active search, diagnostic, memory, and coordination components between bounded search horizons while preserving history and a fixed official evaluator.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A discovery method can encounter a bottleneck its original controller or tools cannot diagnose. Restricting adaptation to candidate programs or a few prompt parameters leaves those operational failures outside the search.

Core method

The agent manages two objects: a persistent population/history and an editable composition of search, tools, memory, worker coordination, and execution rules. It chooses a bounded number of candidate attempts, runs the current search configuration, then inspects scores, lineages, failures, and worker findings. It may continue, replace a provider, add diagnostics, change worker instructions, or withdraw an earlier revision. Dependency-aware, reversible component registration makes these changes live without losing evaluated programs. Later outcomes inform whether to retain or correct the revision, including revisions to the diagnostic procedures themselves. Candidate failures consume budget; the official task evaluator and remaining budget cannot be rewritten.

Contributions

  • Makes runtime capability changes and their reversibility explicit, not just candidate mutation or prompt evolution.
  • Tests twenty-one algorithm, kernel, mathematical, and systems tasks and documents search-policy, diagnostic, and self-correction trajectories.

Strengths and limitations

The common allowance is candidate attempts, not equal monetary or internal diagnostic cost. Repeated evaluations of selected programs are not independent repeated searches. Trajectory analysis covers one run per task, and simultaneous revisions prevent causal attribution; the appendix also records undetected sign errors and unused changes.

What to improve

Add controlled revision ablations, repeat full searches, measure total resource use, and strengthen invariants and automatic rollback tests around dynamically changed components.

Connections

Beyond Algorithm Evolution co-evolves solver code and prompts. Organon changes a wider operational object—selection, survival, tools, coordination, and revision procedures—while keeping authoritative evaluation fixed; this is a design-object contrast rather than a claim of direct inheritance.

papers.title: Discovered, Not Designed: Population Evolution for Collaborative and Compute-Intensive Model Discovery
papers.summary: Connects local model-code searches through cross-instance replay and shared evidence, screening small-scale discoveries before expensive full training.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A locally successful model edit need not transfer to another dataset or survive full-scale training. Population Evolution makes cross-instance evidence and staged promotion part of ongoing search.

Core method

Each source instance retains its own parent archive and training protocol. When a candidate meets its local improvement criterion, the system publishes its executable intervention, mechanism description, provenance, and results to a shared ledger. Peer evaluation restores each receiving instance's reference code, applies the same intervention, and retrains its weights; failed transfers are recorded alongside successes. Summaries of this evidence condition subsequent local proposals without merging code archives. Promotion requires success on at least two of four peers. Joint discovery then tests larger-scale instances and shares their results. For expensive pretraining, small-data searches feed two intermediate evaluations, including a disjoint-data check; passing both permits full-target training. Full-target outcomes are deliberately withheld from proposal context in that track.

Contributions

  • Provides RMD-Bench with recommendation, RL-algorithm, LLM-pretraining, and VLM-pretraining families.
  • Tests shared evidence across multiple search harnesses and proposers.
  • Measures completed discovery runs under matched total GPU compute for expensive pretraining.

Strengths and limitations

Transfer requires compatible intervention interfaces. Recommendation target protocols are calibrated and reported on the same released test splits, so those results are not untouched-test generalization. In held-out RL tasks, the best PE candidate remains below the unmodified reference mean. Expensive full searches need more independent replication; local iteration matching does not equal total evaluation work.

What to improve

Reserve independent calibration and test splits, quantify whole-search variance, and adapt peer/promotion policies without letting target feedback leak into selection.

Connections

The main implementation uses AdaEvolve's local search, but this catalogue does not contain an AdaEvolve node. MECo develops frozen heuristic sets from source-task feedback; PE instead shares executable model interventions, retrains them on peer instances, and promotes successful changes across training scales. The comparison concerns how cross-task evidence supports transfer, not a claimed lineage.

papers.title: PRECOCIAL: Pretraining with Code Curriculums via Iterative Search for Accelerated Learning
papers.summary: Searches executable symbolic-data generators while carrying forward accepted network checkpoints, making successive programs a learned pretraining curriculum.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Useful synthetic pretraining distributions are often hand-written. Searching their generators is expensive because evaluating each program requires both pretraining and downstream fine-tuning.

Core method

A Python generator emits abstract ASCII sequences under a fixed contract that rejects English words. Its initial rule families include hierarchical structures, cellular automata, sequence operations, and reasoning. An LLM sees the accepted program, objective, recent learning curves, and a small downstream training sample; it can reweight, delete, rewrite, or invent rules.

Candidates continue pretraining from the last accepted network checkpoint, then receive downstream validation evaluation. A non-improving candidate is rejected together with its added training steps. Accepted generators and checkpoints accumulate a curriculum along a single chain. Thus fitness depends on the accepted training history, rather than treating each generator as an independently scored artifact.

Contributions

Language, code, and reasoning experiments compare searched programs with hand-written curricula, first-shot LLM programs, and program mutations. Under ten evaluations, continued pretraining reduces training work and improves average perplexity relative to independently trained population-search implementations; frozen-program transfer tests reuse curricula on other datasets.

Strengths and limitations

The method explicitly accounts for checkpoint reuse and rejection. Models are only 0.15M–3.36M parameters, and each task has three ten-evaluation searches. The paired perplexity advantage over FunSearch is not statistically conclusive. Longer accumulated pretraining partly explains gains, rather than generator quality alone.

What to improve

Disentangle curriculum order, total pretraining exposure, and program quality; test larger pretrained models and fully task-hidden discovery.

Connections

AlphaEvolve normally independently evaluates population candidates. PRECOCIAL explicitly replaces that assumption with an accepted single lineage carrying neural training state, trading independent fitness comparisons for cheaper cumulative learning.

papers.title: An important Bottleneck in LLM Optimizers: Principle-Level Local Optima
papers.summary: Diagnoses stalled LLM optimization through retained design principles, attainable reference gaps, and remaining-budget plateaus rather than code variation alone.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Many different candidate programs can express the same exhausted design principle. Surface diversity is therefore insufficient evidence of continued exploration.

Core method

The diagnostic protocol combines three conditions: a substantial gap to an attainable reference, concentration of retained principles, and a prolonged performance plateau. All three give strong support for collapse; incomplete combinations yield limited or unestablished evidence.
