Task-specific descriptors track molecular scaffolds, node incidence in selected sentinel sets, and executed GPU-kernel routes. These are observable proxies, not direct measurements of latent reasoning. Archives of high-performing candidates are inspected across evolutionary, reflective, and principle-space Bayesian optimizers. Interventions vary sampling diversity or provide reference-derived principles without supplying finished solutions.

Contributions

The benchmark separates candidate variation from principle concentration and tests whether broader sampling or explicit hints prevent or relieve stagnation.

Strengths and limitations

Among 161 assessable runs, 78.3% support collapse and 55.3% strongly support it. Kernel source diversity can remain high while one route dominates. Hints help some runs but worsen others. Labels depend on domain-specific descriptors and thresholds; most references are attainable baselines, not global optima, and route-investment correlations are not causal evidence.

What to improve

Validate online detectors prospectively, audit route annotations, and preserve promising principles long enough to improve initially weak implementations.

Connections

BehaveSim compares executed trajectories and uses that distance during candidate selection. Principle Collapse instead diagnoses retained, coarser design routes together with an attainable-reference gap and a plateau. The contrast concerns the granularity and purpose of observable diversity evidence, not an inheritance claim.

papers.title: Directing to Diversify: Multi-Directional Search for Automatic Heuristic Design
papers.summary: PRS separates directional changes to heuristic ideas from code rewriting, using expansion, compression, and steering in a bounded breadth-first search.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Diversity measures applied after generation cannot ensure that new candidates explore different structural regimes. PRS specifies the intended direction of change before producing executable code.

Core method

A parent consists of an idea and its implementation. An LLM first perturbs the idea by expanding its decision mechanisms, compressing redundant or specialized structure, or steering a small refinement. A separate rewrite step produces multiple executable realizations. The search expands a bounded breadth-first frontier, preserves its best candidate, and samples additional survivors by score. Completed trees replenish a small heuristic pool while retaining its elite. Sliding-window UCB chooses among the three directions from relative parent–offspring improvements. When global progress stalls, the pool resets around its best program and operator statistics are reheated to encourage renewed exploration.

Contributions

  • Makes simpler, richer, and locally refined heuristics explicit generation-level alternatives.
  • Evaluates generated components in construction, ant-colony optimization, and guided local search across routing, packing, knapsack, and scheduling tasks.

Strengths and limitations

Three-run experiments and operator ablations support the combined mechanism, including improved larger-instance performance. However, frontier width, depth, restart thresholds, and exploration schedules remain manually specified. Every proposed idea is implemented and evaluated, so expensive rewrite and testing costs remain even for weak ideas.

What to improve

Learn the controller settings, test under equal token and execution budgets, and assess whether cheap screening can reject poor ideas without suppressing useful simplifications.

Connections

EoH couples natural-language heuristic ideas with executable code and evolutionary operators. PRS retains an idea/code separation but replaces recombination-centered variation with explicit expansion, compression, and steering, organized by breadth-first search.

papers.title: RadonBench: A Benchmark of Classical and Learning-Guided Search Techniques for Problems in Combinatorial Geometry
papers.summary: Compares classical and learning-guided Radon-free lattice search using one verifier while separating valid smaller constructions from target-sized near misses.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Different construction spaces and stopping rules can make unsuccessful mathematical searches appear incomparable—or make a near miss sound like a discovery.

Core method

RadonBench seeks eleven-point configurations in integer three-space and twenty-one-point configurations in integer four-space. A shared evaluator checks convex position, enumerates lattice points, and uses feasibility tests to count integral Radon points. Success requires the exact target cardinality and zero such points.

The benchmark compares fixed-seed exhaustive extension, greedy point moves, PatternBoost, AlphaZero-style construction, and OpenEvolve-based program evolution. In the latter, an LLM edits four constructor functions; a protected wrapper supplies sixteen reference configurations and caps verifier calls and returned candidates. An island archive retains programs using fitness and behavioral features. Returned coordinates are independently replayed.

Contributions

The reporting contract distinguishes the largest verified Radon-free construction from the best target-sized violation count and documents each method's reachable domain.

Strengths and limitations

No audited run reaches either open target. PatternBoost and AlphaZero reach valid sizes ten and twenty; local search and program evolution reach target-sized configurations with one Radon point. These are near misses, not improved mathematical bounds. Domains and compute are unmatched, and exhaustive coverage applies only to declared fixed-seed boxes.

What to improve

Match verifier and token budgets, repeat program-evolution runs, and release independently checkable witnesses and audit traces.

Connections

The program-evolution track adapts AlphaEvolve to lattice constructors. The benchmark's contribution is shared verification and honest output semantics, not evidence that evolutionary search dominates the alternatives.

papers.title: Beyond LLM-GA: Secure Fluid Antenna Systems with ReEvo-Designed Memetic Algorithm
papers.summary: Applies ReEvo offline to crossover, mutation, and local-search operators for secrecy-aware fluid-antenna optimization, then deploys the frozen operators without LLM calls.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Secure antenna-port selection couples discrete placement with continuous beamforming. Evolving only a genetic crossover or mutation rule leaves other search stages manually constrained and can miss secrecy-specific local refinements.

Core method

A feasible chromosome selects a fixed number of antenna ports. For each operator class, ReEvo compares higher- and lower-fitness programs, reflects on the differences, and generates improved code. Fitness is the best secure sum-rate achieved by the inner search with secure WMMSE beamforming, rather than a stand-alone port surrogate.

Operators are evolved sequentially: crossover first, mutation with crossover fixed, then local search with both fixed. The final crossover uses elite-port statistics and geometry; mutation performs feasible swaps; local search proposes four complementary one-swap neighbors. Cardinality repair, invalid-program rejection, cached evaluations, and elitist replacement constrain deployment. No online LLM queries are required.

Contributions

The design extends LLM-generated operators to all three discrete stages under a common secrecy objective. Separate training, validation, and paired test channels evaluate the resulting optimizer, which improves reported secure sum-rate over conventional and single-operator LLM genetic algorithms.

Strengths and limitations

Offline code generation makes deployment costs explicit. Perfect channel information, including the eavesdropper channel, is assumed. Equal generation counts are not equal evaluator budgets because local search evaluates additional neighbors; the result should not be read as a matched-compute speedup.

What to improve

Compare equal beamformer-evaluation budgets, test imperfect or delayed channel information, and evaluate whether jointly evolving the three operators improves on sequential freezing.

Connections

ReEvo supplies the reflective code-evolution method directly. This application adapts its generated operators to secrecy-aware antenna selection and couples them to a continuous beamforming evaluator.

papers.title: RLDISCOVER: LLM-driven co-evolution of reinforcement learning algorithms
papers.summary: Moves from bandit-selected RL component edits to joint program evolution, using progressively longer multi-seed training to control evaluation cost and noise.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

RL algorithms contain interacting representation, target, loss, policy, and exploration mechanisms. Joint edits are difficult to credit, but isolated improvements may fail when combined; noisy long training makes either strategy expensive.

Core method

The seed is divided into five executable components. A UCB controller initially selects one component to mutate; unproductive arms freeze. Component champions are merged in gain order, retaining replacements only when validation does not worsen. Subsequent population searches may change multiple components, carrying mechanism-level lessons across rounds.

Candidates pass through 50K-step/one-seed, 200K-step/two-seed, and 1M-step/three-seed evaluations. A quota and the higher-fidelity leader's low-fidelity score govern promotion, with a slot for each round's best candidate. Five intermediate finalists receive full training. Syntax, component-presence, deduplication, and silent-fallback audits precede reporting.

Contributions

The same pipeline evolves SAC, PPO, and DQN across 26 task–algorithm pairs. The paper reports recurring robust losses, progress-dependent value targets, and running statistics, plus selected transfer experiments. Staged evaluation greatly reduces compute relative to fully training the same candidate pool.

Strengths and limitations

Repeated seeds and finalist audits improve credibility. PPO/DQN inherit SAC-oriented budgets and hyperparameters, so their returns are not directly comparable with tuned published implementations. Component credit operates only at short fidelity; slow-learning but strong asymptotic programs can be discarded early.

What to improve

Calibrate each algorithm family, promote candidates using learning-curve uncertainty, and return longer-horizon evidence to component-level search.

Connections

MuEvo keeps component participation reversible and evaluates collaboration contexts. RLDiscover instead first freezes local edits, then switches to unrestricted co-evolution, trading persistent component-level interaction modeling for a staged search and training budget.

papers.title: A Case Study of a Multi-Agent Kernel-Optimization Loop That Learns a New AI Accelerator
papers.summary: Builds and rechecks accelerator knowledge while a multi-agent design-tree search optimizes three kernels under scarce, noisy device access.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

An unfamiliar accelerator demands both implementation search and learning what its compiler, language, and measurements actually mean.

Core method

The loop constructs a checked DSL guide, runs microbenchmarks, records compiler legality rules, and revalidates knowledge after toolchain changes. Strategy, architecture, implementation, and ownership roles explore per-kernel design trees while retaining a best accepted implementation.

Cheap legality and cost checks screen candidates before scarce device runs. Late-stage acceptance uses repeated paired comparisons with the incumbent rather than a single timing. The 12-day campaign optimizes three Gemma decode kernels in the Furiosa RNGD Rust DSL.

Contributions

The final retained kernels achieve a reported 9.293× geometric-mean speedup over the competition baseline. The process documents knowledge repair, measurement calibration, and 44 test-input shortcut rows excluded from the reported outcome.

Strengths and limitations

This is one campaign, not a controlled attribution study: neither onboarding nor role division is ablated. Toolchain and grader changes complicate historical comparisons. The repeated acceptance test's observed false-positive rate exceeds its nominal 5%; public-board position is not an official ranking. Final kernels were tested on generated inputs, not real checkpoint weights.

What to improve

Repeat on isolated devices and new accelerators, preregister acceptance tests, vary inputs from the start, and compare against an otherwise identical loop without active onboarding.

Connections

AscendEvolve retrieves versioned external platform knowledge. This case instead foregrounds actively measuring and rebuilding target knowledge during a changing-toolchain campaign, revealing complementary feedback routes for data-poor accelerators.

papers.title: SEDIMA: Cross-Run Hierarchical Insight Memory for Evolutionary Search Agents
papers.summary: Distills evaluated mutation traces into hierarchically clustered insights and retrieves evidence-linked advice across runs without changing search operators.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Repeated searches can rediscover both useful edits and known failures. SEDIMA tests a small external memory interface that preserves transferable lessons while retaining the host's population and mutation machinery.

Core method

A write hook after evaluation records the parent/child scores, delta, event source, and raw report. An LLM distills each event into an insight linked to that trace, describing either the initial bottleneck or a change and its observed effect. Embedded insights join similarity-based clusters whose non-parametric attention-weighted centroids emphasize semantically prototypical members. Before mutation, a query about the current program retrieves relevant clusters and then insights, optionally including linked traces. A synthesizer converts the bounded evidence into three recommendations inserted into the host prompt. If nothing passes the relevance threshold, the original prompt is used. The store persists across runs; warm-start evaluation memory is populated from disjoint problems, and the same two hooks support OpenEvolve and ShinkaEvolve.

Contributions

  • Separates raw evidence, distilled lessons, and cluster-level retrieval in a persistent memory hierarchy.
  • Tests two search harnesses and five backbones using private benchmark evaluations.
  • Distinguishes cold online memory from same-benchmark and cross-benchmark warm starts.

Strengths and limitations

Main-table cells are single runs, although transfer and ablation analyses use three seeds. Matching 100 evaluated candidates excludes additional distillation, embeddings, and synthesis calls, so fewer iterations are not equivalent to lower total cost. Memory grows without consolidation or forgetting; erroneous insights can persist and propagate. The experiments do not directly compare alternative memory-based evolution systems.

What to improve

Measure amortized costs over repeated searches, benchmark against other persistent memories, and add evidence-sensitive correction, consolidation, and forgetting.

Connections

EvoMem consolidates promising mutation events after a run with exemplar provenance. SEDIMA writes after each evaluation and uses a three-level semantic hierarchy to retrieve synthesized advice across disjoint problems. Their difference is the timing and granularity of memory construction, not simply whether memory exists.

papers.title: Evolving Semantic Indexes for Generative Retrieval
papers.summary: Evolves semantic-index and collision-handling programs using a tiny retrieval model, and tests when its fitness rankings transfer to a much larger generator.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Semantic identifiers define which documents a generative retriever can reach. Their discrete construction cannot simply be optimized through downstream gradients, while retraining the target generator for every candidate is costly.

Core method

An AdaEvolve island population selects parent and inspiration programs. A locally served 31B LLM proposes code diffs inside mutable components. Candidates map fixed document/query embeddings and training relevance pairs to integer identifiers. Execution, collision-rate, and timeout gates trigger repair before costly fitness evaluation.

A roughly 1M-non-embedding-parameter GPT-2 decoder learns each candidate's identifiers; Recall@100 on held-out training pairs guides evolution. Selected programs are subsequently tested with a 1B generator. Experiments separately mutate identifiers, collision handling, generator objectives, and the whole pipeline to examine the validity of this proxy rather than assuming it.

Contributions

Joint identifier/collision evolution raises NQ320K target Recall@100 from 85.82% to 90.57%. A 21-program calibration finds rank correlation 0.90 between proxy and target for semantic-index changes. Three retrieval datasets test the resulting programs.

Strengths and limitations

The component study exposes a consequential failure: objective and full-pipeline searches improve proxy scores while degrading target recall. Search scopes differ in budgets and initialization, so their selected outcomes are not clean isolated causal comparisons. The calibration does not establish universal proxy reliability.

What to improve

Calibrate on more independently sampled candidates, introduce uncertainty-aware target evaluations, and compare coupled components under matched search budgets.

Connections

TGR-EvoDAG addresses another route through generative pipeline coupling: full stage-aware retraining and downstream adaptation. Here, restricting mutable components is crucial to preserving proxy-to-target transfer.

papers.title: SiteEvo: An LLM Agent for Autonomous Discovery of Site-Adaptive Massive MIMO Detectors
papers.summary: Discovers site-specific detector programs, trains their parameters, then reduces preparation and payload cost under a validation error-rate constraint.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Wireless sites differ in interference and channel structure. Parameter tuning within a prescribed detector may be insufficient, while a structurally better detector can still be too expensive to deploy.

Core method

The LLM receives a communication model, site diagnostics, previous candidates, and a contract separating reusable channel preparation from payload detection. It proposes complete PyTorch detectors and trainable parameterizations. Execution-only repair receives errors but no performance ranking, keeping debugging separate from algorithm selection.

A backend trains numerical parameters and returns validation bit-error rates. Promising structures receive progressively larger training budgets. A second search starts from the chosen detector and proposes traceable structural simplifications; it minimizes preparation cost plus coherence-block-weighted payload cost subject to preserving BER within tolerance. The selected code and parameters are frozen, with no online LLM calls.

Contributions

Three simulated deployment sites test structural specialization. Reported BER reductions at 6 dB are factors of 2.6–6.0 versus each site's strongest comparison, while refinement reduces block-level computational cost by 16.7–34.1%.

Strengths and limitations

The preparation/payload split matches reusable channel computation and exposes deployment trade-offs. Results assume perfect channel information and known noise variance in simulated sites. Operation-count reductions do not establish hardware latency or robustness to changing propagation conditions. The public author block does not disclose affiliations.

What to improve

Test channel-estimation errors, online distribution drift, measured device latency, and amortized discovery cost across site updates.

Connections

AITE retains a performance–complexity frontier of wireless algorithms. SiteEvo instead first fixes a site-specific BER anchor, then performs parent-constrained cost refinement, making the accuracy-versus-efficiency trade-off a sequential constrained search.

papers.title: Stateless Language Agents: Scaling Long-Horizon Automated Research
papers.summary: Reconstructs fresh role-specific agent contexts from harness-owned experiment records, coordinating explicit assignments over long research runs.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Longer agent conversations need not produce more experiments. SLA separates durable research evidence from transient reasoning so that context selection and work assignment remain controlled as inference budgets grow.

Core method

The harness stores candidate code, scores, local worker incumbents, and a chronological outcome record. Every Advisor epoch and every Worker trial starts a fresh session. The Advisor sees the global best plus a structured summary grouped by direction, separating measured non-improvements from inconclusive execution failures, and assigns concrete experiments. Each isolated Worker receives only its assignment, retained candidate, and compact local feedback. Workers cannot inspect other workspaces or the complete history. Local incumbents may remain below the global best, allowing alternative approaches to mature; a redirected worker restarts from the global best but establishes a new local baseline after its first valid evaluation. An independent evaluator records outcomes, and only harness-retained artifacts survive between invocations.

Contributions

  • Implements enforced statelessness and context isolation for both planning and execution roles.
  • Studies software, kernel, and algorithm tasks at cumulative budgets reaching one billion tokens.
  • Uses shared-checkpoint continuation ablations to test context reconstruction, isolation, and explicit assignments.

Strengths and limitations

Most task/configuration results are single runs; only one main kernel configuration and checkpoint ablations are replicated. Token matching does not equate total computation, and cost estimates exclude running experiments. The ablations keep all agents stateless, so they isolate context and assignment choices rather than statelessness itself. All tasks require executable evaluators.

What to improve

Replicate full-budget comparisons, include execution costs, and directly vary conversational persistence while holding evidence reconstruction fixed.

Connections

Discovery with Forgetting discards historical evidence during resets, retaining the incumbent and score. SLA retains the full external record but reconstructs bounded role-specific contexts. These are distinct answers to how search should escape unproductive historical commitments.

papers.title: SpecEvo: Speculative Evolution with Large Language Models for Cost-Efficient Scientific Discovery
papers.summary: SpecEvo combines continuous cheap-model program search with rolling evidence consolidation and sparse frontier-model interventions whose scope follows search stagnation.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Uniformly using a powerful model is costly, but cheap mutations can repeat failures or exhaust one strategy. The paper coordinates model roles using the evolving search trajectory.

Core method

Frontier-generated seeds are diversified by cheap models and stored in a bounded niche archive described by AST statistics and strategy-description embeddings. Cheap asynchronous Speculators mutate or cross over parents; stagnation flattens rank-based sampling to expose more archive regions. At checkpoints a frontier Navigator synthesizes complementary mechanisms, performs targeted repair, or reframes the strategy according to stagnation. Each valid intervention seeds cheap local variants. A cheap Advisor periodically consolidates successful, failed, and saturated attempts into a short guidance note. That note is injected probabilistically to avoid forcing all workers toward one interpretation. Every candidate still passes an executable evaluator.

Contributions

  • Coordinates generation, strategic intervention, and evidence consolidation at different costs and cadences.
  • Tests 176 tasks spanning mathematics, systems, combinatorial optimization, and equation discovery under complementary wall-clock, API-cost, and evaluation budgets.

Strengths and limitations

The reported savings concern API expenditure, not total compute. Four-worker parallelism affects wall-clock comparisons, and the evaluators are mostly lightweight CPU tasks. Archive descriptors depend partly on generated descriptions whose fidelity is not systematically tested; misleading descriptions can distort niches and strategic context.

What to improve

Include accelerator and evaluation costs, adapt intervention frequency to evaluator expense, and validate semantic descriptions against code or execution behavior.

Connections

RelayEvolve makes a one-time handoff from cheap exploration to strong refinement. SpecEvo keeps cheap exploration active and repeatedly coordinates frontier interventions and guidance using trajectory evidence.

papers.title: SplatLab: Autonomous Scientific Discovery for 3DGS Research
papers.summary: Combines verified 3DGS plugin scaffolds, island tournaments, falsification, and run-linked claims in an automated research workflow.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Generating a plausible extension is easier than reproducing its baseline and supporting every reported comparison with executable evidence.

Core method

SplatLab organizes 36 agent roles across research phases around a verified reproduction backbone. A seven-category 3DGS taxonomy and nine plugin hooks bound editable components. Literature and measured bottlenecks motivate proposals.

Eight islands apply mutation operators selected by a bandit. An Elo cascade moves from inexpensive idea screening to measured training performance; full evaluation is reserved for strong candidates. Verbal-gradient reflection revises proposals, while a standing falsifier tests stress conditions and penalizes failures. Commit hashes and run identifiers bind manuscript numbers to experiments, and unresolved claims block completion.

Contributions

The reported collection contains sixteen manuscripts with target-relative PSNR improvements of 0.18–3.78 dB. The workflow combines reproducible scaffolds, adversarial testing, and cross-repository checks rather than treating manuscript generation as validation.

Strengths and limitations

The results are domain-specific research campaigns, not a compute-matched comparison with human researchers. Seed coverage varies, reproduction engineering and GPU costs are substantial, and model-based manuscript judgments do not establish scientific novelty. A successful pipeline does not independently identify the contribution of every agent role.

What to improve

Release complete cost-normalized runs, replicate all selected results across seeds and scenes, and separate expert novelty assessment from model-written review.

Connections

The method adapts AlphaEvolve's editable program-block search to 3DGS plugin scaffolds and explicitly uses ReEvo-style verbal gradients to turn experimental evidence into candidate revisions.

papers.title: TGR-EvoDAG: A DAG-based Multi-Agent Code Evolution Framework for Generative Recommendation on Tencent
papers.summary: Evolves a complete generative-recommendation pipeline through a code DAG with cross-branch merging, stage-aware GPU budgeting, and deliberate downstream adaptation.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Changing a semantic tokenizer invalidates downstream training and can initially reduce recommendation quality. A search that counts edits equally or immediately discards regressions misses these delayed improvements.

Core method

Each DAG node records a code snapshot, its parents, hypothesis, affected training stages, measured cost, diagnostics, and distilled lessons. An operator selector chooses exploration, local mutation, or multi-parent merging according to expected gain and retraining cost. Architect–critic and coder–reviewer pairs develop and check the change; merges use diffs against the lowest common ancestor.

Training returns recommendation metrics, mathematical probes, simulated-user diagnostics, and GPU consumption. A distiller records mechanism-level lessons. The pruner can mark a regressed upstream branch as needing downstream adaptation, forcing a later child to repair compatibility rather than abandoning it. Final selection uses validation metrics, not simulated-user satisfaction.

Contributions

The method makes cross-stage dependencies part of search control. Under a 24-GPU-hour public-data budget, it improves Hit@10 from 0.0626 to 0.0869; the transferred architecture produces a reported 0.40% online CTR increase in a 14-day Tencent experiment.

Strengths and limitations

Diagnostic-matched baselines help separate richer feedback from search topology. Industrial testing adds deployment evidence, but simulated users are not human subjects, and the internal production environment limits independent reproduction. Generality beyond the evaluated recommendation pipeline remains unproven.

What to improve

Repeat full searches across datasets and seeds, expose reproducible cost accounting, and quantify when adaptation tags rescue genuinely useful upstream edits.

Connections

Semantic Index Evo restricts search to components with reliable small-model proxies; TGR-EvoDAG instead spends stage-aware training compute to adapt the whole pipeline. EvoSkillRec combines open-code exploration with promotion into typed reusable architecture skills, whereas this work merges whole recommendation-code branches and handles training-stage dependencies.

papers.title: TileCas: Cascading Kernel Development Across Programming Abstractions
papers.summary: Lets coding agents retain, diagnose, lower, and revisit kernel candidates across high-level DSL and low-level accelerator source representations.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A high-level language shrinks the search space but can hide controls needed for performance. Permanently lowering a program sacrifices that convenience even when the low-level branch disappoints.

Core method

TileCas is a pluggable interface around existing kernel agents. Cross-Level Diagnosis maps compiler correspondence and measured evidence to actionable controls at different representations, retaining source versions and measurement conditions.

Abstraction Scheduling chooses both a candidate and representation for refinement. A heterogeneous search tree records same-level edits, lowering, and rollback, so an agent can restore an earlier high-level version or reuse selected low-level components. Experiments pair TileLang with HIP or Ascend C while keeping the base agents' generation and evaluation mechanisms.

Contributions

Across fifty KernelBench Level-3 workloads, two accelerators, two models, and five seeds, AKO with TileCas achieves 4.84× arithmetic-mean speedup versus 3.75× for the strongest evaluated non-TileCas baseline. A KDA integration also improves, supporting interface reuse.

Strengths and limitations

The time budget includes conversion and exploration costs, and unsuccessful candidates contribute zero to the speed metric. Nevertheless, tests use finite inputs and numerical tolerances, only two representation levels are studied, and compiler changes may invalidate correspondence. Selected switching interventions do not establish optimal scheduling at every decision.

What to improve

Test deeper abstraction hierarchies, quantify porting effort, and compare uncertainty-aware scheduling with fixed switching policies.

Connections

ADSL-PDE constrains search to a typed solver language with a fixed compilation path. TileCas makes the abstraction level itself editable and revisitable, trading a smaller guaranteed structure for greater low-level control.

papers.title: LLM Evolutionary Search Strategies Should be Compared by Tokens
papers.summary: Replays evolutionary-search trajectories against cumulative token budgets and audits scorer exploits before comparing them with independent sampling.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A proposal can include long archives, retries, and controller calls. Equal proposal counts need not grant competing search procedures equal resources.

Core method

The analysis reuses 600 logged runs: forty seeds for each of three strategies on five systems and mathematical tasks. Every model call contributes prompt, completion, and reasoning tokens to a best-so-far trajectory. Exact order statistics compare seed-width/depth allocations with an independently sampled program pool at matched token budgets, without extrapolating beyond available samples.

The audit re-executes potentially leading programs and checks transaction coverage, delivered partitions, and simulator inputs. Both evolution and sampling must obey the same task-validity rules.

Contributions

The paper measures the cost hidden by proposal counts and shows how selection amplifies evaluator exploits. A purported fivefold scheduling improvement collapses after incomplete schedules are rejected.

Strengths and limitations

After token matching and audit, evolution's advantage is at most 5% in twelve of fifteen task–method pairs; larger gains remain on Heilbronn search. This does not establish universal parity: the finite sampling pool restricts the comparison window, evolutionary curves still improve there, and token counts are not identical to hardware compute or money across models.

What to improve

Report token, wall-clock, and evaluator costs together, log coverage during search, and select allocation policies on independent tasks.

Connections

Evolution or Illusion? studies width/depth allocation using proposal budgets. This paper reuses that trajectory-analysis setting but changes the accounting unit and audits candidate validity.

papers.title: TRACE: Tackling Real-World Resource Assignment Problems via Agentic Heuristic Design
papers.summary: Extends heuristic evolution with agents that turn execution logs into compact system insights and callable surrogate tools for resource-assignment policies.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Processing affinity, queue behavior, and energy costs are often absent from the problem specification. Execution logs contain this information, but are too large and schema-specific to insert wholesale into mutation prompts.

Core method

An EoH-style population loop evaluates assignment programs and accumulates their logs. At epoch boundaries, a reasoner sees the objective and log schema or excerpt, then proposes a distinct diagnostic hypothesis. A coder writes and runs schema-specific extraction code on the complete log buffer.

Workflow runs alternate textual insights and low-parameter surrogate models with callable prediction interfaces. A merge step rewrites concise system information, including tool signatures, for later heuristic-generation prompts. New heuristics may call these tools and are selected by end-to-end assignment cost. After a bounded number of successful extraction runs, knowledge freezes while evolution continues; the costly reasoner is invoked much less often than the lightweight generation model.

Contributions

Synthetic cloud workloads and a measurement-driven 5G vRAN simulation test policies balancing latency, drops, and energy. The extraction workflow adds under 2% wall-clock overhead relative to the compared EoH generation budget and produces auditable system-aware rules.

Strengths and limitations

Generated parsers adapt to different schemas and process logs without context-window limits. Missing fields, bad hypotheses, or invalid parsing code can remove the benefit; an executable diagnostic is not automatically a true causal explanation. The vRAN result uses measured components and traffic traces inside simulation, not a live deployment experiment.

What to improve

Validate extracted models on fresh traces, quantify misleading-knowledge failures, and measure adaptation cost after hardware and traffic shifts.

Connections

EoH supplies the evolutionary backbone. TRACE extends its proposal context with execution-derived system knowledge and tools, making unknown dynamics inspectable rather than leaving them implicit in a scalar score.

papers.title: TRIZᵃ: Guiding Agent Evolution from Pattern Recognition to Solution Invention
papers.summary: Declares contradiction-guided typed mutations before evaluation and separates functional-information diagnostics from frozen promotion gates.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A better detector score need not justify replacing an incumbent when other benefits, harms, or validation requirements deteriorate.

Core method

TRIZa maps inventive principles to typed code or configuration transformations. Before evaluation, each proposal declares its contradiction, operator, allowed changes, and frozen protocol. The LLM instantiates the edit; a provenance record links it to the resulting evidence.

Useful and harmful functional information are measured separately against fixed reference populations. Integrity, safety, reproducibility, and resource gates determine eligibility before certification level and replication status are compared. FI-based Ideality is diagnostic or tie-breaking evidence, not permission to override a failed gate.

Contributions

Paired legacy reruns report F1 gains on three cybersecurity datasets. More importantly, a completed 45-activity CICIoT2023 campaign improves macro-F1 from 0.8325 to 0.8483 but is not promoted: both the relative-gain and false-positive-reduction thresholds fail. Later deteriorating candidates are also retained as negative evidence.

Strengths and limitations

Frozen protocols and separate decision levels make score improvements auditable. They do not establish that TRIZ or FI caused the gains: matched-budget component ablations are absent. The 2,040 controller decisions form a nested descriptive aggregate, not independent replications. Raw trace artifacts are promised for later release, so current reproducibility is manuscript-level.

What to improve

Release complete records, validate reference-population sensitivity, and compare typed versus unguided edits with identical budgets and promotion rules.

Connections

AlphaEvolve evaluates generated variants through task scores. TRIZa takes a concrete alternative route by constraining mutation types before execution and separating useful metric change from evidence-qualified promotion.

papers.title: Can Test-Time Memory Evolution Outperform Test-Time Training for Scientific Discovery?
papers.summary: TTME replaces online weight updates with evolving operational guidelines and reusable algorithmic strategies while retaining the discovery framework's archive, parent selection, and verifier.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Test-time training can internalize search experience but incurs repeated optimization cost. The paper asks whether the same search framework can learn sufficiently through external memory instead.

Core method

Every fixed update interval, evaluated attempts feed two memories. Guideline Memory distills valid outcomes and failures into implementation rules, merging recurrent entries and pruning stale or low-priority ones. Strategy Memory compares successful parent–child code changes, extracts the underlying algorithmic ideas, and consolidates them into source-backed strategy families. For each selected parent, a selector chooses relevant strategies while discouraging redundant assignments across parents; an adaptor turns them into parent-specific modification instructions. Half the candidate budget uses these instructions and half generates directly, both with operational guidelines. Evaluation updates the original archive and the memories, without changing model parameters.

Contributions

  • Provides a modular replacement for the adaptation component in TTT-Discover and ThetaEvolve, leaving their search rules intact.
  • Tests three models on five mathematical construction tasks, including autocorrelation inequalities, minimum overlap, and maximal determinant.

Strengths and limitations

The reported scores beat the corresponding published TTT results in the evaluated settings. Efficiency measurements include memory calls but exclude task evaluation time, and TTT comparison scores come from the original papers rather than all being rerun. Evidence is confined to a small set of mathematical tasks, not a universal dominance result over weight adaptation.

What to improve

Run repeated, fully matched end-to-end cost comparisons, expand to expensive scientific evaluations, and examine hybrid memory-plus-training adaptation.

Connections

EvoMem also preserves lessons from successful program changes. TTME separates failure-derived implementation rules from reusable strategy families and tests memory as a substitute for parametric adaptation under fixed archive rules.

papers.title: Large Language Model-Guided Discovery of Weight-Five Bivariate Bicycle Codes
papers.summary: Evolves polynomial-tuple generator programs for weight-five quantum codes and audits their outputs for exact distance, equivalence, and connected components.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

Promising estimated code parameters may hide weak distance bounds, repeated presentations, or disconnected copies of smaller codes.

Core method

Four 300-iteration OpenEvolve campaigns evolve Python functions generating polynomial tuples for bivariate bicycle and perturbed bicycle codes. Exact rank and family constraints screen outputs before staged decoder-based distance estimates guide fitness.

Post-search analysis adds exhaustive low-weight exclusion, logical witnesses, and exact MILP certificates where available. Canonical graph signatures merge presentations, while a basis-independent connectivity analysis reduces repeated components before frontier comparisons. The evolved artifacts are generator programs; quantum codes are their outputs.

Contributions

The catalogue contains 1,142 retained proposals, including 1,081 attributed to generated programs. Exact connected CSS realizations include [[96,4,10]], [[140,6,10]], and [[180,4,14]]. Archive comparisons distinguish equivalence, shared parameters, and newly supplied distance evidence rather than calling every point novel.

Strengths and limitations

Among logged positive-distance CSS proposals, 87.18% certify distance at least five, versus 72.50–74.26% in stratified random controls. Controls cover more connected classes. Missing failed campaign calls and repeated observations prevent equal-attempt or equal-compute yield claims. Presentation equivalence is narrower than full code equivalence; physical decoding performance is untested.

What to improve

Log all attempts, search connected components directly, and compare exact certification and circuit-level costs under matched budgets.

Connections

Both this study and FunSearch evaluate programs that construct mathematical objects. The feedback differs: weight-five code search uses staged distance estimates followed by selective exact certification, so a search score is not itself the final certificate. The later EAQECC Families study instead emphasizes researcher-led infinite-family generalization and a separate formal algebraic certificate.

papers.title: WorldSolver: Can LLM Agents Simulate the Physical Dynamics via Solver Generation?
papers.summary: Evaluates generated physical-dynamics solvers within fixed scenes using execution checks, rendered visual fidelity, and numerical physical-law residuals.
papers.body_html:
Why it matters

A simulator can render a plausible animation while violating physics, or satisfy selected invariants without reproducing the intended phenomenon.

Core method

The benchmark derives 168 tasks from 61 graphics papers across seven physical domains. A fixed scaffold supplies geometry, physical parameters, boundary conditions, rendering, and execution interfaces; agents modify only the solver that advances state.

Submitted trajectories are checked for successful execution, scored by a vision-language judge on event order, interaction, signature behavior, and temporal coherence, and tested against hidden task-specific physical rules. Numerical residuals include conservation and contact constraints. Failed execution scores zero; otherwise visual and physical scores are averaged. Agents have thirty minutes to generate a solver and solvers have ten minutes to run.

Contributions

Controlled scenes isolate solver implementation from asset or renderer changes, while complementary visual and continuous-state checks expose different failure modes.

Strengths and limitations

Across seven evaluated agents, the best aggregate score is 48.7/100, leaving substantial headroom. This is a composite score, not a solver correctness rate. The visual judge sees sampled frames, physical checks cover only selected laws, and different agent scaffolds complicate attribution to model capability alone.

What to improve

Increase expert auditing, add perturbation and long-horizon stability tests, and report uncertainty and separate physical-rule failures.

Connections

ADSL-PDE restricts solver designs through a typed description and compiler. WorldSolver evaluates comparatively unrestricted solver code inside a protected environment: they expose complementary representation-level and execution-level approaches to validity.
